definition.name: gripforge_game_project
definition.title: List, create, read, bind, feed, set the controls of or delete Game Kit projects
definition.description:
Journey — create, then bind a model to every creature slot (get carries the creatures report) and set the controls: action=controls applies the control scheme of the gameplay, a proposal to adapt. Before telling the user the game is done: gripforge_game_audit. Manage Game Kit projects (gkp_…): the container holding installed kits, their lockfile, asset bindings and data collections. action=list lists the workspace projects; create needs name and takes a preset (see gripforge_gamekit_search; adventure is the reference game of game.engine) or an explicit kits map — every new project gets game.engine first (the engine of the game: scenes, archetypes, scripts, life cycle; its answer carries the engine start pack { structure, scene, blocks, order, next, rules } and added, the kits installed for dependencies), then the default kits ui.menu (title / pause / options / load and save screen), input.remap (key remapping), settings.graphics (graphics options), ui.prompts (on-screen key prompts that follow remapping and the gamepad), ui.endscreen (end screen and credits), save.persistence (save slots, quick save, autosave), audio.core (game audio: mixer, music, effects, event → sound table), i18n.text (game texts in the player’s language: translation tables in the translations collection, ICU plurals) ui.theme (the design of every interface as kit config: colours, font, shapes, key glyphs; unset = built-in look) and input.virtualpad (the on-screen gamepad of touch screens, mode auto: shown on a touch screen without a gamepad, Touch controls tab) and display.fullscreen (the game in fullscreen: F11, the Options entry, start in fullscreen with atStart, the player’s choice saved), asset.preload (the files of the game loaded in phases — first playable frame, background, next scene ahead — each file once, checked; progress as state and events shown by ui.menu, ui.endscreen and hud.action) and asset.cache (the files kept on the device between visits: IndexedDB, then Cache Storage with a service worker, then the HTTP cache; quota and eviction) and, on web, ai.navigation (the paths of the game over its real collision geometry: route and steer for NPCs, enemies and click-to-move), addedBy default: keep and configure them (never recode a pathfinding: ask ai.navigation and adapt its config, the hook navigation.plan and the event navigation.blocked; never recode an asset loader, a download queue or a cache: adapt their rules, asset_preload documents, scenes ahead and cache quota instead), leave one out ({ "ui.menu": false }) or remove it only if the user asks. They hold for EVERY game, a compiled module with its own page or a custom page included: that page mounts the menu, Options › Controls and Video, fullscreen and the prompts from the bindings through the kits’ web views (gripforge-ui.mjs, GET /api/v1/hud) or their adapter, never its own copy; get returns the full ProjectDetail (installed kits, bindings, capabilities, missing, playUrl); bind maps asset slots to Library items (lib_…, null to clear); data reads a collection or upserts / removes documents validated against the kits’ schemas (replace=true swaps the whole collection); collection asset_passports = the game’s own passport of a Library model, over the global GripForge one (what it leaves out is inherited): { id: <slot>, item: lib_…, passport: { kits: { lod: { ratios, minTriangles, fit, maxError… } } } } changes the mesh levels of that model for this game only (its own game copy; ratios: [] = no level; characters keep their bone weights); controls reads or sets the controls: without scheme it returns the control schemes of the catalogue (fps, third_person, moba_click, top_down, platformer, fighting, vehicle, rts, point_click: movement by keys or by click, what the mouse is for, expected actions and keys, touch layout), the project scheme, the one its kits suggest, every action with its effective key and the keys two actions share in one mode (warnings with a proposed reassignment, never a refusal — also in get → report.controls); with scheme and dry_run=true it returns the diff of keys the scheme would write; with scheme alone it applies it (input.actions overrides marked source: scheme, the touch layout of input.virtualpad, the actions of the ui.prompts help bar — the bar itself stays off: no key on screen outside a tutorial). Choose the scheme from the kind of game, never from a kit default: 
Kits offer capabilities that can be switched off and tuned; the game makes one high-level gameplay choice and enables only the coherent set that choice needs: what is not chosen is off and invisible, and no kit default is imposed on the game. The generic modules propose choices, the request picks one: name the kind of game, take its control scheme from the table below (usually the only one allowed), and embed only what that scheme uses on each device — its input sources, its on-screen controls on a touch screen, its settings (remapping, sensitivity, inversion, capture, dead zone only where the scheme uses them). Every option is a choice of the request too: the network input frame is embedded only for a multiplayer game, each other option only when asked. Write the choice into the project: gripforge_game_project create with controls=<scheme>, or action=controls scheme=<scheme> on an existing game (dry_run first, reset=true to drop old key overrides). A dungeon crawler is played with the mouse, not on W A S D. In play, input.scheme (a default kit) implements that choice: it follows the device in hand (keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch) with the variant of the scheme for it, takes the vehicle scheme while the player drives, gives the input to the interface while a menu, a dialogue or a text field is open, and the Options show per device only the controls the scheme uses; tune it within the choice (input.scheme allowed: the closed list the player may switch between, usually one; variants; composites for held / double / charged / chorded / combo actions), never by enabling every option.
Gameplay choices (kind → control scheme, per device):
- MOBA → `moba_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: tap_world, settings: touch_layout). A hero is ordered with the mouse (right click to move / attack, abilities toward the cursor); a gamepad moves it with the stick. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style bold, on: highlight, cursor, confirm, fail, sound, orderMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Real-time strategy → `rts` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: click to move, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: tap to move, on screen: stick + buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). Units are selected and ordered with the cursor; nothing is moved with W A S D. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, cursor, confirm, fail, sound, moveMarker, orderMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Dungeon crawler / action RPG seen from above → `arpg_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). Played with the mouse: click to walk, click an enemy to attack, right click for the special; the left stick on a gamepad, a tap on a touch screen. W A S D is not the default for this genre. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, cursor, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound, orderMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Top-down shooter / twin-stick roguelike → `top_down` (mouse+keys: WASD, right click = aim, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Constant dodging needs direct movement (W A S D / left stick) with the cursor or right stick to aim. The game may also allow: arpg_click. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Point-and-click adventure → `point_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). A free cursor: click where to go and what to use. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, cursor, confirm, fail, sound, moveMarker; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- First-person shooter / survival → `fps` (mouse+keys: WASD, captured mouse, right click = aim, settings: remap, mouse_sensitivity, invert_y, pointer_capture; gamepad: stick, right stick looks, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, stick_sensitivity, invert_y, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, right stick looks, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout, stick_sensitivity, invert_y). W A S D and the captured mouse to look (right stick on a gamepad). Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: highlight, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Third-person action / open world → `third_person` (mouse+keys: WASD, captured mouse, right click = aim, settings: remap, mouse_sensitivity, invert_y, pointer_capture; gamepad: stick, right stick looks, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, stick_sensitivity, invert_y, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, right stick looks, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout, stick_sensitivity, invert_y). W A S D relative to the camera and the captured mouse (right stick) to turn it. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Platformer → `platformer` (mouse+keys: WASD, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: virtual stick, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Direct movement and jump, no pointer. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: worldPrompt, confirm, fail, sound.
- Fighting → `fighting` (mouse+keys: WASD, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: virtual stick, on screen: buttons, settings: touch_layout). One key per blow, no pointer. No interaction.feedback.
- Racing / vehicles → `vehicle` (mouse+keys: vehicle, settings: remap; gamepad: vehicle, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: vehicle, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Throttle, brake and steering; no pointer. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: worldPrompt, confirm, fail.
- Turn-based combat / tactics → `point_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). Each turn is played with the cursor or a tap (combat.turns, tactics.grid): pick a unit or an action, then its cell or its target; no direct movement. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, cursor, confirm, fail, sound; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Card game / deckbuilder / pack opening → `point_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). Cards and packs are played with the cursor or a tap (cards.deck on combat.turns; collection.packs for a pack-opening or gacha game with an album): pick a card or a pack, then its target or the next object to turn over; no direct movement. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, cursor, confirm, fail, sound; interaction.system pointerTarget: true.
- Puzzle → `third_person` (mouse+keys: WASD, captured mouse, right click = aim, settings: remap, mouse_sensitivity, invert_y, pointer_capture; gamepad: stick, right stick looks, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, stick_sensitivity, invert_y, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, right stick looks, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout, stick_sensitivity, invert_y). The puzzle kits (puzzle.circuits, puzzle.beams) sit in the world: the player reaches them with the game's character, seen from behind by default, in first person or with the cursor when the game is built that way. The game may also allow: fps, point_click. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style default, on: highlight, nearbyHint, worldPrompt, holdGauge, confirm, fail, sound.
- Sports / ball game → `third_person` (mouse+keys: WASD, captured mouse, right click = aim, settings: remap, mouse_sensitivity, invert_y, pointer_capture; gamepad: stick, right stick looks, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, stick_sensitivity, invert_y, aim_assist; touch: virtual stick, right stick looks, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout, stick_sensitivity, invert_y). sport.ball on foot: the athlete moves with W A S D or the left stick and kicks where it faces; in its car mode, the vehicle controls. The game may also allow: vehicle. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: worldPrompt, confirm, fail, sound.
- Golf / mini-golf → `point_click` (mouse+keys: click to move, right click = context, settings: remap; gamepad: stick, aim assist, settings: remap, deadzone, aim_assist; touch: tap to move, on screen: buttons + tap_world, settings: touch_layout). sport.golf: the shot is aimed with the free cursor (the ball goes where the pointer is) and played with a click or a tap that stops the power gauge; nobody walks, so no W A S D and no captured pointer; the left stick turns the aim on a gamepad. No interaction.feedback.
- Flight / space combat → `vehicle` (mouse+keys: vehicle, settings: remap; gamepad: vehicle, settings: remap, deadzone; touch: vehicle, on screen: stick + buttons, settings: touch_layout). Throttle, yaw and pitch on the keys or the sticks, no pointer: vehicle.spaceship pilots a starfighter (the space_combat preset) and the same vehicle controls drive a plane. Interaction feedback: interaction.feedback style subtle, on: worldPrompt, confirm, fail.
Per device: the cursor per kind of target only with a mouse; on a gamepad the prompt shows the button of the active gamepad, on a touch screen the text alone (ui.prompts / input.actions promptFor); the designated target comes from input.scheme target() (cursor, aim axis, stick).
Interactions must be visible. Install interaction.feedback for any game with interactive objects (not for a pure fighting game) and set its elements from the gameplay table row; never draw an interaction prompt in a kit or a script: kits that offer an interaction pass their kind to interaction.use.register(entity, label, action, kind) (or interactable.kind on an archetype), and slow uses get a hold (interactable.hold / interaction.system.holdSeconds) instead of a custom timer. Styles and kinds are data (feedback_styles, interaction_kinds): restyle with them, do not recode. Leave the player settings (interaction.feedback.settings) to the menu.
A scheme is a starting proposal: a preset applies its own at creation (create takes controls to pick another one — pass the scheme of the kind of game the user asked for — or none), and any key stays changeable with gripforge_gamekit_configure input.actions { overrides: [{ action, keys, buttons?, disabled? }] } — the action of any kit; those entries always win over the scheme. logic chooses where the kits’ logic runs: wasm = logic of the kits in Rust compiled to wasm (Bevy player), the only logic; default wasm (create takes logic too; action=logic without logic reads it, with logic sets it). A game installing a kit without a Rust module cannot start: logic reports runs: none and fallback: the kits. delete needs confirm=true. Call this first to create or pick the project, then gripforge_gamekit_installed (existing project) or gripforge_gamekit_install. 0 credits.

action.description: list | create | get | bind | data | controls | logic | delete.

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Required for get, bind, data, controls, logic and delete.

name.description: create: project name.

preset.description: create: preset id whose default kits are installed (gripforge_gamekit_search returns presets).

kits.description: create: explicit kit toggles { "vehicle.driveable": true, … } on top of the preset. Unchecking a required kit fails with toggle_requires. The default kits (ui.menu, input.remap, settings.graphics, ui.prompts, ui.endscreen, save.persistence, audio.core, i18n.text, ui.theme, input.virtualpad, display.fullscreen, asset.preload, asset.cache, ai.navigation on web) are included unless set to false here — only when the user asked for it.

target.description: create: pass the confirmed engine explicitly (Three.js=web). Ask the user to choose Unity / Godot / Unreal Engine / Three.js before creating if unknown. API default web is for compatibility, not an engine choice.

bindings.description: bind: { slot: lib_… | null } — Library item per asset slot declared by the installed kits, null clears. A model bound to a creature slot gets its animations by itself as far as that is free (the answer carries the chain in creatures); see gripforge_gamekit_creatures.

collection.description: data: collection name declared by an installed kit (e.g. missions, npcs, zones).

documents.description: data: documents to upsert (each with its id), validated against the kit schema.

replace.description: data: true to replace the whole collection with documents.

scheme.description: controls: the control scheme to show (dry_run) or apply — fps, third_person, moba_click, arpg_click, top_down, platformer, fighting, vehicle, rts, point_click: the one of the kind of game (gameplay choices above; a dungeon crawler → arpg_click, a MOBA → moba_click, an RTS → rts). Omit to read the schemes and the project controls.

dry_run.description: controls: true returns the diff of keys without writing.

force.description: controls: also replace a touch layout or a help bar the game edited (kept by default).

reset.description: controls: also drop the key overrides the game wrote itself (kept by default), so the game ends exactly on the scheme — what a game made before the schemes needs to move to one. Preview with dry_run.

controls.description: create: the control scheme of the kind of game the user asked for (gameplay choices above: one scheme, usually the only one allowed), applied at creation instead of the preset’s own or of the one the kits suggest; none keeps the kits’ own keys.

logic.description: create, logic: wasm = logic of the kits in Rust compiled to wasm (Bevy player), the only logic; default wasm. logic without it reads the current choice.

confirm.description: delete: must be true. The project, its revisions and data are removed.

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.

definition.name: gripforge_game_scenes
definition.title: Scenes and levels of a game: list, create, order, link, assets, load plan
definition.description: The scenes and levels of a Game Kit project (gkp_…), game.engine 1.7 — use this tool, never code a scene manager. A scene has a kind: interface (no world: title, main menu, credits — kits build nothing, the renderers draw no world), 2d, 3d (default), loading (shown while the next scene loads), cinematic; a role: menu (entered first, Play leads on), level (levels follow the order), credits, other; next (the scene that follows: Play from the menu, the end of a level, the script verb next_scene); loading (how it shows when its files are not ready — on demand: preloaded or cached files go straight in, a screen comes up only after sceneFlow.showAfterMs; overlay = ui.menu's loading screen with the real asset.preload progress, none, background = the scene left stays until this one is ready, or a scene id: a loading scene or an interface scene of the game); loadingScreen { image, tips, background, title } (several screens per game: one per scene, or flow.loadingScreen); background { image, video, color, scene } of an interface scene; unload (release | keep); transition (replace: the scene left is unloaded | add: it stays loaded under this one) and below (what the scenes under an added scene do: run, pause = drawn but frozen, hide = not drawn). Scenes stack and keep their states at run time — the game changes scene by program (engine.scenes.enter(scene, entry, { unload: false, previous: { visible, paused } }), push / pop / unload / activate / set(scene, { visible, paused }); script verbs load_scene { unload: false }, push_scene, pop_scene, set_scene): a scene kept loaded is frozen in memory and resumed at once; nothing a loaded scene uses is freed. The flow (game.engine config sceneFlow): transition replace | add, menu scene | overlay (scene: the title of ui.menu is a scene of its own, entered first with no world behind it — synthesised as menu when the project writes none; every new game and every opened game has it), menuScene, loading overlay | scene | none | background, loadingScene, showAfterMs, minLoadingMs, loadTimeout (s), onFail retry | enter | wait, retries, loadingScreen, unload. Each scene loads its files before it is entered (asset.preload, progress on the loading screen) and leaving it frees its instances and the memory of the files only it used (never the disk cache); hooks engine.scene.change (redirect or refuse a change) and engine.scene.release, events engine.scene.loading / loaded / unloaded / refused for mods. The asset list of a scene (scene_assets: files with role, phase, size, shared) is generated from its content (instances → archetype models, the global slots a played scene needs, world, HUD, music, menu art) — retouch it by hand or with assets_put; asset.preload uses it as one more source, never a restriction. action=list (default; scene: one scene with its files and plan): the flow (menu, start, levels, loading), each scene (kind, role, next, instances, world kit, files, written or generated list), the scene issues of the report, the check of the asset lists and the load plan (per scene in play order: what entering it loads, what leaving it frees, what is shared, and the loading screen of that transition). action=create { id, kind?, role?, title?, next?, loading?, background?, world?, at? (index) } | update { id, set: {…} } (null clears a key) | remove { id } | order { ids } (these first, in this order) | link { id, next } (next null: unlink) | flow { set: { menu, menuScene, transition, loading, loadingScene, showAfterMs, minLoadingMs, loadTimeout, onFail, retries, loadingScreen, unload } } | menu { id?, title?, background? } (writes the menu scene as a document, first, role menu) | assets { scene? } (generate or refresh the lists; files written by hand are kept) | assets_put { scene, files } | assets_check (missing file, file used by nothing, duplicate, list out of date). dry_run answers the new state without writing. definition.name: gripforge_game_test
definition.title: Playtest a Game Kit project
definition.description: Journey — after each change: it also checks what the game chose (its scheme's gestures, fullscreen, right button, pointer capture, texts against the bindings). A playtest that passes is not a finished game: gripforge_game_audit (playtest="run" runs this test) gives the verdict and everything the tester cannot see. Play the project headless and report what works and what is broken. Run it after building or changing a game, before telling the user it is done. An automatic player spawns, walks, follows the mission waypoints, uses what offers a prompt, picks things up and attacks enemies. Probes check each capability the game provides (character control, combat, XP and levels, inventory, interactions, missions, needs, gathering, crafting, building, machines, world counters). Detectors flag a stuck player, unreachable goals, kit exceptions, NaN positions, a player under the ground, enemies that never reach the player, and step time. Then it checks the game on what it CHOSE, on a fresh run (lines game.*): the gestures its control scheme promises (a click game: click to walk, held to follow the cursor, click an enemy to strike, held to keep striking), fullscreen when the game offers it, the right button when the game gives it a role (no browser menu), the pointer captured exactly when the scheme looks with the mouse, and its texts (title, help, tutorial, dialogue) against the real bindings — never a fixed W A S D in a click game; nothing is imposed on a game that did not choose it. The frame rate is · not verified here: only a real page measures it (the play page reports it to the audit). Returns { summary, text, report, next }: text has one line per result, ✓ pass, ⚠ warning, ✕ failure, · not checked, each with its time, position, entity or kit; "provoked" means the tester set the condition up through the kit service. Fix the ✕ lines first, then run it again. report.notCovered lists the capabilities no probe looks at. report.replay replays the same inputs; pass it back as replay to check a fix against the same run. Deterministic: same project, seed and budget, same report. Runs in the compute service, about 5–20 s. 0 credits.

definition.title: Animation layers: what an action keeps or blends of the body, and of the movement
definition.description: The animation layers of the characters of a Game Kit project (gkp_…), part of the generic animation layer of the kits (packages/gamekits/src/runtime/anim-layers.ts, mixed in Rust by the players: Bevy on the web and natively, libgfkits for Godot / Unity / Unreal). definition.name: gripforge_gamekit_configure
definition.title: Configure an installed Game Kit
definition.description: Journey — while composing, and to fix what gripforge_game_audit reports (its defects carry the exact config to write). Tune an installed kit: merge config values validated against the kit configSchema (read it with gripforge_gamekit_get), or patch the config as a document (patch: set a nested key, add / change / remove one element of a list without rewriting it), or toggle enabled to switch the kit off without uninstalling it. Configure installed kits freely rather than recoding what they do (game.engine: startScene, startEntry, flow.title, story flags). The interface look of a game is ui.theme: set preset (scifi-lowpoly, military, fantasy-medieval, cyberpunk-neon, cartoon-bright, horror-dark, minimal-clean, retro-pixel) for a complete look, and only the colours, typography, shapes or glyphs that must differ (they win over the preset); gripforge_game_theme_from_concept fills it from the art direction. No key on screen in game outside a tutorial: never write a legend of the controls into a HUD text (hud.action hint, captions, labels) and leave ui.prompts bar off (its default); a tutorial step pushes its prompt with ui.prompts show(), and ui.prompts context: true / interaction.feedback worldPrompt: true are set only when the gameplay needs contextual prompts (the key is then the live binding, never written) — the controls live in Options › Controls (input.remap). Switching game.engine off follows the confirmation of a removal: the first call answers 409 confirm_required with details.confirm; send it back with enabled=false after the user agreed — never on your own. Returns { kit, project } with the new project revision. Call this AFTER gripforge_gamekit_install. 0 credits.

definition.description: Journey — right after creating or binding: no unit stays a capsule, every model gets its movement and action clips. gripforge_game_audit folds this report with the rest and applies the free steps with fix=true. YOU judge: read the reasons, pick the model that fits the game (any monster beats a capsule), bind it with gripforge_game_project { action: "bind" }; nothing is final, rebind any time. A slot with no proposal at all carries defect creature_no_model: generate a model (paid — quote and ask first), never leave the capsule. action=animate: run the free steps of the chain now for the bound models (a free Community model is copied into the workspace and bound in place of the original; the standard clip pack is retargeted, 0 credits; wait=true waits for the result, else it runs in the background — read report again). action=fill: bind the best free proposal to every unbound creature slot, then animate (what the hosted creation does). Nothing here spends credits: the automatic rig, a priced Community asset and generated motions always come back as proposed steps for you to quote and ask about. definition.description: Journey — last. Run gripforge_game_audit then gripforge_validate_release first: deliver a game whose verdict is complete and whose release is ready, or tell the user what is left. Turn catalogue kits, or the enabled kits of a Game Kit project, into engine files: Godot gets GDScript, scenes and config under gripforge/kits/<kit>/, Unity gets an embedded UPM package plus C# files and Unreal a Blueprint-first plugin for every kit with an engine delivery (gameplay and net.* kits; recipes otherwise), web needs nothing. definition.name: gripforge_gamekit_install
definition.title: Install a Game Kit into a project
definition.description: Journey — while composing. A kit installed and left empty is not done (audio.core without a sound, ui.endscreen without an end condition): gripforge_game_audit names them. Add a gameplay kit (a brick) to a Game Kit project (gkp_…); installing marks that the game uses it. Decide it yourself, no confirmation needed. Always the latest version; dependencies are added automatically and listed in added [{ kit, version, requiredBy, capability }] (e.g. game.engine for a kit that requires it). A kit that looks with the mouse (first person, third person, shooters, vehicles, mounts) also brings its companion input.pointer_lock (mouse capture) the first time it is added — listed in added with reason "companion of …"; keep it unless the user wants the cursor visible (remove it alone with gripforge_gamekit_remove), and never code requestPointerLock by hand. Kits are bricks that go together: two kits handling the same thing (e.g. two lightings) are a same-scene overlap, never a game-level conflict — only one is active in a scene. Returns { plan, applied, added, project }; dry_run=true previews without writing. Check gripforge_gamekit_installed first, then gripforge_gamekit_search; tune with gripforge_gamekit_configure. To adapt a kit to the game, go through its extension points first — its configuration, its overridable collections, rules and scripts on its events, hooks documents on the hooks it declares (engine.hooks) — and recode or copy a kit only as a last resort, saying why: a copy is no longer updated. Versions are for your information (projects always follow the latest): each kit also has version (in the project), latest, delivered { godot | unity | unreal } (the version the last engine delivery carries — a delivered game can run an older one) and pendingMigrations (manual migrations left to you). Installed kits are choices already made for this game: build on them for what they cover and configure them as needed; search the catalogue only for what they do not cover. 0 credits.

definition.name: gripforge_gamekit_remove
definition.title: Uninstall a Game Kit from a project
definition.description: Uninstall a kit from a Game Kit project (gkp_…). Remove a kit the user installed (addedBy user in gripforge_gamekit_installed) only when the user asks. game.engine (the engine of the game) and the default kits (ui.menu, input.remap, settings.graphics, ui.prompts, ui.endscreen, save.persistence, audio.core, i18n.text, ui.theme, input.virtualpad, display.fullscreen, asset.preload, asset.cache, ai.navigation on web, addedBy default) are removed only when the user explicitly asks — never to "clean up". A kit other kits depend on, and game.engine always, is not removed by a first call: it answers 409 (kit_in_use, or confirm_required) with details { dependents, confirm } — nothing applied; show the user the dependents, then call again with with_dependents=true and confirm=<token> to remove the kit and its dependents together (the token is bound to the project revision). dry_run=true returns the plan, the dependents and the token without writing. force=true (legacy) removes it and disables its dependents instead; prune=true also drops the dependencies nothing else needs (never game.engine nor a default kit). Returns { applied, removed[], dependents, project }. 0 credits.

definition.name: gripforge_gamekit_search
definition.title: Search the Game Kit catalogue
definition.description: Journey — first: find the preset of the genre. Its `done` says what a finished game of that genre has beyond the request: write it into the contract (gripforge_define_game) as required, and gripforge_game_audit checks it at the end. Start here. Search the modular Game Kit catalogue (vehicle.driveable, mission.objectives, npc.wanted, …) by free text, capability, tag or engine target. Pass project_id to score kits against that project: each hit then carries state { installed, enabled, fills, reason } and kits that fill one of its missing capabilities rank first. Kits are bricks that go together: a kit handling the same thing as an installed one is a same-scene overlap (only one active in a scene), never a reason to skip it. Returns { kits, presets }; each kit carries its presentation: name, tagline (one-line hook), tags, targets and status per engine (web / godot / unity / unreal), and cover / coverUrl, the featured landscape image (WebP) to show the user when proposing kits. legacy.* kits play through their existing client. Kart Racing is native: compose world.racetrack + vehicle.driveable + race.kart; edit race_tracks through project data. world.lighting adds shared sun/fill, point lights and spots, presets, bounded light budgets and bloom; edit world_lights through project data. world.fluids adds interactive mud / blood surfaces, displaced 3D wheel ruts and footprints; edit fluid_surfaces through project data (web renderer). world.terrain adds a seeded large landscape (terrain_edits data), movement.traversal climbing / swimming / gliding with stamina, world.elements data-driven fire, water, ice, electricity and poison (element_rules, element_materials, element_climates data). Also returns packs: content packs (ready-made game content — documents and kit configs, e.g. a realistic atmosphere, a tree of life, a star system) that gripforge_gamekit_install { pack } installs into a project. Call this BEFORE gripforge_gamekit_install. 0 credits.

definition.name: gripforge_generate_building
definition.title: Generate a building
definition.description: Reusable plan → artistic concept → isolated reference views → review → Meshy or explicitly selected Tripo build workflow. Generate 1–4 images through OpenAI or Imagine; alternate views reference one master but must be checked for actually different viewpoints. If edits repeat the front, use one good concept instead of a false multiview set. Separate explicit budgets for concepts and 3D. Accepts text, owned concept views or a static GLB. Optional delivery preserves the source master and prepares reusable LOD GLBs with PBR and a common metric fit. Durable jobs return workspace links; poll generation_read, cancel/retry preserves finished steps. Review the actual render before publishing. No guaranteed interiors, collisions or runtime LOD switching; no automatic game replacement.

stage.description: plan is free: exact prompts and separate image/3D quotes. concept creates reviewable workspace images. First review artistic scene, then isolated views of the SAME building, then build 3D from chosen isolated references.

budget.description: Required for paid concept/build: maximum GripForge credits OR subscription USD accepted. Use the quote funding currency: insufficient AI allowance falls back to GripForge credits for the whole new job, never both. Use plan.concept_quote for images, plan.quote for Meshy. Provider credits are separate.

look.description: Rendering look, separate from the game style: stylized (neutral) | painted | toon | anime | realistic | lowpoly | pixel. Old values (handpainted, cartoon, low_poly…) are read as aliases. Omit for the style default. Fills style when style is omitted; toon, anime and pixel add their phrase to the prompt.

provider.description: 3D provider pinned to this recipe, Meshy by default. Tripo v3.1 requires one reviewed concept (no multiview yet) and uses v3.5 PBR textures. No automatic paid provider fallback.

tripoQuality.description: Tripo-only quality; default detailed geometry and detailed textures. extreme requests 8K. Read the separate provider quote. Exclusive with Meshy meshQuality and source.

dimensions.description: Maximum footprint and height in metres. Uniform fit preserves proportions; actual dimensions are returned.

concept.description: Owned PNG/JPEG/WebP revision for Meshy image-to-3D. At most 12 MiB. Mutually exclusive with source.

concepts.description: Coherent views of ONE building, front first, for Meshy multi-image-to-3D. Exclusive with concept/source. Review coherence before building.

meshQuality.description: Meshy 7.1 quality. Defaults standard geometry and 2K PBR. Multi-image supports standard/2k geometry only. Texture resolution is preserved during optimization. Read the updated quote.

delivery.description: Preserve an immutable full-detail source without provider remeshing, then prepare 1–3 independent LOD GLBs. Highest detail first, decreasing triangles and texture sizes. Default maxError=.001, lockBorder=true prioritizes detail and may exceed targets. For distant levels, explicitly allow e.g. maxError=.005/.01 and lockBorder=false after review. Shared metric fit and preserved PBR. No normal rebake, runtime LOD switching or inferred collision. Also works with source at no provider cost.

source.description: Reuse an owned static GLB revision instead of paying for this building. The source is never modified.

finish.description: Free deterministic repair of an owned source + delivery. All coordinates are Y-up metres AFTER the returned importTransform. Explicit oriented removal boxes (rotation XYZ radians), regular shutters (+Z outward, yaw radians) and railing paths (feet, vertical posts, supports slopes). Measure and review regions first. Applied AFTER each LOD simplification to keep thin parts straight. Textures outside cuts stay byte-identical; removed surfaces are not capped. Triangle targets remain soft. No AI auto-segmentation or collision repair.

concept_provider.description: Default openai (GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, high quality). xai explicitly selects Imagine. Provider is pinned in the durable job; never silently falls back. Read the provider-specific concept_quote.

concept_reference.description: Owned artistic reference to EDIT into new scene/isolated views. Distinct from recipe.concept, which reuses an existing front view without generation. Exclusive with recipe.concept/concepts/source and stage=build.

concept_views.description: Unique views starting with front_right. Default one view for scene or Tripo, three for isolated Meshy. Tripo requires one view. Alternate views edit the SAME master. recipe.concept reuses an existing master; concept_reference guides a NEW master.

definition.description: Manufacture a NEW fps-arms work asset using the native FPS template: curved hand surface refinement, fitted skinned long sleeves/cuff, optional tactical glove reinforcement and embedded PBR. recipe={version:1,name,quality:high|standard,gloves:tactical|light,sleeves:long|none,colors?:{fabric:#RRGGBB,sleeve:#RRGGBB,trim:#RRGGBB},source?:{assetId,revisionId,fileRole?}}. Legacy modular_doors remains available for articulated doors. stage=plan quotes each stage without spending; paid stages require its budget. Durable job; poll generation_read. Work draft, real-render review and target-engine driving test required; no automatic publication/replacement.

definition.name: gripforge_generate_weapon_catalog
definition.title: Generate a weapon catalogue
definition.description: Plan then manufacture 1–64 original static weapon models using the existing Meshy PBR pipeline. plan is free and returns an exact aggregate quote and plan_hash. build requires that hash, an explicit budget covering the quote and a stable idempotency_key. One durable job, two bounded fabrication lanes, per-weapon checkpoints and billing; cancellation/retry preserves finished work and provider task IDs. Results remain private work assets. Inspect geometry, textures and actual renderer output before publishing. Does not create attack/reload animations, grip bindings, or flexible-chain physics. Poll gripforge_generation_read; result.items contains Library IDs and Studio links.

prompt.description: The weapon to model, up to 2000 characters accepted. The catalogue is made by Meshy text-to-3D: a description longer than its room (about 680 characters) is refused by name (prompt_too_long_for_provider) at the plan, never cut; gripforge_generate_weapon with provider "gpu" takes the 2000.

definition.name: gripforge_hud
definition.description: Required completion gate: action=workflow stays ready=false until a current runtime capture passes all artistic criteria. After screen_assets/assembly, submit screen_item (or design/project), renderer_version, capture_item, capture and the authorized review_budget; workflow schedules the reviewer automatically. Poll workflow; correct and recapture if changes_requested. No paid retry loop. Genre-independent workflow: pass design (from plan, edited) WITHOUT project to get/quote/concept/review_quote/review. get returns the normalized design hash; quote then concept returns reference_item. For review supply design, reference_item, renderer_version (fingerprint of actual presenter/build including styles/assets/dependencies), capture_item and capture. Forward exact quote.next and poll the generation job. This reviews an immutable snapshot; compare returned identity with current files before reusing the result. No installed kit or per-genre adapter is needed for concept/review. Project mode remains available: Artistic QA: get returns renderer_version and latest review. Upload a fresh HUD viewport screenshot to the private Library, call review_quote with capture_item/capture, forward exact next to review and poll its job. Re-read get: only current approved review validates that capture/state; preview cannot validate game contrast. Reusable HUD design: action templates/plan/get/apply/quote/concept uses HUD Studio v2 + hud.tactical + ui.theme; concept is a durable per-game AI reference. Live web adapters: FPS hud.tactical, or a shared document presenter for health/mana/XP bars, currencies, quest trackers, panels, text and images using explicit bindings. Other widgets and native document presenters require integration. Omit action for legacy. Survivor HUD kit: hud.json + cartoon PNGs + Godot .tscn + Three / Unity / Unreal snippets. Writes the folder (npm). 1 credit. Do not redraw the hearts.

Use it when an asset arrives and before delivery; with project_id it reads what each bound model needs, makes only the missing copies and gives them to the server. definition.name: gripforge_map_generate
definition.title: Create map concept views or an editable map
definition.description: Queue a persistent map job. stage=concept creates a private master overview plus optional views and stops. views: overview,top_down,entrance,objective. All additional views are conditioned on the SAME pinned master; they are illustrations, not exact 3D renders. reference is an environment screenshot for a NEW layout. To add views to an existing concept, pass source_concept instead; the master is kept unchanged and is free. One credit per new image (full new 4-view set = 4); default is overview only. Poll generation_read with include_preview=true to see the views. After the user selects the concept, submit stage=build with the returned concept and a new idempotency key. Build costs 1 credit and is the default for existing callers; legacy concept_item accepts a Library image ID, while concept pins its exact version. wizard: look stylized|painted|toon|anime|realistic|lowpoly|pixel (rendering, separate from style; omit for the theme default); style realistic|stylized|lowpoly|handpainted (legacy wording); world open_world|closed_arena|dungeon|linear|battle_map; terrain auto|plains|desert_canyon|forest|snow|island|volcanic; size small|medium|large; boundary fixed|infinite (open edge, finite terrain); spawn single|teams; teams 2|4; boss,safeZone,extraction booleans. sources selects catalog/workspace/community props. Build uses the common Scene Engine with independent terrain, regions, paths, zones and asset instances. Cancel/retry keeps successful images and billing. No automatic visual validation, promotion or Unreal import.

style.description: Legacy wording kept in the intent; it does not change the rendering. Use look.

look.description: Rendering look, separate from the game style: stylized (neutral) | painted | toon | anime | realistic | lowpoly | pixel. Old values (handpainted, cartoon, low_poly…) are read as aliases. Omit for the style default. Map: the theme gives the biome, the look the materials (LevelSpec.look).

dimensions.description: Explicit ground footprint in metres. Overrides size presets and world multipliers. Example: {width:500,depth:500}. Four-team maps require a square.

reference.description: Pinned source-environment screenshot for stage=concept only. Upload to Library and pin first.

source_concept.description: Existing immutable master to add views to, stage=concept only. Mutually exclusive with reference; never regenerate this master.

views.description: Unique requested views, stage=concept only. The master overview is always included; omitting views keeps overview only.

concept.description: Exact chosen concept revision for stage=build. Mutually exclusive with concept_item.

concept_item.description: Legacy Library concept image ID. Prefer an immutable concept reference.

Read gripforge_map_schema for the contract. Preserves canyon voids; validates bridge clearance, endpoints and slopes. Uses durable per-piece assets and the common SceneDocument. Dimensions must match wizard.dimensions. Solo maps only; result is a structural work version requiring visual review.

definition.name: gripforge_moba_map
definition.title: Generate, dress, check and set the map of a MOBA project
definition.description: The map of a moba project as a gameplay plan: bounds, team bases and spawns, 1 to 5 lanes (the minions' paths), structure slots (towers, inhibitors, nexus), jungle zones and camp slots, objective zones, the divider (river: walkable; chasm, lava, void: crossed only at bridges), crossings, bush zones, walls, camera limits and symmetry. action "generate" builds a fair map (mirrored through the centre) from lanes, divider, size, team_size, camps_per_jungle, objectives, bushes, walls and returns it with a playability report; apply: true puts it in the project (moba_maps, the match's map and team size, the camera turn). action "validate" checks a map you pass, or the project's: every lane open end to end, spawns, structures and camps reachable, nothing out of bounds, the declared symmetry respected. action "set" stores an edited map document (refused while it has errors, unless force). action "get" returns the current map and its report. New maps default to style {theme: "sanctum", detail: "high", seed: 11, relief: "landscape"}. action "dress" previews a reusable procedural finish for the current map: jungle plateaus, river banks and paved fords, terraced bases, walkable staircases, carved structures, clustered forests, stone guardians and lilies; apply: true saves only the map document, keeping its lane layout and camera configuration; relief updates the shared terrain mesh, ground queries and stair collisions; landscape is the default, terraced keeps base terraces only, flat keeps a level arena. Themes: sanctum, wildwood, ashen; detail: low, medium, high; seed makes the finish repeatable. Bound Library models and textures take precedence. The scenery kit dresses walls and bushes with the bound models. 0 credits.

definition.name: gripforge_prepare_vehicle
definition.title: Prepare segmented vehicle hinges in Blender
definition.description: Durable Blender preparation of an owned static segmented GLB. Map each Door_FL/FR/RL/RR or Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR to exact mesh node names from the segmentation report. Keeps geometry placement, UVs and PBR; normalizes +Z forward/metres using yaw and length; adds hinge origins, seat/entry sockets and portable GLB open/close/preview clips. Optional hinge coordinates are in normalized vehicle metres. thickness adds an inward door shell, not a full cabin. Optional cuts provide strictly convex door outlines [forwardZ,heightY] and depth [near,far] measured from the centre on that side, in normalized metres. cuts[].meshes restricts each cut to exact exterior/glazing meshes so seats and dashboard cannot be cut. removeMeshes discards explicitly named obsolete trim in the work copy only. Optional clearanceDepthM clears scoped inner walls behind the door skin; trim adds measured body frames, seals and moulded cards below cardTopY. framePoints follows outline in normalized [x,y,z]. Optional trim.fitToSurface projects frames, seals and the inner card onto only the explicitly selected opaque door skin, preserving the supplied outline. attachments adds scoped [min,max] [x,y,z] volumes for mirrors extending beyond the door profile. Blender cuts those explicit profiles while interpolating UVs. Does not infer outlines or guarantee clearance. Returns job_id, new private work GLB, Blender source and animated Studio review link. 0 credits; storage applies. Inspect before replacement.

definition.name: gripforge_projectile_create
definition.title: Create projectile VFX
definition.description: ADMIN ONLY. Create an editable 3D projectile: ignition, elemental volume, world-space trail, embers, contact flash, oriented ring and soot. 20 named variants: darts, short bolts, orbs, wisps, carrot rocket, spinning disc, spears, comets, coils and lightning. config.variant selects the geometry, trail and impact; style/color optionally override its palette. definition.name: gripforge_scene_realism
definition.title: Shared materials, automotive lighting and post-processing
definition.description: Apply reusable architectural surface profiles and GTAO to a saved work scene. Read gripforge_scene_schema.realism first. assignments [{nodeId,material:"*" or a named slot,surface:{preset:preserve|brick|stone|metal|glass,detail:0..1,weathering:0..1,regions:[]}}]; surface:null removes only this local profile. Optional glass regions use explicit normalized mesh-local min/max bounds and interior parallax settings. Never guess masks from colours. ambientOcclusion {enabled,radius:0.02..3 metres,intensity:0..1,quality:low|medium|high}, or null to remove. Preserves transforms, source PBR maps, other instances and validated revisions. Returns Studio link for visual comparison. Optional quality {preset:performance|balanced|quality,resolutionScale:0.5..1,sharpness:0..0.5}, or null to restore the original presentation. Quality supports viewport resolution up to a bounded 4K budget. Optional automotive {look:studio|daylight,quality,lengthM,depthOfField:false,focusDistanceM} explicitly applies a whole-scene look: HDR strip reflections, contact AO, quality and restrained post-processing. Studio replaces an existing HDRI; daylight keeps it. Optional colorGrading/depthOfField overrides or null. DOF is perspective/capture only, disabled with volumetric passes. No generation charge, DLSS or automatic approval.

definition.name: gripforge_third_party_kit_add
definition.title: Declare a third-party kit in a game
definition.description: Declare a third-party kit — a kit of game logic compiled alone into one .wasm (a kit module), not one of GripForge's — in a local game, in the COMMON memory of the game by default (not isolated) or, with trust "isolated", with a memory of its own. Reads one build of gripforge_third_party_kit_build (kit: its output folder; or wasm + manifest, file or http(s) URL), checks it (the binary against the manifest; against the core and the kits of the game's kit modules when the game has them; the kits it requires against the game), then writes: project.thirdPartyKits (source, sha256, manifest), its entry in project.installed (config), its place at the end of lock.order, and lock.thirdParty (version and sha256 frozen). A module given as a file is copied beside the game (third-party-kits/). A third-party module is loaded only when the game declares it; the page then plays the kit modules by itself. Use GripForge's kits first (gripforge_gamekit_search): a third-party kit is for a rule no kit has. check=true writes nothing. Calling it again with a new build replaces the kit. Guide: gripforge_docs { topic: "kit-third-party" }.

game.description: Absolute path of the game: its game.json ({ "project": …, "lock": … }), or the folder that holds it (an exported web game).

kit.description: Absolute path of the output folder of gripforge_third_party_kit_build (it holds build.json): the build of the trust asked is taken from it. Use this, or wasm + manifest.

wasm.description: The kit module: absolute path of the .wasm, or an http(s) URL (with manifest; or give kit instead).

manifest.description: The .kit.json written beside the module by the build: absolute path, or an http(s) URL.

trust.description: How far the game trusts this kit. "common" (default): the kit is placed in the memory of the core and of the other kits, as a GripForge kit is — faster, and NOT isolated. "isolated": the kit keeps a memory of its own and cannot read or corrupt the game — choose it explicitly for a kit you do not trust. The build declared must be the one of that mode.

config.description: Config of the kit in the game (what kx.config() returns). Kept from the previous declaration when omitted.

modules.description: Absolute path of a folder of kit modules (kit-modules.json) to check against and to install the module in. Default: <game folder>/runtime-rust/kit-modules, else <game folder>/kit-modules, when present.

definition.name: gripforge_third_party_kit_build
definition.title: Build a kit of your own on the build base
definition.description: The common build tool of the kit logic modules: compiles the source of a kit of your own (a folder with kit.json — { "schema": "gripforge.kit-module/1", "id", "version", "services"?, "requires"?, "optional"? } — and src/lib.rs giving "pub fn module() -> Rc<dyn KitModule>"; no Cargo.toml, no export macro) on the base GripForge fixes: the pinned Rust toolchain with its components, the locked crates, the options of each mode. Writes, per mode, <id>-<version>.<mode>.wasm and its manifest .kit.json (provides/consumes read from the binary, sha256), plus build.json; checks each binary against the base (its mode, its structures table, the links it takes). Both modes by default: "isolated" (a memory of its own) and "common" (relocatable, for a game that trusts the kit). Runs cargo locally: the first build of the common mode rebuilds the standard library (a minute or two). When the toolchain is missing the error gives the one rustup command to run (install: true runs it; it adds a toolchain beside the others and never changes the default one). Then declare a build with gripforge_third_party_kit_add. Guide: gripforge_docs { topic: "kit-third-party" }.

out.description: Absolute path of the output folder. Default: <kit>/build.

mode.description: Which build(s) to make. Default: both.

install.description: true: install the pinned toolchain with rustup when it is missing.

target_dir.description: Absolute path of the cargo target folder. Default: <kit>/target/gripforge-kit.

sdk.description: Absolute path of the kit SDK: the kit-sdk folder of the GripForge CLI, or a GripForge checkout. Default: GRIPFORGE_KIT_SDK, else the SDK of the gripforge CLI found on PATH.

definition.name: gripforge_vehicle_finish
definition.description: Repair generated automotive surfaces. Preferred: source (immutable static GLB with Body/Wheel_* groups) + repair recipe queues a persistent Blender job; guided glazing/panel regions, paint cleanup, coloured caliper extraction, measured replacement panels/curves with PBR and fitted boundaries, optional rebuilt wheels and rigid wheel rig. features.marks adds surface-fitted pinned PNG logos, relief badges and mesh lettering; wheel markings follow their wheel, named authored marks are replaced in the new work copy. For grilles or trim on a reconstructed recess, set curves.fitSurface.panel to its non-structural panel name to follow the final part. Returns a NEW private work version with GLB/Blend/optional FBX and GripForge review link. Does not promote or overwrite the source. Regions use +Y up/+Z forward metres, bounded displacement; region-only glass stays opaque, authored transmissive panes need an authored cabin. Poll/cancel/retry generation-jobs. 0 provider credits. Legacy id without repair uses one-time material/wheel finish and rewrites its Library file.

id.description: Library id; with repair pins source, without repair uses legacy finish

source.description: Pinned static source, instead of id

denoise.description: Bounded Body smoothing across UV seams; pins open boundaries, retains UVs and wheel/caliper transforms; review small details

replaceBody.description: Explicitly replace coachwork in a new work copy using structural panels; preserve wheels and Body calipers.

Explicit normal/up frame; target wheel marks spin with that wheel. Optional receiver scopes fitting to a mesh in the target. PNGs <=1 MiB/2048px, max 16 distinct sources. No URLs or local paths.

features.description: Measured panels, curves, badges and decals; explicit PBR, clipping, symmetry, 250k vertex budget.
