definition.name: asset_add
definition.description:
Add a local media file (image, font, video, or audio) to the workspace so it can be used in a design. Copies the file bytes into the content-addressed asset store at `assets/<sha>.<ext>`. The bring-your-own arm of the asset family: `asset_search` finds an existing asset, `asset_generate` makes one, `asset_add` takes one off your disk — all three return a `workspace://` uri to embed in `edit`. (To turn a design FILE into a new design, use `import`.)

Returns JSON: `{ uri, httpUrl, mimeType, kind, width?, height?, bytes, note? }`; an image has `width` and `height` in pixels — frame it at that aspect unless you mean to crop it (a logo never). `uri` (a `workspace://` URI) is the durable handle — embed it in a subsequent `edit` (image/video fill or audio `fileURI`; for a font, as both `text.font: { typeface, uri }`'s uri and `typeface.fonts[].uri`), NEVER `httpUrl` and NEVER the original `file://` path, so the design stays loadable after a restart or rewind. `httpUrl` is a fetch link for opening the asset now.

Files are classified by content (magic bytes) first, extension second: a misnamed file is stored under its actual type, and `note` explains any correction, rescue, or unverifiable content.

Make-available only: it never edits a scene and never creates a revision — do the placement in `edit`.

Source: `{ path }` — an absolute path to a file the server can read.

path.description: Absolute path to a local media file the server can read (image/font/video/audio).

definition.name: asset_generate
definition.description:
Generate images, video, speech, music and sound effects — and transcribe speech — via the AI gateway.

Call with NO arguments first: returns the curated model catalog, every entry tagged with its `capability` (text2image, image2image, text2video, image2video, text2speech, speech2text, …). Filter with `capability`; `source: "all"` (together with a `capability`) adds the provider models — e.g. music and sound effects under `text2audio`.

Then call with `model` + `prompt` (+ optional `format` aspect like "16:9"). Model-specific inputs (duration, voice, lyrics, an input file…) go in `params`, sent to the model verbatim under the model's own field names — `model` + `schema: true` returns the fields a model takes. A `uri` inside `params` that an earlier tool result gave you is uploaded for the model first (e.g. `{ audio_url: '<id>' }` to transcribe).

For image-to-image, pass `image_uris` with uris an earlier tool result gave you. Never assemble one by hand.

Returns ONE JSON part: the asset, in the engine's own asset shape — `{ id, meta: { uri, mimeType, kind, duration?, width?, height?, thumbUri? } }`, the same objects `asset_search` returns, plus `cost` (credits) when the gateway reports it. `id` is the durable handle: embed it in `edit` code (image or video fill, audio block) and pass it back here as an `image_uris` entry. It equals `meta.uri`. `meta.kind` is `image`, `video`, `audio` or `file`; `meta.duration` (seconds, as a string) is present for audio/video when the file header states it. Any other result that is data rather than a file comes back as `{ output }`, verbatim.

Transcription (speech2text, e.g. `elevenlabs/scribe-v2`): put the recording's uri in the model's audio field (`audio_url`) — audio OR video of any length; the audio is extracted and long recordings are split for you. The result is `{ transcriptUri, duration, language?, wordCount, lines }`: `lines` holds one `[mm:ss.s–mm:ss.s] sentence` per sentence (times in the source), enough to pick moments by; the word timings stay in the `transcriptUri` asset — read them inside `edit` with `engine.design.readTranscript(transcriptUri, { from, to })` (words whose start lies in [from, to) seconds), e.g. to build captions.

NO PICTURE COMES BACK. To see what was generated, place it and look at the render `edit` returns: `await engine.design.setProps(blockId, { fill: { type: 'image', uri: '<id>' } })`, or `await engine.design.create({ type: 'graphic', props: { width: 400, height: 400, shape: { type: 'rect' }, fill: { type: 'image', uri: '<id>' } } }, { parent: page })`. That shows it in the layout, which is what you have to judge anyway. Do not assume a generation is good — look before you build on it.

Multi-output models (layerize-class: decompose an input image into layers) add an `assets` array of the same objects, in stack order (residual background first, then cutout layers). The top-level fields ARE `assets[0]`. Single-output results carry no `assets` array. Any non-image output the model produced is passed through VERBATIM under `metadata` — read it, it binds semantics to the assets.

Requires a free IMG.LY sign-in (the `login` tool); all other design tools work without an account.

model.description: Model id from the catalog (call with no arguments to list). Required to generate or to read a schema.

prompt.description: What to generate. Required with `model` unless the model takes its input through `params`.

format.description: Aspect ratio, e.g. "16:9" or "1:1".

image_uris.description: Uris returned by `import` or an earlier `asset_generate`, used as inputs (image-to-image models).

source.description: Catalog source: "catalog" (default, curated) or "all" (adds the provider models; needs `capability`).

schema.description: With `model`: return that model's input schema instead of generating.

params.description: Model-specific inputs sent verbatim (e.g. { "voice": "Aria" }, { "duration": 8 }). Asset uris inside are uploaded first.

definition.name: asset_search
definition.description:
Search every asset source of this server's engine, live; earlier sources rank first. Read-only — never creates a revision.

Returns JSON `{ sources: [{ source, description, total, nextPage, failed, assets }] }`; each asset has `id`, `label`, `mimeType`, `uri` and `groups`, an image its `width` and `height` in pixels, and a typeface asset (e.g. from the `ly.img.gfonts` Google Fonts source) a compact `typeface: { name, weights, styles }`. A source's `description` says what it holds. Typefaces: `mimeType: ['application/ubq-typeface']`.

The `ly.img.workspace.images` source is this workspace's own store: every image the agent generated or imported AND every image the human uploaded in the browser editor, newest first. Uploads carry their original filename as `label` (the human will refer to it — "use logo-final.png" — so search that name) and `groups: ["uploads"]`. "The image the user just uploaded" = the first asset in the `uploads` group.

⚠ Asset sources are deployment configuration — where their content lives (IMG.LY CDN, a customer host) is the server's business. NEVER fetch asset manifests (`content.json`) or hardcode `cdn.img.ly` URLs yourself; this tool and the uris it returns are the only correct path. A source this tool does not name is not available on this server — say so instead of working around it.

To USE a result, apply it inside `edit` code — either:
(A) new block: `await engine.design.create({ type: 'graphic', props: { shape: { type: 'rect' }, fill: { type: 'image', uri }, width, height, contentFill: { mode: 'Cover' } } }, { parent: page })` with the asset's `uri` — keep `width`:`height` at the asset's aspect, or let `Cover` crop a photo; a logo or other mark takes `{ mode: 'Contain' }`; audio: `{ type: 'audio', props: { audio: { fileURI: uri } } }`;
(B) existing block: `await engine.design.setProps(blockId, { fill: { type: 'image', uri }, contentFill: { mode: 'Cover' } })` with the asset's `uri` — `Cover` fills the frame and crops what does not fit, right for a photo; a logo or mark takes `{ mode: 'Contain' }`, or a frame at its `width`:`height`, so it is never cut.
(C) fonts: set the family BY NAME inside `edit` — `text: { font: { family: name, weight: 'normal' } }` in `engine.design.create` or `engine.design.setProps`; the edit API finds the family and loads the weight. Never copy font URIs out of this tool into edit code.

query.description: Words to find in labels and tags. Omit to list.

mimeType.description: Only these types: exact (`image/png`) or a family (`image/*`).

source.description: Only this source, as a result named it.

groups.description: Only assets in one of these groups.

definition.name: checklist
definition.description:
Register the brief's ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST — the machine-checkable claims that must hold before the work counts as done. Do this right after intake, before the first edit: extract from the brief every required output file, every string of approved copy that must land verbatim, and note the constraints only you can check. Skip it only when the brief fixes no outputs or copy.

Item kinds:
- { kind: 'output', path } — a file that must exist when the work is delivered (absolute path, e.g. every variant the brief orders exported with `outPath`).
- { kind: 'copy', text } — approved copy that must appear VERBATIM in the design's text (whitespace variants are folded; wording, case and punctuation are exact).
- { kind: 'note', text } — a self-check the server cannot verify. Kept on record; never machine-checked.

Every `export` checks the list against the design and the disk and names the unmet items — treat one exactly like a failing test. Calling `checklist` again REPLACES the whole list; it lasts for this conversation.

Returns `{ itemCount }`, or `{ items }` (the current list) when called without `items`.

items.description: The full checklist (at most 64 items); replaces the current one. Omit to read the current list.

definition.name: designs
definition.description: The saved designs you can `open` or `import` a copy of, newest first. The one you are working on is marked `current`. A row marked `unsaved` is work an earlier session left without saving: `open` it to continue, then save.

definition.name: diagnostics
definition.description: Inspect this codesign MCP server: `status` (default) reports what is running (build id, CE.SDK engine version, non-secret config); `summary` returns a bounded digest of recent activity (counts, recent errors, slowest calls); `open` returns a clickable local viewer URL with a Download-ZIP button to send diagnostics to IMG.LY.

action.description: status (default) | summary | open

definition.name: edit
definition.description:
Edit the CE.SDK canvas by running JavaScript against the live CreativeEngine. The result becomes the session’s current state.

⚠ BEFORE your first `edit`, load the installed `handbook` skill; if it isn't installed, read the MCP resource `skill://codesign/handbook/SKILL.md`. It documents the design loop, the typeface schema, and the engine recipes; on cryptic errors, read `skill://codesign/handbook/quirks.md`.

There is no `parent` and no revision id: `edit` always continues the current session. To start over from a file, use `import`.

NOTHING YOU DO HERE IS VISIBLE TO THE USER until you save the design with `export({ format: "imgly" })`. Edits advance the session; saving is what produces a file they can open.

Returns: the first content part is JSON `{ names? }` — every named block in the scene, which are exactly the strings `engine.design.findByName(name)` resolves in your NEXT edit. Name what you build and re-find it instead of matching copy. When the edit changed the scene, the result also ends with a downscaled render of the first page it changed — verify your work from it instead of spending a `preview` call. `preview` remains required for full-size judging (the judge loop) and multi-page review; set `render: false` to skip the image on read-only/diagnostic edits.

`code` return contract (STRICT): return `undefined` (no message back), `{ type: "text", text }`, `{ type: "image", data: "<base64>", mimeType }`, or an array of those. Anything else (raw strings, Blobs, plain objects) is rejected.

DIALECT (enforced): edit code uses `engine.design` only — scene, pages, props, text, variables, spot colours, transitions. Code that reaches engine.block/scene/variable/editor/asset/event is rejected before execution with the equivalent calls.

`code` scope: `engine.design`, plus `findText(copy)` / `findAllText(copy)` for reaching a block by its text. Use them instead of comparing text strings with `===` — the copy on the page routinely carries a trailing space or an NBSP (before a `€`/`%`), which is what makes hand-rolled lookups throw. Matching folds those space variants and trims; a miss lists the copy actually on the page.

Dirty-on-throw: if your `code` throws, nothing is checkpointed and the next `edit` reloads the session from its last good state. Do not catch-and-swallow errors that should propagate — let them throw so this safety contract kicks in.

code.description: Async JS body using `engine.design` — the whole edit API; EVERY member returns a Promise (await it): create({ type, name?, props?, children? }, { parent? }), setProps(id, props), getProps(id, select?) — see the api skill. Strict return contract per the handbook.

note.description: Freeform descriptive text — what this edit accomplished. Metadata only; never load-bearing.

render.description: Default true: a mutating edit's result ends with a downscaled render of the canvas. Set false to skip the image on read-only or diagnostic edits where seeing it adds nothing.

skills.description: Optional: comma-separated names of the CoDesign skills you are following for this edit (e.g. "handbook,api,judge"). The names are sent with usage telemetry; the edit itself ignores them.

definition.name: export
definition.description:
Export the design you are working on — `format` picks the deliverable: `pdf` (print PDF), `png`/`jpeg`/`webp` (image), `svg` (vector SVG), `pdfx` (print-ready PDF/X), `html` (responsive HTML5), `idml` (Adobe InDesign), `psd` (layered PSD), `mp4` (video), `wav`/`m4a` (audio), `imgly` (editable design file). Renders `blockId` — or the whole document when `blockId` is omitted.

ONE VERB, TWO DESTINATIONS. `format: "imgly"` SAVES the design: it is the only call that produces a file the user can open, and the only thing that appears in the viewer. Every other format DELIVERS a copy — a pdf to print, a png to post — and is not a design. Save before you deliver, and save again after any further edit; there is no separate `save` tool.

Returns JSON — a save: `{ uri, designId, viewerUrl, title, bytes, format }`; a delivery: `{ uri, httpUrl, bytes, format }` (plus `path` when you pass `outPath`). `uri` is the durable handle — treat it as opaque and pass it back verbatim where a URI is wanted. `httpUrl` is a fetch link tied to this process — fetch it to download the bytes to disk, or hand it to the user.

`outPath` (optional, absolute path including the filename): ALSO write the artifact to that local path — the workspace copy is still written, and the response then carries `path`. Use it when the file is wanted on disk, and always when your environment cannot fetch localhost URLs (sandboxed harnesses, e.g. Claude Cowork — target your session's outputs folder there).

`format=svg` is the engine's vector export: text is outlined into paths (renders identically everywhere, but is not editable text in the SVG), and raster images are embedded in the file at source resolution — an SVG of a photo-heavy design can be much larger than its source images.

`format=imgly` writes a portable, self-contained `.imgly` design file (scene + all asset bytes bundled) — the inverse of `import`, and the only format that stays editable. Whole-design only: `blockId` is not accepted. This is THE SAVE: until you make it, nothing you edited is visible to the user, and re-saving overwrites the same design rather than piling up copies. Because the archive inlines every referenced asset it is the heaviest call this server makes, and it REFUSES rather than ship a design whose fonts or images could not be loaded — retry it, do not ignore it.

`format=pdfx` runs the print PDF through a PDF/X conversion: CMYK with an embedded ICC profile and PDF/X conformance markers, ready for a print shop. Tune it via the optional `pdfx` object — conformance standard (X-4 default / X-3 / X-1a), output profile (fogra39/gracol/srgb/custom), transparency flattening and its resolution, OutputIntent metadata. srgb is never PDF/X compliant. The result carries `warnings` when the file breaks its standard (each names the fix): relay them or re-export before calling the file print-ready. CMYK and spot colours, bleed and the print checklist: `skill://codesign/handbook/print.md`.

`format=html` renders ONE page (`blockId` required — pass a page id) to responsive HTML5. Default is a single self-contained `.html` (assets inlined; animated designs get a CDN GSAP player injected so the file plays as-is); `html: { assets: "external" }` delivers html + separate image/font files as one `.zip`.

`format=mp4` renders the authored timeline of the block (typically a page) to an H.264 `mp4`; duration and resolution come from the scene; frame rate is `fps` (default 30). Requires the native engine (the default). Long encodes report MCP progress notifications when the client sends a progressToken. The result also carries `duration` (seconds of video) and `audioDuration` (seconds of audio; absent when the mp4 has no audio track), both read from the encoded file — no need to probe it.

`format=wav` / `format=m4a` renders the audio mix of a page (`blockId` required, a page id): every audio block and video-fill audio on it, over the page duration. `wav` is 48 kHz stereo 32-bit float, `m4a` is AAC. The result carries `duration` (seconds, read from the encoded file). To get one clip alone, export while it is the only audio on the page. Requires the native engine. Every clip sounds over exactly its own window (within a few ms; its first ~10 ms may be silent), whatever its start and trim. `m4a` as a whole may sit ~35 ms late from AAC encoder priming, as in the mp4.

format.description: The deliverable: pdf → print PDF; png/jpeg/webp → image; svg → vector SVG; pdfx → print-ready PDF/X; html → HTML5 page; idml → Adobe InDesign document; psd → layered PSD; mp4 → video; wav/m4a → audio; imgly → editable design file.

blockId.description: The page to render; an image format takes any block. Omit to export the whole document: a multi-page PDF, or one composite image of all pages. Required for format=html/psd (pass a page id). Required for `format=mp4` (pass a page id). Required for `format=wav`/`m4a` (pass a page id).

pdfx.description: Options for `format=pdfx` only (invalid with any other format). Omit entirely for sensible print defaults: PDF/X-4, fogra39, embedded ICC.

outputStandard.description: PDF/X conformance target. PDF/X-4 (default) keeps live transparency. PDF/X-3 is the older PDF 1.4 standard — it flattens transparency by default and can rasterize gradients/alpha content. PDF/X-1a: CMYK and spot only (no srgb), always flattened.

outputProfile.description: Target printing condition / ICC output profile. fogra39 (default) = ISO Coated v2 (ECI), European offset. gracol = GRACoL 2013 CRPC6, US commercial. srgb = keep RGB, for digital distribution — not PDF/X compliant. custom = supply the print shop's ICC file via profileUri.

profileUri.description: Required with outputProfile="custom" (invalid otherwise): an https:// URL or absolute local file path of the .icc profile to embed.

flattenTransparency.description: PDF/X-3 only (default true there): rasterize transparent content for strict compliance. false keeps transparency live — better fidelity, may not validate. Ignored on PDF/X-4; PDF/X-1a always flattens.

flattenResolution.description: Dpi of flattened pages, default 300 (PDF/X-1a, and PDF/X-3 unless flattenTransparency is false).

nonPrinterProfile.description: Output profile that is not a printer profile (srgb, a custom RGB one): keep (default) writes the file, not compliant; reject fails the export.

embedICCProfile.description: Default true. false → plain CMYK (or RGB) PDF with no embedded ICC profile, OutputIntent, or PDF/X markers — for prepress pipelines that apply their own profile.

title.description: PDF document title. Defaults to the design's title.

outputConditionIdentifier.description: Overrides the PDF's /OutputConditionIdentifier — the REGISTERED printing-condition name preflight tools and print shops check (e.g. "FOGRA39", "CGATS 21.2"). Defaults from outputProfile; with a custom profile, your print shop tells you what to put here.

outputCondition.description: Overrides /OutputCondition — the human-readable printing-condition description (e.g. "ISO Coated v2 (ECI)"). Defaults from outputProfile.

html.description: Options for `format=html` only (invalid with any other format).

assets.description: embedded (default): one self-contained .html, assets inlined as data URLs — viewable anywhere as-is. external: html + separate image/font files, delivered as one .zip.

fps.description: Frames per second for `format=mp4` only (invalid with any other format), greater than 0. Default 30. Common values: 24, 25, 30, 60.

overwrite.description: format=imgly only. Save even though the saved design changed since your work on it began. Set it ONLY after the user chose your version over theirs — it discards their changes.

outPath.description: Absolute path (including filename) to ALSO write the artifact to — the workspace copy is still written, and the response then carries `path`. Use when you need the file on disk and cannot fetch localhost URLs (sandboxed harnesses).

definition.name: import
definition.description:
Import a design FILE as a NEW design — a CE.SDK `.imgly` design file; a Photoshop (`.psd`/`.psb`), InDesign (`.idml`), PowerPoint (`.pptx`) or PDF file; or a plain image or SVG, which becomes a one-page design sized to the image. To make a media file (image/font/video/audio) available for use INSIDE a design instead of becoming one: Use `asset_add` to bring it into the workspace, then apply it inside `edit`.

Source: `{ url }` (http/https), `{ uri }` (a saved design — you get a copy of it — or a file you were given), `{ demo }` (a design bundled with this server — ids: `"cybernews"`) or `{ path }` (absolute local file path).

Every import starts a NEW design, and you work on it from then on: the design you were on is left as it is. To keep working on a saved design itself rather than a copy, use `open` with its `uri`. With only a `title` and no `source`, it starts an empty design: do that for every new design, before you name it or build it.

Returns JSON `{ uri, title, format }` — the new design, unsaved until `export({ format: 'imgly' })` saves it; to continue it later, `open` the `uri` that save returns. Foreign-format imports may add `warnings` (what did not survive — substituted fonts, unsupported features): treat them as your touch-up list — `preview` the pages, then repair with `edit`.

source.description: The design to load. Provide exactly one of `url` (http/https), `uri` (a saved design), `demo` (a bundled demo design), `path` (absolute local file path; Local only).

url.description: http(s) URL of the design file to load.

path.description: Absolute local file path of the design file. Local-only.

uri.description: The `uri` of a saved design (you get a new design that starts as a copy of it) or of a file you were given.

demo.description: Id of a demo design bundled with this server — a finished design to demonstrate on, with no file and no build required.

title.description: Display name for the design once you save it. Defaults to the source file's basename. Without a `source`, starts an empty design under it.

discard.description: Drop the unsaved edits of the design you are on. Set it ONLY when that work is meant to be thrown away (the user said so, or it was a throwaway sketch); otherwise save it first with `export({ format: 'imgly' })`. Never set it by default.

definition.name: login
definition.description: Sign in with your IMG.LY account (opens the system browser). The session saves automatically once the user finishes in the browser; call login again anytime to confirm — safe to repeat, it does not restart the flow or invalidate the open link. Pass switch_account=true to sign in as a different user.

switch_account.description: Force a fresh sign-in screen even if a session exists.

definition.name: logout
definition.description: Sign out of your IMG.LY account (revokes the session and clears local credentials).

definition.name: open
definition.description: Work on a saved design itself: every later edit is part of it once you export `imgly`. Pass the `uri` an `import`, an `export` or `designs` gave you, verbatim. To start from a copy instead, `import` its `uri`. Returns `{ uri, title }`.

discard.description: Drop the unsaved edits of the design you are on. Set it ONLY when that work is meant to be thrown away (the user said so, or it was a throwaway sketch); otherwise save it first with `export({ format: 'imgly' })`. Never set it by default.

definition.name: preview
definition.description:
Render blocks (almost always pages) to inline images so you can see the result.

`blockIds` is a LIST, rendered in the order you give it: `[pageId]` for one page, `[a, b]` for a subset, or OMIT it entirely to preview every page of the design in document order.

There is nothing to address: this always renders the design you are working on. Its last state is loaded before rendering, so the ids always resolve against the right scene — never against a different design another agent may have loaded on a shared server.

Preview several blocks at once when REVIEWING or capturing a finished design — a whole deck in one call, or just the pages a fix touched. While BUILDING a multi-page design, keep previewing each page right after you build it: batching there does not avoid the bugs, it only delays finding them.

Animated or video designs (any scene mode): pass `time` (seconds along the timeline of what is rendered — the page, since a block is previewed in place on it; 0 = first frame) to render any frame as a still — use `export format=mp4` for motion. `time` applies to every block in the call, and each timed preview (and every preview of a Video-mode scene) returns `{blockId, time, duration}` JSON alongside its image; `duration` is the scrubbable range.

Output is always PNG (lossless — thin lines render exactly). EACH block gets the full 0.25 megapixel budget, adjusted to its own aspect ratio — a square page renders 512×512, a 1:4 page 256×1024. There are no size or format knobs, and at most 10 blocks render per call.

To SEE SMALL TYPE as it is actually set — legal copy, a caption, a label — the simplest zoom is to pass THAT BLOCK'S id: `blockIds: [<textId>]` renders it on its page, framed, with context around it. No coordinates needed.

For a tighter or arbitrary crop, pass `region`: a rectangle `{x, y, width, height}` with ONE id in `blockIds`. Its numbers are the design's own coordinates — what `engine.design.getProps(id, ['globalBoundingBox'])` returns inside `edit` — NOT pixels of a preview image you already have. Either way the crop is rendered into the same budget, so a smaller rectangle means bigger pixels, and it is never enlarged past the design's own resolution.

Previewing a block that is NOT a page renders it IN PLACE on its page — background and neighbours included — so you score what is actually on the page. `export` still produces the block alone when you need it with an alpha channel. For native-resolution certainty, `export` the page and open its `httpUrl`.

To look at a stored ASSET rather than the design — an image you just generated, or one the customer uploaded — pass `uri` instead: `preview({ uri: <meta.thumbUri from the asset> })`. Use the asset's `thumbUri`, not its `id`: the id is the full-resolution original and is refused. Nothing is rendered and no design is touched; you simply see the picture.

uri.description: Look at a stored ASSET instead of the design. Pass the `meta.thumbUri` an asset tool gave you — not its `id`, which is the full-resolution original. Cannot be combined with `blockIds`.

blockIds.description: Blocks to render, in the order you want them back — almost always page ids, not the scene root. Omit to preview every page of the design in document order. At most 10 render per call.

region.description: Rectangle to render, in the design's own coordinates — the space block bounding boxes are reported in. Requires exactly one id in `blockIds`; the rectangle is taken on that block's page. Rendered into the same 0.25 MP budget, so a smaller rectangle reads bigger, up to the design's native resolution.

time.description: Playback time in seconds (any scene mode) along the timeline of what is rendered — the page a block sits on, since blocks are previewed in place (0 = first frame) — applied to every block in the call. Each video preview returns {blockId, time, duration} JSON alongside its image — duration is the scrubbable range.

definition.name: read_skill_resource
definition.description: Read a CoDesign skill file by its `skill://codesign/<name>/<path>` URI; returns the same text as the MCP resource. Use it only when your host can't read MCP resources — otherwise read the resource directly.

definition.name: rename
definition.description:
Give a design its title — the name `designs` lists it by.

Without `uri`, renames the design you are working on: its next `export({ format: 'imgly' })` saves under the title, and if it is saved already, the saved design is renamed now. With `uri` (from `designs` or a save), renames that saved design.

Returns JSON `{ uri, title, previousTitle }`, or `{ title }` while the design is not saved yet. Nothing in the design changes.

uri.description: A saved design to rename. Omit it to rename the design you are working on.

definition.name: scorecard
definition.description:
Record the verdict of a judge loop you have COMPLETED for the design you are working on — the final step of the `judge` skill. Recording is a claim about work already done: never call this without having scored the axes against actual `preview` renders of the design in its current state.

`verdict: 'pass'` — every applicable axis scored ≥ 8; the design may be delivered. `verdict: 'fail'` — you are stopping with an axis below 8 (e.g. the user cut remediation short); the failure stays on record.

There is no `revision`: the verdict covers the session as it stands when you record it, and ANY later `edit` or `import` clears it — so judge last, and re-judge after every further change. `export` checks it: delivering or saving a design the latest verdict does not cover adds a reminder to its result.

verdict.description: 'pass' when every applicable axis scored ≥ 8, 'fail' when stopping below the gate.

definition.name: view
definition.description: Get a URL the human can open to view and edit the SAVED design in CE.SDK. Returns the design's stable URL — it survives re-saving, so print it ONCE and don't re-emit a fresh URL every turn. The page is a full editor; when the human clicks 'Save', their edits land in the same design file. Nothing is viewable until you have saved with `export({ format: 'imgly' })`. The editor opens in the mode the human last chose for this design, else 'motion' (timeline) when the design has animation, video, audio or timed blocks and 'design' otherwise; pass `mode` to force one.

mode.description: Editor mode to open in: 'motion' shows the timeline and clip tools, 'design' the still-design editor.

prompts.name: codesign
prompts.description: Start a design session with the FULL context preloaded in one message — handbook, design rules, API surface, judge + copy rules, quirks, fonts — so no reference reads are needed before the first edit. Optional brief: what to design.

arguments.name: brief
arguments.description: What to design (topic, format, audience, key content). Omit to just load the context.

resources.name: handbook
resources.description:
The CoDesign design loop, tool contract, session model, typeface schema,
common operations cheatsheet, and the full design-quality rubric.
**Read this skill before any edit call** — it contains the 6-step Loop
(resolve brief → read API → edit → verify → judge → SAVE), the tool roster
and cross-tool rules, the session model (one design context, checkpointed
after every edit, saved only by `export({ format: 'imgly' })`), the typeface
shape text.font declarations need, and §6: the design-rules index. The full
enforceable rubric (typography, hierarchy, composition, craft) ships as this
skill's design-rules.md, the runtime-quirk reference as its quirks.md, and
the input-resolution contract every skill follows as its intake.md — all read
on demand.

Triggered for any task using this server's `edit` or `preview` tools.

resources.name: animate
resources.description: Use when an existing CoDesign design should move — "animate this", "make it move", "turn this post/poster/carousel into a video", "motion version", "make a loop of this". Turns a still single- or multi-page design into one animated page and an mp4 without redesigning it, steered by one intake round and plain-language follow-ups ("slower", "logo last", "no bounce"). Not for videos from a repo or website (launch-video) or for new designs (create).

resources.name: api
resources.description:
Authoritative TypeScript signatures for `engine.design`, the only API edit
code uses. Use this skill whenever you need the exact signature, prop path,
or return type — especially before calling a member you haven't used yet.
Generated from the `.d.ts` of the same `@cesdk/node` package the engine
runs, it is THE source of truth; prose docs can drift.

This skill's entry document carries the WHOLE edit-code API surface inline
— the engine.design facade, the props trees, the attachment unions and the
capability matrix: all edit code needs, in one read.

The sub-file "signatures.d.ts" adds the upstream CE.SDK core as reference
only (edit code never calls it), every vocabulary type flattened to its
literal union.

resources.name: brand
resources.description: Use when applying a brand kit / brand style to an existing CoDesign / CE.SDK design — a rules-governed restyle (recolor + refont + logo + treatment by role), not a free-form style change; when a restyled design reads off-brand (free-chosen colors, wrong accent, a second colour used as structure, a coloured button the brand forbids, a headline set in a weight the brand bans, a flat bordered card, or the wrong / recoloured / redrawn logo); when loading a brand's fonts, wordmark SVG, or signature device into a scene; or when turning an external brand (a guidelines PDF, a website / URL, a Figma file, or a raw asset dump) into a reusable brand kit.

resources.name: create
resources.description: Use when the user asks to create / generate / make a NEW design from a prompt — a deck or slides, poster, flyer, social post, business card, a video (animated post, reel, clip with music or voiceover), or a custom-size canvas. Runs the guided intake: derive every brief parameter the prompt already answers (class, format, audience, vibe, brand, content), ask ONLY the missing questions — one round, chip-style options, "Decide automatically" defaults — then echo the design brief and hand off to the handbook Loop. A brief given to the /codesign prompt lands here as the stated input.

resources.name: formats
resources.description: Canvas-format reference for CoDesign designs — one file per screen/print format (ig-post, ig-square, ig-story, tiktok, yt-shorts, widescreen, linkedin-post, x-post, youtube-thumbnail, deck, poster, flyer, business-card): exact W×H, aspect, medium, platform safe zones, print bleed/dpi. Use when picking or setting up a canvas size, checking a platform safe zone, or preparing print dimensions. Re-composing an existing design into a format is the `resize` skill; new-design intake is the `create` skill.

resources.name: judge
resources.description: Use to quality-gate a design before reporting it done — the mandatory step 5 of the handbook Loop; when the user asks for a design review, score, audit, or QA; or when a design needs remediation after a failed review. The axes, the gate, the scorecard format, and the remediation loop are defined in this skill's body — read it before scoring; do not judge from memory of this description.

resources.name: launch-video
resources.description: Use when turning a project — a repo, an app, a product, a website — into a short launch or promo video (15–25 s, mp4): "make a launch video", "brag about this", "make a promo for what we built", "turn this into a video". Reads the project itself for the story, then builds, animates, scores and exports the video with CoDesign.

resources.name: layerize
resources.description: Use when rebuilding a flat raster image — an ad, banner, social post, poster or other creative (PNG / JPEG / WebP) — as an editable, layered CoDesign design or `.imgly` file; when asked to layerize, decompose, de-flatten or "make editable" an image; or when splitting an image into separate layers with live, editable text.

resources.name: localize
resources.description: Use when creating or fixing translated / localized variants of an existing CoDesign / CE.SDK design (e.g. de/ja/ru/ar editions); when a localized edition's text blocks or decorative elements have drifted, re-centered, or resized away from the source layout; when translated copy is tofu, overflowing, mis-tracked, or the wrong font after a language swap; or when loading a non-Latin script (Cyrillic / CJK / Arabic RTL / Vietnamese) font into a scene. Also for animated / video designs: longer holds, re-timed reveals, a new voice-over and captions per language.

resources.name: models
resources.description: Use when picking a model for `asset_generate` (image, video, speech, music, sound effects, transcription), writing its prompt or `params`, or reading its result; when a generation is rejected ("could not be processed", "flagged by a content checker", "Upstream service error"), returns the wrong content, or loses its transparency; or before chaining generation models (layer decomposition, background removal, upscaling).

resources.name: onboard
resources.description: Use when the user is new here or asks what this server is / what it can do ("what is CoDesign", "what can you make", "show me"). A guided, plain-language introduction for a HUMAN: explain what CoDesign is in everyday terms, put the six jobs it does on the table, let the user pick one, then run it either on the bundled demo design or on the user's own idea — closing with the optional (never required) IMG.LY sign-in and the ways to earn more credits. Not a design manual: the handbook remains the required read before any edit.

resources.name: resize
resources.description: Use when resizing or reformatting a CoDesign / CE.SDK design to a new size or aspect ratio (ig-post ↔ ig-square ↔ ig-story ↔ widescreen, or a custom W×H); when building the size/format editions of a design from an existing design or from a brief; or when a reformatted edition has a dead void / letterboxed empty band, drifted or broken margins, off-canvas or clipped elements, mis-scaled decoration, or a stretched / squished layout. Also for animated / video designs: timed blocks, animations, captions, and audio carried into each edition.

resources.name: video-thumbnail-template
resources.description: Use when building a reusable thumbnail template and design guideline for a video channel (YouTube and other 16:9 video platforms) — from a channel link whose latest thumbnails set the style, from one or more example thumbnails or designs, or from scratch; or when making new thumbnails from such a template, one at a time or in a batch.

definition.name: a11y_take-aria-snapshot
definition.description:
ARIA snapshot of the page or a scoped element. Returns a tree with refs (e1, e2, ...) and a refs map.
Use refs in interaction tools: selector "e1" or "@e1" to click/fill that element. Output includes URL, title, and YAML tree.
Refs are valid until next snapshot or navigation. interactiveOnly: only interactive elements get refs; omit for content roles (headings, etc.) too.
cursorInteractive: true adds refs for clickable elements without ARIA (e.g. div with cursor:pointer/onclick).
Use with a11y_take-ax-tree-snapshot for full UI analysis.

selector.description: Scope to this element; omit for full page. If it matches nothing, the full page is returned with a note.

output.description: Includes the page URL, title, and a YAML-formatted accessibility tree with [ref=e1] etc.

refs.description: Map of ref id to { role, name?, selector, nth? }. Use selector "e1" or "@e1" in interaction tools.

definition.name: a11y_take-ax-tree-snapshot
definition.description:
Combines Chromium AX tree with runtime visual diagnostics (bounding box, visibility, viewport).
Use to detect: elements with role/name but hidden or off-screen; layout/geometry issues; overlap/occlusion (enable checkOcclusion).
When investigating UI/layout or when clicks fail on seemingly visible elements, set checkOcclusion:true—it uses elementFromPoint()
at center+corners to find what is actually on top. boundingBox is from getBoundingClientRect() (viewport coords; layout box only).
selectorHint is best-effort (data-testid/data-selector/id). Use with a11y_take-aria-snapshot for full UI analysis.

roles.description: ARIA/AX role names to include; omit for default set. Standard roles: ARIA https://w3c.github.io/aria/#role_definitions, Chromium AX https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/ui/accessibility/ax_enum_util.cc (e.g. button, heading, staticText, image, main, navigation). Matching is case-insensitive; "text" also matches staticText, "img" matches image.

checkOcclusion.description: Use elementFromPoint to detect what is on top.

url.description: The current page URL at the time the AX snapshot was captured.

title.description: The document title of the page at the time of the snapshot.

axNodeCount.description: Total number of nodes returned by Chromium Accessibility.getFullAXTree before filtering.

candidateCount.description: Number of DOM-backed AX nodes that passed role filtering before enrichment.

enrichedCount.description: Number of nodes included in the final enriched snapshot output.

truncatedBySafetyCap.description: Indicates whether the result set was truncated by an internal safety cap to prevent excessive output size.

axNodeId.description: Unique identifier of the accessibility node within the AX tree.

parentAxNodeId.description: Parent AX node id in the full AX tree. Null if this node is a root.

childAxNodeIds.description: Child AX node ids in the full AX tree (may include nodes not present in the filtered output).

role.description: ARIA role of the accessibility node (e.g. button, link, textbox).

name.description: Accessible name computed by the browser accessibility engine.

ignored.description: Whether the accessibility node is marked as ignored.

backendDOMNodeId.description: Chromium backend DOM node identifier used to map AX nodes to DOM elements.

domNodeId.description: Resolved DOM nodeId from CDP if available; may be null because nodeId is not guaranteed to be stable/resolved.

frameId.description: Frame identifier if the node belongs to an iframe or subframe.

localName.description: Lowercased DOM tag name of the mapped element (e.g. div, button, input).

id.description: DOM id attribute of the mapped element.

className.description: DOM class attribute of the mapped element.

definition.name: debug_add-watch

Sets the exception tracepoint state:

- "all": Capture on all exceptions (caught and uncaught)

definition.name: debug_put-logpoint
definition.description:
Puts a logpoint at the specified location.
When the logpoint is hit, the logExpression is evaluated and the result 
is captured in the snapshot's logResult field.

Logpoints are lightweight - they only capture the log expression result,
NOT call stack or watch expressions. Use tracepoints for full debug context.

urlPattern matches script URLs (e.g., "app.js"). Auto-escaped, do not add backslashes.

logExpression: a single JavaScript expression (e.g. "user.name", "JSON.stringify({ a, b })", or "{ discountAmount, finalAmount, n }"). Object literals are supported; for maximum compatibility prefer a single variable or JSON.stringify(...).

definition.name: debug_put-tracepoint

Puts a non-blocking tracepoint at the specified location.
When hit, a snapshot of the call stack and local variables is captured 
automatically without pausing execution.

The urlPattern matches script URLs. Special characters are auto-escaped.
Examples:
- "app.js" matches scripts containing "app.js"
- "bundle.min.js" matches scripts containing "bundle.min.js"

DO NOT escape characters yourself (e.g., don't use "app\.js").

If 0, the pattern didn't match any loaded scripts.

resolvedLocations.description: Number of locations where tracepoint was resolved

removed.description: Whether the probe or watch was removed

definition.name: debug_resolve-source-location
definition.description:
Resolves a generated/bundled code location to its original source via source maps.
Useful for translating minified stack traces or bundle line numbers to original TypeScript/JavaScript source.

Requires a page with debugging context (debugging is auto-enabled on first use).
Input: generated script URL, line, column (1-based).
Output: original source path, line, column when a source map is available.

definition.name: execute
definition.description:
Batch-execute multiple tool calls in a single request via custom JavaScript. Reduces round-trips and token usage.

**IMPORTANT**
- The code is already run inside an async function. Pass only the body (statements).
  Do NOT wrap in `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }` — that causes a syntax error.
  Write `await callTool(...); return x;` directly.

**IMPORTANT:** 
- `page` (Playwright Page) is available in the VM — use it for navigation or `page.evaluate()`. 
- Prefer interaction tools with refs (e1, e2 from a11y_take-aria-snapshot); use raw Playwright only as last resort.
- `document`/`window` are not in the VM — use `page.evaluate(() => { ... })` to run code in the browser.
- Use `waitForNavigation: true` on interaction_click when the click navigates; it returns the new page's ARIA snapshot + refs.
- After navigation, refs from the previous page are refused — use the refs the navigating call returned, or take fresh ones with a11y_take-aria-snapshot.

Bindings:
- await callTool(name, input, returnOutput?): async — always use with await. Returns the tool output for in-code use.
  Every callTool invocation is listed in the response toolCalls array (name, in order), whether or not returnOutput is set.
  returnOutput=true additionally attaches that call's full output to its toolCalls entry; false (default) lists the call by name only.
  Throws on failure — execution stops at the first error; calls that ran before the failure are still listed in toolCalls (partial), with logs.
  On failure, failedTool in the response identifies which tool caused the error.
  Max 50 callTool invocations per execution.
- console.log/warn/error: captured in the response logs array.
- sleep(ms): async delay.
- args: the parameterization object passed in the `args` input (default {}). Read values via plain JS, e.g. `const { baseUrl } = args;`.

Built-ins: Math, JSON, Date, RegExp, Number, String, Boolean, Array, Object, Promise, Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet,
           Symbol, Proxy, Reflect, URL, URLSearchParams, TextEncoder/Decoder, structuredClone,
           crypto.randomUUID(), AbortController, setTimeout/clearTimeout.
NOT available: require, import, process, fs, Buffer, fetch.


**Example** — fill form, submit (with navigation wait; returns the new page's snapshot + refs), then screenshot:
  await callTool('interaction_fill', { selector: 'e3', value: 'user@test.com' });
  await callTool('interaction_fill', { selector: 'e5', value: 'secret123' });
  await callTool('interaction_click', { selector: 'e7', waitForNavigation: true }, true);
  // Or with page.locator / page.evaluate — then take the snapshot yourself with a11y_take-aria-snapshot.
  await callTool('content_take-screenshot', {}, true);

code.description: JavaScript code: the body only (no async function wrapper). Use await callTool(name, input, returnOutput?) and return for result. Do NOT wrap in async function() { ... }.

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock timeout for the entire execution in ms, including awaited tool calls and sleep (default: 30000, max: 900000).

args.description: Optional parameterization object exposed to the code as the `args` binding (default {}). Opaque — not validated. Read via plain JS, e.g. `const { baseUrl } = args;`.

name.description: Tool name (every nested call, in execution order).

startTime.description: Epoch ms when the call started.

endTime.description: Epoch ms when the call settled.

duration.description: endTime - startTime (ms).

stepId.description: Execution id of the scenario STEP this call ran inside, when a scenario-run threaded it via _metadata.stepId. Lets a consumer correlate an internal call to its step.

output.description: Tool output — present only when callTool used returnOutput=true.

children.description: Composite calls (scenario-run) expose the inner run's toolCalls here, recursively.

toolCalls.description: Complete, ordered list of every nested callTool invocation. Each entry always has `name`; `output` is present only when the call used returnOutput=true; composite calls (scenario-run) expose the inner run as `children`.

result.description: Return value of the code (JSON-safe). Undefined on error or when nothing is returned.

error.description: Error message on failure. Partial toolCalls/logs are still returned.

name.description: Tool name that failed.

error.description: Error message from the failed tool.

failedTool.description: Present when a callTool invocation caused the error.

definition.name: flush
definition.description:
Waits until this session's async background work (collector events, artifact uploads, scenario step
events) has settled. Call before ending a run or handing off, so everything reported has actually
been sent. Instant no-op when idle.

timeoutMs.description: Max total time to wait before giving up.

waited.description: Number of background tasks that were in flight.

timedOut.description: True when the timeout hit while work was still pending.

definition.name: interaction_click
definition.description: Clicks an element. Accepts selector or ref (e.g. e1, @e1). Set waitForNavigation: true when the click opens a new page — waits for navigation then up to 5 s for `load` and the page's own requests, and returns the new page's ARIA snapshot with refs (refs of the previous page stop working).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

timeoutMs.description: Wait for element, ms. Default 10000.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation triggered by click (parallel with click). Use when click opens a new page.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for navigation and for network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

animate.description: Draw a ripple at the click point so the click is visible in recordings. Defaults to whether a screen recording is running.

includeSnapshot.description: Return ARIA snapshot with refs after the click. Defaults to waitForNavigation.

output.description: When a snapshot was taken: page URL, title, and ARIA tree with refs.

refs.description: When a snapshot was taken: map of ref id to role/name/selector for use in interaction tools.

definition.name: interaction_drag
definition.description: Drags an element to a target location. Accepts CSS selectors or refs (e.g. e1, @e1) from the last ARIA snapshot.

sourceSelector.description: CSS selector or ref for the element to drag.

targetSelector.description: CSS selector or ref for the drop target.

timeoutMs.description: Wait for elements, ms. Default 10000.

animate.description: Draw a box around the element so the action is visible in recordings. Defaults to whether a screen recording is running.

definition.name: interaction_fill
definition.description: Fills out an input field. Accepts a CSS selector or a ref from the last ARIA snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot for the input.

timeoutMs.description: Wait for element, ms. Default 10000.

animate.description: Draw a box around the element so the action is visible in recordings. Defaults to whether a screen recording is running.

definition.name: interaction_hover
definition.description: Hovers an element on the page. Accepts a CSS selector or a ref from the last ARIA snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot.

timeoutMs.description: Wait for element, ms. Default 10000.

animate.description: Draw a box around the element so the action is visible in recordings. Defaults to whether a screen recording is running.

definition.name: interaction_press-key
definition.description:
Presses a keyboard key with optional "hold" and auto-repeat behavior.

Key facts:
- keyboard.press(key, { delay }) does NOT trigger OS-style auto-repeat.
- Some UI behaviors (especially scrolling) require repeated keydown events.
- Use repeat=true + holdMs to approximate real keyboard holding.

Execution logic:
- If selector is provided, the element is focused first.
- If holdMs is omitted or repeat=false:
  → a single keyboard.press() is executed.
- If holdMs is provided AND repeat=true:
  → keyboard.press() is called repeatedly until holdMs elapses.

selector.description: Focus this element first; omit for page focus.

repeat.description: Repeat key while holdMs (e.g. for scroll).

animate.description: Draw a box around the element so the action is visible in recordings. Defaults to whether a screen recording is running.

definition.name: interaction_resize-viewport
definition.description:
Resizes the PAGE VIEWPORT using Playwright viewport emulation (page.setViewportSize).

This affects:
- window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight
- CSS media queries (responsive layouts)
- Layout, rendering and screenshots

Notes:
- This does NOT resize the OS-level browser window.
- Runtime switching to viewport=null (binding to real window size) is not supported by Playwright.
  If you need real window-driven responsive behavior, start the BrowserContext with viewport: null
  and use the window resize tool instead.

viewport.description: Viewport metrics observed inside the page after resizing.

definition.name: interaction_resize-window
definition.description:
Resizes the REAL BROWSER WINDOW (OS-level window) for the current page using Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).

This tool works best on Chromium-based browsers (Chromium/Chrome/Edge).
It is especially useful in headful sessions when you run with viewport emulation disabled (viewport: null),
so the page layout follows the OS window size.

Important:
- If Playwright viewport emulation is enabled (viewport is NOT null), resizing the OS window may not change page layout.
- On non-Chromium browsers (Firefox/WebKit), CDP is not available and this tool will fail.

state.description: When not normal, width/height may be ignored.

width.description: Requested window width (pixels). Null if not provided.

height.description: Requested window height (pixels). Null if not provided.

windowId.description: CDP window id for the current target.

top.description: Window top position before resizing.

windowId.description: CDP window id for the current target.

top.description: Window top position after resizing.

viewport.description: Page viewport metrics after resizing (helps verify responsive behavior).

definition.name: interaction_scroll
definition.description:
Scrolls the page viewport or a specific scrollable element.

Modes:
- 'by': Scrolls by a relative delta (dx/dy) from the current scroll position.
- 'to': Scrolls to an absolute scroll position (x/y).
- 'top': Scrolls to the very top.
- 'bottom': Scrolls to the very bottom.
- 'left': Scrolls to the far left.
- 'right': Scrolls to the far right.

Use this tool to:
- Reveal content below the fold
- Jump to the top/bottom without knowing exact positions
- Bring elements into view before clicking
- Inspect lazy-loaded content that appears on scroll

mode.description: by=dx,dy; to=x,y; or edge (top/bottom/left/right).

selector.description: Scrollable container: ref (e.g. from latest <a11y_take-aria-snapshot>), getBy… expression, or CSS. Omit for viewport.

mode.description: The scroll mode used.

selector.description: The selector of the scroll container if provided; otherwise null (document viewport).

x.description: ScrollLeft before scrolling.

y.description: ScrollTop before scrolling.

before.description: Scroll metrics before the scroll action.

x.description: ScrollLeft after scrolling.

y.description: ScrollTop after scrolling.

after.description: Scroll metrics after the scroll action.

canScrollX.description: Whether horizontal scrolling is possible (scrollWidth > clientWidth).

canScrollY.description: Whether vertical scrolling is possible (scrollHeight > clientHeight).

isAtLeft.description: Whether the scroll position is at the far left.

isAtRight.description: Whether the scroll position is at the far right.

isAtTop.description: Whether the scroll position is at the very top.

isAtBottom.description: Whether the scroll position is at the very bottom.

definition.name: interaction_select
definition.description: Select an option in a dropdown. Accepts a CSS selector or a ref from the last ARIA snapshot (e.g. e1, @e1).

selector.description: CSS selector or ref from a11y snapshot for the dropdown.

timeoutMs.description: Wait for element, ms. Default 10000.

definition.name: navigation_go-back-or-forward
definition.description:
Navigates to the previous or next page in history.
- `direction: "back"` — previous page in history.
- `direction: "forward"` — next page in history.

In case of multiple redirects, the navigation will resolve with the response of the last redirect.
If cannot go back/forward, returns empty response.

By default (includeSnapshot: true), an ARIA snapshot with refs is returned. Use `snapshotOptions` for `interactiveOnly` (default false) and `cursorInteractive` (default false), same as a11y_take-aria-snapshot.

When `includeScreenshot: true`, the screenshot is always saved to disk; `screenshotFilePath` is returned. By default `outputPath` is the OS temp dir and `name` is "screenshot" (same as content_take-screenshot). Use `screenshotOptions.includeBase64: true` only when the file cannot be read from the returned path (e.g. remote, container).

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle: when the main frame reaches this state. With waitForNavigation, `load` is awaited within its 5 s settle.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation, then up to 5 s for `load` and the page's own requests (its domain; not ads, trackers or streams) before snapshot/screenshot.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for navigation and network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

cursorInteractive.description: Include cursor:pointer / onclick elements. Default false.

snapshotOptions.description: Options when includeSnapshot is true. Same as <a11y_take-aria-snapshot>.

includeScreenshot.description: Take a screenshot after navigation; saved to disk (default: OS temp dir). Use includeBase64 only when file cannot be read from path.

outputPath.description: Directory to save the screenshot. Default: OS temp dir.

name.description: Base name for the screenshot file. Default: "screenshot".

fullPage.description: Capture full scrollable page. Default: true.

annotate.description: Overlay ARIA ref labels on the screenshot. Default: true.

includeBase64.description: Include base64 image in response; use only when file cannot be read from path (e.g. remote, container).

screenshotOptions.description: Options when includeScreenshot is true. Same semantics as <content_take-screenshot> (outputPath/name default to tmp and "screenshot").

status.description: Contains the status code of the navigated page (e.g., 200 for a success).

statusText.description: Contains the status text of the navigated page (e.g. usually an "OK" for a success).

data.description: Base64-encoded image data.

image.description: When includeScreenshot and screenshotOptions.includeBase64 are true: image sent as separate image content part.

definition.name: navigation_go-to
definition.description:
Navigates to the given URL.
**NOTE**: The tool either throws an error or returns a main resource response. 
The only exceptions are navigation to `about:blank` or navigation to the same URL with a different hash, 
which would succeed and return empty response.

**By default** (`includeSnapshot: true`), an ARIA snapshot with refs is taken after navigation and returned in `output` and `refs`; you can use refs (e1, e2, ...) in interaction tools without calling a11y_take-aria-snapshot separately. Use `snapshotOptions` for `interactiveOnly` (default false) and `cursorInteractive` (default false). Set `includeSnapshot: false` to get only url/status/ok.

When `includeScreenshot: true`, the screenshot is always saved to disk; `screenshotFilePath` is returned. By default `outputPath` is the OS temp dir and `name` is "screenshot" (same as content_take-screenshot). Use `screenshotOptions.includeBase64: true` only when the file cannot be read from the returned path (e.g. remote, container).

timeout.description: Max wait ms. 0=no timeout.

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle: when the main frame reaches this state. With waitForNavigation, `load` is awaited within its 5 s settle.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation, then up to 5 s for `load` and the page's own requests (its domain; not ads, trackers or streams) before snapshot/screenshot.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for navigation and network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

includeSnapshot.description: Return ARIA snapshot with refs after nav.

interactiveOnly.description: Only interactive elements get refs. Default false (content roles like headings also included).

cursorInteractive.description: Include cursor:pointer / onclick elements. Default false.

snapshotOptions.description: Options when includeSnapshot is true. Same as <a11y_take-aria-snapshot>.

includeScreenshot.description: Take a screenshot after navigation; saved to disk (default: OS temp dir). Use includeBase64 only when file cannot be read from path.

outputPath.description: Directory to save the screenshot. Default: OS temp dir.

name.description: Base name for the screenshot file. Default: "screenshot".

fullPage.description: Capture full scrollable page. Default: true.

annotate.description: Overlay ARIA ref labels on the screenshot. Default: true.

includeBase64.description: Include base64 image in response; use only when file cannot be read from path (e.g. remote, container).

screenshotOptions.description: Options when includeScreenshot is true. Same semantics as <content_take-screenshot> (outputPath/name default to tmp and "screenshot").

url.description: Contains the URL of the navigated page.

status.description: Contains the status code of the navigated page (e.g., 200 for a success).

statusText.description: Contains the status text of the navigated page (e.g. usually an "OK" for a success).

ok.description: Contains a boolean stating whether the navigated page was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.

screenshotFilePath.description: When includeScreenshot is true: full path of the saved screenshot file.

output.description: When includeSnapshot is true: page URL, title, and ARIA tree with refs.

refs.description: When includeSnapshot is true: map of ref id (e1, e2, ...) to role/name/selector for use in interaction tools.

definition.name: navigation_reload
definition.description:
Reloads the current page.
In case of multiple redirects, the navigation resolves with the response of the last redirect.
If the reload does not produce a response, returns empty response.

By default (includeSnapshot: true), an ARIA snapshot with refs is returned. Use `snapshotOptions` for `interactiveOnly` (default false) and `cursorInteractive` (default false), same as a11y_take-aria-snapshot.

When `includeScreenshot: true`, the screenshot is saved to disk; `screenshotFilePath` is returned. Default path/name: OS temp dir and "screenshot" (same as content_take-screenshot). Use `screenshotOptions.includeBase64: true` only when the file cannot be read from the path.

timeout.description: Max wait ms.

waitUntil.description: Playwright navigation lifecycle: when the main frame reaches this state. With waitForNavigation, `load` is awaited within its 5 s settle.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for reload, then up to 5 s for `load` and the page's own requests (its domain; not ads, trackers or streams) before snapshot/screenshot.

waitForTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for reload and network idle wait (ms). Only when waitForNavigation is true. Default 30000.

interactiveOnly.description: Only interactive elements get refs. Default false (content roles like headings also included).

cursorInteractive.description: Include cursor:pointer / onclick elements. Default false.

snapshotOptions.description: Options when includeSnapshot is true. Same as <a11y_take-aria-snapshot>.

includeScreenshot.description: Take a screenshot after reload; saved to disk (default: OS temp dir).

outputPath.description: Directory to save the screenshot. Default: OS temp dir.

name.description: Base name for the screenshot file. Default: "screenshot".

fullPage.description: Capture full scrollable page. Default: true.

annotate.description: Overlay ARIA ref labels on the screenshot. Default: true.

includeBase64.description: Include base64 image in response; use only when file cannot be read from path (e.g. remote, container).

screenshotOptions.description: Options when includeScreenshot is true. Same semantics as <content_take-screenshot> (outputPath/name default to tmp and "screenshot").

url.description: Contains the URL of the reloaded page.

status.description: Contains the status code of the reloaded page (e.g., 200 for a success).

statusText.description: Contains the status text of the reloaded page (e.g. usually an "OK" for a success).

ok.description: Contains a boolean stating whether the reloaded page was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.

screenshotFilePath.description: When includeScreenshot is true: full path of the saved screenshot file.

data.description: Base64-encoded image data.

image.description: When includeScreenshot and screenshotOptions.includeBase64 are true: image sent as separate image content part.

definition.name: o11y_get-console-messages
definition.description: Retrieves console messages/logs from the browser with filtering options.

type.description: Filter by level (this level or higher).

search.description: Filter by message text.

timestamp.description: Only messages at or after this Unix ms.

sequenceNumber.description: Incremental: only messages with sequence > this.

from.description: Keep from start or end when truncating.

text.description: Text of the console message.

url.description: URL of the resource.

location.description: Location of the console message in the resource.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch timestamp (in milliseconds) of the console message.

sequenceNumber.description:
A monotonically increasing sequence number assigned to each console message.
It reflects the order in which messages were captured and can be used by clients
to retrieve messages incrementally by requesting only those with a higher sequence
number than the last one received.

definition.name: o11y_get-http-requests
definition.description: Retrieves HTTP requests from the browser with filtering options.

status.description: HTTP status range.

timestamp.description: Only requests at or after this Unix ms.

sequenceNumber.description: Incremental: only requests with sequence > this.

from.description: Keep from start or end when truncating.

includeRequestHeaders.description: Include request headers in each item. Default false.

includeResponseHeaders.description: Include response headers in each item. Default false.

includeResponseBody.description: Include response body in each item. Default false.

url.description: HTTP request url.

method.description: HTTP request method. Valid values are: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,HEAD,OPTIONS

headers.description: HTTP request headers as key-value pairs. Present when includeRequestHeaders was true.

body.description: HTTP request body if available. Secret JSON keys are redacted; truncated to BROWSER_HTTP_CAPTURE_BODY_MAX_BYTES.

resourceType.description:
HTTP request resource type as it was perceived by the rendering engine. 
Valid values are: document,stylesheet,image,media,font,script,texttrack,xhr,fetch,eventsource,websocket,manifest,other

failure.description: Error message of the HTTP request if failed.

duration.description: HTTP request duration in milliseconds. "-1" if not available (no response).

status.description: HTTP response status code.

headers.description: HTTP response headers. Present when includeResponseHeaders was true.

body.description: HTTP response body if available. Present when includeResponseBody was true. Secret JSON keys are redacted; truncated to BROWSER_HTTP_CAPTURE_BODY_MAX_BYTES.

ok.description:
Flag to represent whether the HTTP request successful or failed. 
An HTTP request is considered successful only if its status code is 2XX.
Otherwise (non-2XX status code or no response at all because of timeout, network failure, etc ...) it is considered as failed.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch timestamp (in milliseconds) of the HTTP request.

sequenceNumber.description:
A monotonically increasing sequence number assigned to each HTTP request.
It reflects the order in which requests were captured and can be used by clients
to retrieve requests incrementally by requesting only those with a higher sequence
number than the last one received.

definition.name: o11y_get-session-logs
definition.description:
Reads every log record recorded under an IronBee session back from the platform — across all its
traces — optionally narrowed to one activity and then one verification. Ids default to the current
session / activity / verification, so the usual call takes no arguments. Use <o11y_get-trace-logs>
for a single correlated request, <o11y_get-session-traces> for the spans of the same scope.

sessionId.description: Session id (UUID). Defaults to the current session.

activityId.description: Narrow to one activity of that session.

verificationId.description: Narrow further to one verification — requires `activityId`.

detail.description: summary: time/severity/body/service (+ spanId when present). attributes: + the record attributes (log.source, console.method, …). full: + resourceAttributes and instrumentationScope.

serviceName.description: Keep records whose service name contains this (case-insensitive).

minSeverityNumber.description: Keep records at or above this OTLP severity (9=INFO, 13=WARN, 17=ERROR).

bodyContains.description: Keep records whose body contains this (case-insensitive).

waitMs.description: Keep polling (1s interval) for up to this long while nothing is found — records are ingested asynchronously. Max 120000.

count.description: Records returned. 0 with hasMore=false means nothing matched (records not ingested yet read the same way).

hasMore.description: More records exist past this page.

nextOffset.description: `offset` for the next page; present only when hasMore.

errorCount.description: Records at ERROR severity or above (>= 17).

definition.name: o11y_get-session-traces
definition.description:
Reads every span recorded under an IronBee session back from the platform — across all its traces —
optionally narrowed to one activity and then one verification. Ids default to the current session /
activity / verification, so the usual call takes no arguments. Use <o11y_get-trace> for a single
correlated request instead.

sessionId.description: Session id (UUID). Defaults to the current session.

activityId.description: Narrow to one activity of that session.

verificationId.description: Narrow further to one verification — requires `activityId`.

detail.description: summary: identity/timing/status (+ traceState/links when present). attributes: + the span attributes, status message, events. full: + resourceAttributes and instrumentationScope.

serviceName.description: Keep spans whose service name contains this (case-insensitive).

status.description: error: keep only failed spans.

minDurationMs.description: Keep spans at least this long.

waitMs.description: Keep polling (1s interval) for up to this long while nothing is found — spans are ingested asynchronously. Max 120000.

count.description: Spans returned. 0 with hasMore=false means nothing matched (a trace that has not been ingested yet reads the same way).

hasMore.description: More spans exist past this page.

nextOffset.description: `offset` for the next page; present only when hasMore.

spans.description: Ordered by start time. Flat by design — a filtered/paged page is missing parents, so nesting it would invent roots; use `parentSpanId` to rebuild the tree.

definition.name: o11y_get-trace
definition.description:
Reads one distributed trace back from the IronBee platform: every span every service recorded under
`traceId`, as a waterfall tree. Defaults to the trace this call is already correlated to, then to the
one pinned by <o11y_new-trace-id> / <o11y_set-trace-context> — so the usual flow is pin -> drive the app
-> call this with no arguments.
Spans are ingested asynchronously; use `waitMs` right after an action.

traceId.description: 32-hex trace id. Defaults to the correlated trace, then the session pin.

detail.description: summary: identity/timing/status (+ traceState/links when present). attributes: + the span attributes, status message, events. full: + resourceAttributes and instrumentationScope.

serviceName.description: Keep spans whose service name contains this (case-insensitive).

status.description: error: keep only failed spans.

minDurationMs.description: Keep spans at least this long.

waitMs.description: Keep polling (1s interval) for up to this long while nothing is found — spans are ingested asynchronously. Max 120000.

count.description: Spans returned. 0 with hasMore=false means nothing matched (a trace that has not been ingested yet reads the same way).

hasMore.description: More spans exist past this page.

nextOffset.description: `offset` for the next page; present only when hasMore.

spans.description: Ordered by start time. Flat by design — a filtered/paged page is missing parents, so nesting it would invent roots; use `parentSpanId` to rebuild the tree.

definition.name: o11y_get-trace-context
definition.description:
Returns the session's currently pinned W3C trace context: the pinned `traceId` / `traceState` (each
present only when set — a trace is pinned iff at least one is returned). Pin one with <o11y_new-trace-id>
or <o11y_set-trace-context>.

traceId.description: Pinned W3C trace id, when set.

definition.name: o11y_get-trace-logs
definition.description:
Reads the log records of one distributed trace back from the IronBee platform: browser console output
and app logs recorded under `traceId`. Defaults to the trace this call is already correlated to, then
to the pinned one — the usual call takes no arguments. Use <o11y_get-trace> for the spans of the same
trace. Records are ingested asynchronously; use `waitMs` right after an action.

traceId.description: 32-hex trace id. Defaults to the correlated trace, then the session pin.

detail.description: summary: time/severity/body/service (+ spanId when present). attributes: + the record attributes (log.source, console.method, …). full: + resourceAttributes and instrumentationScope.

serviceName.description: Keep records whose service name contains this (case-insensitive).

minSeverityNumber.description: Keep records at or above this OTLP severity (9=INFO, 13=WARN, 17=ERROR).

bodyContains.description: Keep records whose body contains this (case-insensitive).

waitMs.description: Keep polling (1s interval) for up to this long while nothing is found — records are ingested asynchronously. Max 120000.

count.description: Records returned. 0 with hasMore=false means nothing matched (records not ingested yet read the same way).

hasMore.description: More records exist past this page.

nextOffset.description: `offset` for the next page; present only when hasMore.

errorCount.description: Records at ERROR severity or above (>= 17).

definition.name: o11y_get-web-vitals
definition.description:
Collects Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB, FCP) with Google thresholds and recommendations.
Call after navigation or user actions; use waitMs for more stable LCP/CLS/INP.
Some metrics may be unavailable depending on browser and interactions.

waitMs.description: Ms to wait before reading (e.g. let LCP settle).

includeDebug.description: Include entry counts and LCP element hint.

url.description: Current page URL.

timestampMs.description: Unix epoch timestamp (ms) when the metrics were captured.

inpMs.description: Interaction to Next Paint in milliseconds (best-effort approximation).

ttfbMs.description: Time to First Byte in milliseconds.

coreWebVitalsPassed.description: True if all Core Web Vitals are rated "good".

recommendations.description: Recommendations based on the measured values and their ratings.

notes.description: Notes about metric availability, browser limitations, and interpretation.

waitMs.description: Actual wait duration used before reading metrics.

entries.description: Counts of PerformanceEntry types used to compute metrics.

lastLcpSelectorHint.description: Best-effort selector hint for the last LCP element (if available).

lastLcpTagName.description: Tag name of the last LCP element (if available).

definition.name: o11y_new-trace-id
definition.description:
Generates a fresh W3C / OpenTelemetry-compatible trace id (32 hex chars) and pins it on the session so
subsequent calls share one correlation root — the platform propagates it into outgoing requests. Use
<o11y_set-trace-context> to pin a specific id / tracestate, or <o11y_get-trace-context> to inspect the
current pin.

traceId.description: The newly generated, now-pinned 32-hex W3C trace id.

definition.name: o11y_set-trace-context
definition.description:
Sets or clears the session-pinned W3C trace context. Two independent slots:

  - `traceId`: hex string up to 32 chars (short ids are zero-padded by the platform). Empty string clears
    the pinned trace id. Must not be all-zero.
  - `traceState`: opaque W3C `tracestate` value (comma-separated key=value list). Empty string clears.

At least one of `traceId` / `traceState` must be supplied; omitted fields are left untouched. Use
<o11y_new-trace-id> to generate one, or <o11y_get-trace-context> to inspect the current pin.

traceId.description: Hex string up to 32 chars to pin, or empty string to clear. Omit to leave unchanged.

traceState.description: W3C tracestate value to pin, or empty string to clear. Omit to leave unchanged.

traceId.description: The resulting pinned trace id (post-set), if any.

traceState.description: The resulting pinned tracestate (post-set), if any.

definition.name: react_get-component-for-element
definition.description:
