Finds React component(s) for a DOM element via React Fiber (best-effort). Give selector or (x,y); we resolve the element,
find __reactFiber$ on it or ancestors, then build the component stack from the host fiber that owns that node.
Fiber is not a public API—results vary by dev/prod build; names can be displayName, wrappers, or minified.
wrappersDetected/wrapperFrames help with memo/forwardRef/context. If hostMapping.strategy is ancestor-fallback,
use a more specific selector or deeper node for better accuracy.

selector.description: Target element; takes precedence over x/y.

x.description: Viewport X when selector omitted.

y.description: Viewport Y when selector omitted.

includePropsPreview.description: If true, includes a best-effort, truncated props preview for the nearest component.

maxPropsPreviewChars.description: Maximum characters for props preview (after safe stringification).

fiberOnTargetElement.description: Whether the initial fiber pointer was found directly on the target element.

anchorDomHint.description: DOM hint of the element where fiber pointer was found (target or ancestor).

targetDomHint.description: DOM hint of the actual target element.

hostFiberMatchedTarget.description: Whether we found the exact host fiber for target element (fiber.stateNode === targetEl) via subtree scan.

subtreeScanNodesScanned.description: Number of fiber nodes scanned during subtree search.

subtreeScanMaxNodes.description: Maximum fiber nodes allowed to scan (safety cap).

strategy.description: Mapping strategy used to produce the final stack.

definition.name: react_get-element-for-component
definition.description:
Maps a React component instance to the DOM elements it renders (DOM footprint) by traversing the Fiber graph.
Prefer an anchor (anchorSelector or anchorX/anchorY) to target the instance; optionally add a query
(componentName, fileNameHint, lineNumber) to search Fiber. With both, we rank candidates and pick the best match near the anchor.
React DevTools hook gives reliable root discovery (getFiberRoots); without it we fall back to DOM scan for __reactFiber$ (best-effort).
For more reliable roots in a persistent browser, install the React Developer Tools Chrome extension.
Debug source is best-effort and may be missing in some builds.

fiberDetected.description: True if DOM appears to contain React Fiber pointers (__reactFiber$...).

definition.name: scenario-add
definition.description:
Adds a new scenario. A scenario is a reusable JS script (like execute) that can call tools via callTool().
Scenarios are stored on disk as one file per scenario (project-level by default, or global with scope="global").
Optionally declare a params contract (name + optional description/type/default/example/required): the script reads each param via the args binding, defaults are applied when a run omits the arg, and declared types are shallow-validated by <scenario-run>. Without params, args stays fully opaque.
An optional free-form metadata object is persisted and returned verbatim (devtools never interprets it).
The store also stamps createdAt / updatedAt timestamps automatically.

name.description: Unique scenario name (used as key).

description.description: Description of what this scenario does.

script.description: Legacy single-script form. Same sandbox as <execute>: use await callTool(name, input, returnOutput?). Omit when providing `steps`.

name.description: REQUIRED and unique among siblings — a group exists to be named, and its name is what a reader sees in the path.
Optional stable, unique name (else the index).

code.description: Sandbox JS: callTool/console/sleep/args/ctx/assert available.

tool.description: Bare tool name, exactly what callTool takes (e.g. bdt_navigation_go-to). Never templated.

input.description: Tool input. Values may carry {{args.<path>}} / {{ctx.<path>}} references, resolved at run time: a whole-value reference preserves type, an embedded one stringifies, an unresolved one fails the step.

assignTo.description: When set, the tool's output is stored at ctx[assignTo]. Without it the output is not kept (outputs are routinely tens of KB).

name.description: Optional stable, unique name (else the index).

command.description: Host shell command (build/migrate/seed).

allowNonZeroExit.description: When true a non-zero exit does not fail the step.

name.description: Required stable name — its cache is keyed by it (unique within the scenario).

intent.description: Natural-language intent handed to the agent.

name.description: Optional stable, unique name (else the index).

ref.description: Scenario name to include (project→global).

args.description: Args for the ref's params — literal or `{{args.x}}` from parent args.

as.description: Optional ctx namespace: the part's ctx roots at ctx[as].

steps.description: Ordered steps (script/command/llm-action/include). Each llm-action needs a unique name.

body.description: The scenario itself — the steps that run between `setup` and `teardown`. When present this is the authoritative run form and the legacy `script` field is ignored. On update, a provided body replaces the stored one wholesale; omit to keep it.

requiredPlatforms.description: Platforms this scenario needs to run at all (browser / backend / node / python / android / terminal). Checked BEFORE any step — including setup — so a scenario that cannot work on this server says so up front instead of failing mid-run with "tool not found". Declare every platform any phase touches; an included scenario's requirements are unioned in automatically.

steps.description: Ordered script/tool-call/command steps. llm-action and include are not allowed here.

whenReused.description: Whether this section runs when the scenario is REUSED (included, or invoked by a nested scenario-run). Default "skip" — two scenarios that both want the app up would otherwise start it twice. Ignored on the entry scenario.

setup.description: Steps run BEFORE the body to establish what the scenario needs (app up, fixture seeded). Requires `steps`. Background a long-running process with its output REDIRECTED (`npm start > app.log 2>&1 &`) — an inherited stdout pipe keeps the step open until it times out.

teardown.description: Steps run AFTER the body however it ended, to undo what the run created. Does not fail fast: every step runs even if an earlier one failed, and a failure here is reported without changing the run verdict.

formatVersion.description: Step-schema version (forward-compat guard). A value beyond what this build supports is rejected on write.

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

params.description: Optional declared parameter contract. Each entry: name (the arg key) plus optional description/type/default/example/required. Defaults are applied when the caller omits an arg; a required param with no value and no default rejects the run; object/array are shallow-validated (kind only). On update, a provided array replaces the stored one wholesale; omit to keep the existing params. Declaring params is opt-in — a scenario with no params keeps fully-opaque args passthrough.

metadata.description: Opaque free-form metadata, persisted and returned verbatim (devtools never interprets it). On update it is applied as a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) — send ONLY the keys that change: objects merge recursively, a null value DELETES that key, an array or scalar replaces it, and any key you omit is left untouched. So you never need to read-then-resend the whole object, and you cannot accidentally drop keys another writer owns (this field is shared space).

scope.description: Storage scope (default: project).

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

definition.name: scenario-delete
definition.description: Deletes a scenario by name.

name.description: Name of the scenario to delete.

scope.description: Storage scope (default: project).

deleted.description: Whether the scenario was found and deleted.

definition.name: scenario-list
definition.description:
Lists scenarios. When scope is omitted, returns scenarios from both project and global scopes (project overrides global for same name).
Optionally filter by metadataMatch: a subset/containment filter over the opaque metadata (a partial template the stored metadata must contain). Objects match recursively (extra sibling keys are ignored), arrays require the stored array to contain all listed elements, a scalar against a stored array uses membership, and scalars use equality. Keys are never interpreted (devtools-agnostic). Use this to find scenarios by what they cover, e.g. metadataMatch={"ironbee":{"coveredPaths":["src/auth/login.ts"]}}.

scope.description: Filter by scope. Omit to list from both (project overrides global).

metadataMatch.description: Subset/containment filter over the opaque metadata — a partial template the stored metadata must contain. Objects match recursively (a query key must exist; extra sibling keys are ignored), so { "ironbee": { "coveredPaths": ["src/auth/login.ts"] } } matches metadata that also has other ironbee.* keys. Arrays require the stored array to contain all listed elements; a scalar against a stored array uses membership; scalars use equality. All top-level keys must match (AND); keys are never interpreted. Omit for no filter.

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

definition.name: scenario-recorded-actions
definition.description:
Returns the platform tool calls recorded since the current <scenario-run> llm-action pause began ([{seq,toolName,input}], _metadata stripped).
Use it while resolving an llm-action to reconstruct a clean, deterministic cache script (drop exploration/failed attempts, keep order). Empty when no llm-action pause is active. Only platform calls are recorded — scenario-* / execute / this tool are excluded.

name.description: Optional scenario name (advisory).

definition.name: scenario-run
definition.description:
Runs a saved scenario by name (project scope first, then global).

A scenario is either a single legacy JS script or an ordered list of steps
(script / command / llm-action / include). Script steps run in the same sandbox as
execute (callTool/console/sleep/args), share a mutable ctx object, and can use
an assert binding for mechanical checks. command steps run a host shell command.
include steps expand another scenario inline. An llm-action step is a natural-language
intent the agent resolves: the run PAUSES (status:'paused', with pendingStep + ctxSnapshot),
the agent performs the intent with its own tools, then calls scenario-run again with
resume:true (+ resumeOutput / cache) to continue. Once resolved, the realization is
cached in a sibling <name>.cache.json and future runs replay it without pausing (warm);
a broken cache self-heals by pausing again.

Pass args to parameterize the run; declared params are validated. stepByStep pauses
after every step; refresh ignores cache; persistCache:false skips writing the cache.
Scenarios can compose others via callTool('scenario-run', ...) (no pausing when nested;
an unresolved llm-action there is a hard error). Max recursion depth: 5.

name.description: Name of the scenario to run.

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock timeout in ms (default: 30000).

args.description: Parameterization exposed to script steps as `args`. Validated against the scenario's declared params. Latched at fresh-run start; ignored on resume.

param.description: CLI ergonomics: repeatable key=value pairs (the --param flag), coerced to declared param types and merged over `args`.

resume.description: Resume this scenario's paused run in this session (continues from the pending step).

resumeOutput.description: The completed llm-action's output — merged into ctx (plain object, or a JSON-object string, → shallow merge; anything else → ctx._resume).

cache.description: Freeze the just-resolved llm-action's realization script into the sibling cache file.

refresh.description: Ignore cache: true → all llm-actions; [name,…] → matching source names.

persistCache.description: Write the authored cache to disk (default true).

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

name.description: Tool name (every nested call, in execution order).

startTime.description: Epoch ms when the call started.

endTime.description: Epoch ms when the call settled.

duration.description: endTime - startTime (ms).

stepId.description: Execution id of the scenario STEP this call ran inside, when a scenario-run threaded it via _metadata.stepId. Lets a consumer correlate an internal call to its step.

output.description: Tool output — present only when callTool used returnOutput=true.

children.description: Composite calls (scenario-run) expose the inner run's toolCalls here, recursively.

toolCalls.description: Nested calls made by script/warm-cache steps in THIS response (ordered).

stepEvents.description: Per-call step-timeline delta (step_start/step_end transitions since the last response), replayed by ironbee-cli. Each lifecycle phase's steps hang under a synthetic phase ROOT span named <setup> / <main> / <teardown> — the only parentless steps of a run. Top-level step runs only.

activeSteps.description: The absolute open-step stack after this call (outermost → innermost); [] on a terminal run.

runId.description: Per-execution run id (stable across pauses/resumes); read by ironbee-cli to correlate and finalize the run. Top-level step runs only.

teardownErrors.description: Why teardown steps failed, if any did. Separate from `error` on purpose: a failed cleanup does not mean the scenario failed.

recordings.description: Screen recordings captured for this run (file paths). Present only on the terminal response of a recorded run.

definition.name: scenario-search
definition.description:
Full-text search over scenario name + description across both project and global scopes.
Uses configurable search strategy (SEARCH_STRATEGY or SCENARIO_SEARCH_STRATEGY env var).
Returns matching scenarios (including their metadata) ranked by relevance.
Optionally narrow the corpus with metadataMatch (subset/containment over the opaque metadata) before ranking — e.g. text-search only among scenarios that cover a given path. For a pure metadata lookup with no text query, use scenario-list with metadataMatch.

query.description: Search query.

metadataMatch.description: Subset/containment filter over the opaque metadata — a partial template the stored metadata must contain. Objects match recursively (a query key must exist; extra sibling keys are ignored), so { "ironbee": { "coveredPaths": ["src/auth/login.ts"] } } matches metadata that also has other ironbee.* keys. Arrays require the stored array to contain all listed elements; a scalar against a stored array uses membership; scalars use equality. All top-level keys must match (AND); keys are never interpreted. Omit for no filter.

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

definition.name: scenario-update
definition.description:
Updates an existing scenario's description, script, params, and/or metadata.
Write semantics differ between the two, deliberately. params is a wholesale replace: a provided array replaces the stored one (that is how you reorder or drop an entry); omit it to keep the current contract. metadata is a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386): send only the keys that change — objects merge recursively, a null value deletes that key, an array/scalar replaces it, omitted keys survive. Metadata is shared space (IronBee's ironbee.* keys alongside the user's own), so patching is what keeps one writer from silently dropping another's. The store refreshes updatedAt automatically.

name.description: Name of the scenario to update.
REQUIRED and unique among siblings — a group exists to be named, and its name is what a reader sees in the path.
Optional stable, unique name (else the index).

code.description: Sandbox JS: callTool/console/sleep/args/ctx/assert available.

tool.description: Bare tool name, exactly what callTool takes (e.g. bdt_navigation_go-to). Never templated.

input.description: Tool input. Values may carry {{args.<path>}} / {{ctx.<path>}} references, resolved at run time: a whole-value reference preserves type, an embedded one stringifies, an unresolved one fails the step.

assignTo.description: When set, the tool's output is stored at ctx[assignTo]. Without it the output is not kept (outputs are routinely tens of KB).

name.description: Optional stable, unique name (else the index).

command.description: Host shell command (build/migrate/seed).

allowNonZeroExit.description: When true a non-zero exit does not fail the step.

name.description: Required stable name — its cache is keyed by it (unique within the scenario).

intent.description: Natural-language intent handed to the agent.

name.description: Optional stable, unique name (else the index).

ref.description: Scenario name to include (project→global).

args.description: Args for the ref's params — literal or `{{args.x}}` from parent args.

as.description: Optional ctx namespace: the part's ctx roots at ctx[as].

steps.description: Ordered steps (script/command/llm-action/include). Each llm-action needs a unique name.

body.description: The scenario itself — the steps that run between `setup` and `teardown`. When present this is the authoritative run form and the legacy `script` field is ignored. On update, a provided body replaces the stored one wholesale; omit to keep it.

requiredPlatforms.description: Platforms this scenario needs to run at all (browser / backend / node / python / android / terminal). Checked BEFORE any step — including setup — so a scenario that cannot work on this server says so up front instead of failing mid-run with "tool not found". Declare every platform any phase touches; an included scenario's requirements are unioned in automatically.

steps.description: Ordered script/tool-call/command steps. llm-action and include are not allowed here.

whenReused.description: Whether this section runs when the scenario is REUSED (included, or invoked by a nested scenario-run). Default "skip" — two scenarios that both want the app up would otherwise start it twice. Ignored on the entry scenario.

setup.description: Steps run BEFORE the body to establish what the scenario needs (app up, fixture seeded). Requires `steps`. Background a long-running process with its output REDIRECTED (`npm start > app.log 2>&1 &`) — an inherited stdout pipe keeps the step open until it times out.

teardown.description: Steps run AFTER the body however it ended, to undo what the run created. Does not fail fast: every step runs even if an earlier one failed, and a failure here is reported without changing the run verdict.

formatVersion.description: Step-schema version (forward-compat guard). A value beyond what this build supports is rejected on write.

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

params.description: Optional declared parameter contract. Each entry: name (the arg key) plus optional description/type/default/example/required. Defaults are applied when the caller omits an arg; a required param with no value and no default rejects the run; object/array are shallow-validated (kind only). On update, a provided array replaces the stored one wholesale; omit to keep the existing params. Declaring params is opt-in — a scenario with no params keeps fully-opaque args passthrough.

metadata.description: Opaque free-form metadata, persisted and returned verbatim (devtools never interprets it). On update it is applied as a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) — send ONLY the keys that change: objects merge recursively, a null value DELETES that key, an array or scalar replaces it, and any key you omit is left untouched. So you never need to read-then-resend the whole object, and you cannot accidentally drop keys another writer owns (this field is shared space).

scope.description: Storage scope (default: project).

name.description: Arg key read inside the script.

type.description: Declared kind (string/number/boolean/object/array). Absent → no type check. object/array are shallow-validated (top-level kind only).

default.description: Applied when the caller omits this arg; for object/array it also doubles as the concrete shape example.

required.description: Reject the run when no value and no default. Default false.

definition.name: secrets_list
definition.description:
Lists the secrets this run was given — name, what each is for, and the {{secret:NAME.FIELD}}
reference to write into a tool input in place of the value. Never returns a value.

boundOrigins.description: Hosts it may be used on.

usableIn.description: Tools a reference to it may be written into.

secrets.description: Empty when the run has no secrets.

definition.name: stub_clear
definition.description:
Clears stubs installed.

- If stubId is provided, clears only that stub.
- If stubId is omitted, clears all stubs for the current session/context.

stubId.description: Remove this stub; omit to clear all.

definition.name: stub_intercept-http-request
definition.description:
Installs a request interceptor stub that can modify outgoing requests before they are sent.

Use cases:
- A/B testing / feature flags (inject headers)
- Security testing (inject malformed headers / payload)
- Edge cases (special characters, large payload)
- Auth simulation (add API keys / tokens in headers)

Notes:
- pattern is a glob matched against the full request URL (picomatch).
- This modifies requests; it does not change responses.
- times limits how many times the interceptor applies (-1 means infinite).

modifications.description: Changes to apply to the request.

stubId.description: Unique id of the installed stub.

kind.description: Stub kind.

enabled.description: Whether the stub is enabled.

definition.name: stub_list
definition.description:
Lists currently installed stubs for the active browser context/session.
Useful to debug why certain calls are being mocked/intercepted.

id.description: Stub id.

kind.description: Stub kind.

enabled.description: Whether stub is enabled.

usedCount.description: How many times it has been applied.

action.description: For mock_response: fulfill/abort.

status.description: For mock_response: HTTP status (if set).

definition.name: stub_mock-http-response
definition.description:
Installs a response stub for matching requests using glob patterns (picomatch).

Use cases:
- Offline testing (return 200 with local JSON)
- Error scenarios (force 500/404 or abort with timedout)
- Edge cases (empty data / huge payload / special characters)
- Flaky API testing (chance < 1.0)
- Performance testing (delayMs)

Notes:
- pattern is a glob matched against the full request URL.
- stubs are evaluated in insertion order; first match wins.
- times limits how many times the stub applies (-1 means infinite).

stubId.description: Unique id of the installed stub (use it to clear later).

kind.description: Stub kind.

enabled.description: Whether the stub is enabled.

action.description: Applied action.

status.description: HTTP status (present when action=fulfill).

definition.name: sync_wait-for-network-idle
definition.description:
Waits until the page is network-idle: in-flight requests <= maxConnections for at least idleTimeMs (server-side tracking, no page globals).
Use before SPAs, screenshots, or AX snapshots for stable results. With long-polling, increase maxConnections or use shorter idleTimeMs.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait ms before failing.

idleTimeMs.description: Network must stay idle for this many ms to resolve.

waitedMs.description: Total time waited until the network became idle or the tool timed out (milliseconds).

timeoutMs.description: Maximum allowed wait time (milliseconds).

maxConnections.description: Idle threshold used: in-flight requests must be <= this value.

pollIntervalMs.description: Polling interval used to sample the in-flight request count (milliseconds).

finalInFlightRequests.description: The last observed number of in-flight requests at the moment the tool returned.

observedIdleMs.description: How long the in-flight request count stayed <= maxConnections right before returning (milliseconds).

prompts.name: default_system
prompts.title: Default System Prompt
prompts.description: General behavior for the AI assistant

server_info.name: mcp-graphql-enhanced
server_info.description: Federated GraphQL-to-MCP bridge with broadcast introspection and full type visibility.

definition.name: introspect-schema
definition.description: Retrieve GraphQL schema details or system manifest. READ-ONLY: Non-destructive metadata discovery. Usage: 1. If 'typeNames' is provided: Returns the full SDL (Schema Definition Language) for the requested types, including fields and relations. 2. If 'typeNames' is omitted: Returns a Federated Manifest—a high-level summary of connected nodes, their capabilities, and available domain entities (not the full schema). Use this to navigate the federated graph topology before executing queries.

typeNames.description: List of specific GraphQL type names to introspect. If provided, returns the detailed SDL definitions for these types. If omitted, returns a system-wide Federated Manifest overview.

typeDepth.description: Depth of nested fields to retrieve (default: 2)

endpoint.description: Optional target GraphQL HTTP/HTTPS URL to dynamically switch endpoint before execution.

headers.description: JSON stringified object of extra HTTP headers for the introspection request (e.g. '{"Authorization": "Bearer token"}').

definition.name: query-graphql
definition.description: Execute GraphQL operations (queries and mutations) against the federated system. WARNING: This tool performs remote operations. 'Mutation' operations will modify persistent state; execute these only when a state change is intended. Prerequisites: Verify schema structure using 'introspect-schema' before executing complex queries. Security: Inherits environment-based authentication. Returns: A JSON object containing the execution result ('data') or a list of 'errors' in case of failure.

query.description: The GraphQL query or mutation string. Example: 'query { guilds { id name } }'.

variables.description: JSON stringified object of variables. Example: '{"id": "123"}'.

headers.description: JSON stringified object of extra HTTP headers for the request.

endpoint.description: Optional target GraphQL HTTP/HTTPS URL to dynamically switch endpoint before execution.

prompts.name: system-health
prompts.description: Check status of all nodes

definition.name: meshy_analyze_printability
definition.title: Analyze Model Printability
definition.description:
Check whether a model is printable: watertightness, non-manifold edges, holes, degenerate faces and volume — plus thin walls when printer_type and/or a print size is given (FDM, SLA/resin or full-color). FREE. This is the authoritative answer to "is it printable?".

The finished task (task_type "print-analyze") reports printability.status:
  - error → meshy_repair_printability (pass this analyze task as input_task_id to reuse its printer and size)
  - warning → repair is optional
  - healthy → download the analyzed source task's model (the analyze task has none)

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", printer_type: "sla", intended_print_height_mm: 100 }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, remesh or retexture task on Meshy 6 or newer, or a print-repair task. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

printer_type.description: Sets the minimum wall: fdm 1.0 mm, sla 0.8 mm, full_color 2.0 mm (fdm when only a size is sent). Without a size: 150 mm tall for GLB / tasks, an STL's own size, else 150 mm longest side.

intended_print_height_mm.description: Print height in mm (1–1000); GLB / input_task_id only. At most one print size.

intended_print_longest_side_mm.description: Print's longest side in mm (1–1000); any format. At most one print size.

definition.name: meshy_animate
definition.title: Animate Rigged 3D Character

action_id.description: One preset action; find ids with meshy_list_animations (free), never guess.

action_ids.description: 1–10 unique preset ids, returned as ONE file with one clip per action, in this order (e.g. for a game-engine state machine).

motion_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_motion task (biped rigs only; within 3 days, before the clip expires).

definition.name: meshy_auto_split
definition.title: Auto Split Model into Printable Parts
definition.description:
Cut a model into separately printable parts: when it is too big for the bed, parts need different colors/materials, or it should be assembled. Cost: 10 credits. The texture is not kept.

There is no bed-size parameter: cuts follow mode and prompt, not your printer, so resize the model to the print size first (meshy_resize) when parts must fit a bed, then check the part sizes and re-split by_parts if one is still too big.
Then meshy_download_model (3mf if requested) and meshy_send_to_slicer.

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", mode: "by_parts", prompt: "the figure and the base", target_formats: ["3mf"], connectors: true }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-3d preview, remesh, convert or resize task made with meshy-6, meshy-7, meshy-7.1 or latest (not low-poly or Smart Topology).

mode.description: 'auto' (default; Meshy picks the cuts), 'by_parts' (the parts named in prompt), or 'by_color' (the color regions named in prompt; image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d sources only).

prompt.description: Required for by_parts / by_color: name 1–10 parts, e.g. 'head, torso, arms, legs'; the rest becomes one more part. If unreadable, the task falls back to auto, still charges, and reports prompt_ignored.

target_formats.description: Extra formats (glb is always made). 3mf gives separately selectable parts in a slicer; stl fuses them into one solid.

layout.description: 'assembled' (default) or 'on_plate' (parts laid flat, ready to slice).

connectors.description: Add mortise-and-tenon connectors at each cut so the parts fit together.

definition.name: meshy_cancel_task
definition.title: Cancel or Delete Task
definition.description:
Cancel a queued task, or delete a finished one. What happens depends on the task:

Creative Lab tasks (task_type "creative-lab-..."):
  - PENDING → canceled, credits refunded
  - IN_PROGRESS → canceled, credits NOT refunded
  - SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED → cannot be canceled or deleted, even with confirm_delete

Every other task:
  - PENDING → deleted, credits refunded
  - IN_PROGRESS → refused: the task keeps running and its credits are not refundable. Wait until it finishes
  - SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED → PERMANENTLY deleted with its files, no refund. Requires confirm_delete: true — ask the user first

Returns { success, task_id, task_type, previous_status, message }.

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

confirm_delete.description: true to permanently delete a finished task, only after the user agreed.

definition.name: meshy_check_balance
definition.title: Check Credit Balance
definition.description: Check the Meshy credit balance. Free. For team members it is the team's shared pool.

balance.description: Credits available now (usually monthly_credits + permanent_credits; lower when a member or workspace credit limit applies)

monthly_credits.description: Credits that expire at the next monthly refresh

permanent_credits.description: Credits that never expire (credit packs, rewards)

monthly_resets_at.description: Next monthly refresh (ISO 8601); omitted when none is scheduled

definition.name: meshy_convert
definition.title: Convert 3D Model Format
definition.description:
Convert a model to other file formats. Cost: 1 credit (cheaper than remesh for a format-only change).

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", target_formats: ["stl", "3mf"] }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a model. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

definition.name: meshy_creative_lab
definition.title: Creative Lab — Make a Product (end-to-end)
definition.description:
Turn a photo (file_path or image_url; no text prompt) into a finished Creative Lab product 3D model, end to end.

Products and cost — confirm before calling:
  - figure (chibi), vinyl-figure, brick-figure, keychain, fridge-magnet, fidget-pixel (pixel-art board of interlocking pieces) → 36 credits (6 + 30)
  - lamp (3D-printable lampshade with base plate) → 36 (30 + 6)
  - keycap (Cherry MX 1u) → 62 (12 + 50)
  - fidget-collapsible (nested-ring fidget from the photo's outline) → 6, one stage

Most products run a concept prototype, then a 3D build. One call runs both, blocks while they run (typically 2–5 minutes, with progress) and returns only the final model; the concept image is internal and never shown. If the prototype does not succeed, the build is NOT started: a FAILED stage is refunded; one still running when the wait ends keeps running and is charged.

Outputs: GLB (or output_format) for figures, keychain and fridge-magnet; lamp_stl (+ base_stl with a fixture preset); keycap a model; fidget-pixel a 3MF with one object per piece; fidget-collapsible STL + GLB. Download with meshy_download_model and the task_type this tool reports; omit format to save every part.
To multicolor-print it, pass its GLB URL (or a GLB data URI) to meshy_process_multicolor as model_url; its task id is not accepted there.

Examples:
  - { product: "keychain", file_path: "/Users/me/dog.jpg", name_text: "Biscuit", build_options: { badge_shape: "star" } }
  - { product: "fidget-pixel", file_path: "/Users/me/cat.jpg", pixel_subject: "other", build_options: { grid_size: 16 } }

product.description: The product (see the tool description for costs).

image_url.description: Public URL or data URI of the photo (.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp). For local files use file_path.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local photo; the server encodes it.

image_subject.description: Lamp only: what the photo shows.

pixel_subject.description: fidget-pixel only, REQUIRED: 'person' → chibi pixel sprite; 'other' (pets, objects, logos, landscapes) → bead-art icon.

name_text.description: Keychain only: text to engrave, ≤10 characters (CJK count one each).

head_size_mm.description: Keycap only: the head's LONGEST edge in mm (default 23), not its height.

vertical_offset_mm.description: Keycap only: raise (+) or lower (-) the head on the base, in mm (default 0).

build_options.description: Build options (the API checks ranges). Keychain / fridge-magnet: badge_shape (circle|rounded-rect|hexagon|shield|star), size_mm, relief_height_mm, relief_offset_mm, base_thickness_mm, has_closed_back, relief_curve (linear|gamma|s-curve), curve_param, invert_depth, smoothing, relief_scale, depth_threshold, remove_background, export_resolution. Lamp: diameter_mm (50–400), thickness_mm, cut_amount_percent, light_source_preset (bambu_mh001_60mm|none), fixture_offset_x_mm, fixture_offset_z_mm, rotate_x_deg, rotate_y_deg, rotate_z_deg, include_result_json. Fidget pixel: shape (square|hex), grid_size (16|32), piece_size_mm (6|8|10; hex 6|8), color_count (1–8), piece_height_mm (10–80). Other products take none.

output_format.description: Keychain / fridge-magnet: glb (default), obj (zip of OBJ + MTL + texture) or zip (everything). Lamp: stl (default) or zip. Fidget pixel: 3mf. Others: none.

name.description: Display name for the task; not engraved (see name_text).

timeout_seconds.description: Max wait per stage in seconds; a longer stage keeps running (check it with meshy_get_task_status).

definition.name: meshy_download_model
definition.title: Download Model or Image
definition.description:
Save a finished task's output under meshy_output/ (project folders with history), or at save_to.

  - 3D tasks: ONE model format — ask the user which first (GLB viewing, OBJ white-model printing, 3MF multicolor printing, FBX game engines, USDZ AR, BLEND Blender); never download all. A format exists only if it was generated: 3mf needs target_formats ["3mf"] at creation, meshy_convert or meshy_process_multicolor.
  - Creative Lab: omit format to save every part.
  - Images and text-to-motion clips save their own files and ignore format.
  - Rigging and animation tasks are not saved: they return their file URLs.
If a download fails, its URL is returned instead.

Example (print): { task_id: "abc-123", format: "obj", print_ready: true, print_height_mm: 100 }

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

format.description: Model format (default glb; omit for every Creative Lab part).

save_to.description: Absolute file path to save to instead of meshy_output/{timestamp}_{prompt}_{id}/

parent_task_id.description: Earlier task of the same chain (e.g. the preview of a refine); saves into its project folder.

print_ready.description: OBJ only: rotate Y-up to Z-up, scale to print_height_mm, center, bottom at Z=0. Changes only the local file (free); meshy_resize (1 credit) rescales the model on Meshy.

print_height_mm.description: Height in mm with print_ready (default 75; '15 cm' → 150).

definition.name: meshy_get_task_status
definition.title: Get Task Status
definition.description:
Wait for a task to finish (wait=true, default) or check it once (wait=false). Reports the task's real task_type; pass it to the download and cancel tools.

wait=true polls at the API's suggested interval (else 5s→30s backoff) until SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELED or timeout_seconds runs out; a failed status check (timeout, 429, 5xx) is retried at the next poll. Running out of time returns outcome "TIMEOUT": the task keeps running on Meshy — call again with the same task_id (Meshy advises allowing up to 60 minutes from creation).

task_type.description: Optional: if omitted or wrong, the server finds the task and reports its real type.

wait.description: true (default): poll until it finishes; false: return the current status.

timeout_seconds.description: Max wait for this call when wait=true; the task keeps running after it.

outcome.description: Outcome of this call; TIMEOUT means the wait ended, not the task

task_type.description: The task's actual type (pass it as task_type to the download and cancel tools)

printability.description: print-analyze result: status, issue counts, metrics, thin walls

prompt_ignored.description: Auto Split: the prompt was unreadable, so the cuts were chosen automatically

result.description: Rigging, animation and text-to-motion file URLs

consumed_credits.description: Credits consumed by the task (0 for FAILED — credits are refunded on failure)

error_type.description: Failure category if the task failed: invalid_input (fix the input), timeout / service_unavailable / server_error (refunded; create it again)

definition.name: meshy_image_to_3d
definition.title: Generate 3D Model from Image
definition.description:
Generate a 3D model from one image, textured by default (no refine step; should_texture false for a bare mesh). Typically 2–3 minutes.
Cost: meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 20 mesh only, 30 textured, 35 at 8K; meshy-6-lite 5 / 15; meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 5 / 15 / 20 at 8K; Ultra geometry +5.

IMAGE INPUT (exactly ONE):
  - file_path: a local image (RECOMMENDED; never base64-encode it yourself)
  - image_url: a public URL
  - input_task_id: a SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image task with ONE image (multi-view output → meshy_multi_image_to_3d)

Example: { file_path: "/path/to/character.png", pose_mode: "t-pose" }

image_url.description: Public image URL. For local files use file_path.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp; the server encodes it.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-image / image-to-image task with exactly one image, used as the input.

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7.1) or 'meshy-7.1' (best), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, cheap, 2K textures only); 'meshy-7' is deprecated. With model_type smart-topology: 'meshy-t2' (the default there) or 'meshy-t2.5' (newest, sharper detail for game assets); 'meshy-t1' is deprecated.

geometry_resolution.description: Ultra geometry pass: standard (default), 2k or 4k (finest); meshy-7.1/latest with model_type standard only, +5 credits.

model_type.description: standard (default); smart-topology (ai_model meshy-t2 or meshy-t2.5): a clean, part-separated, triangle-only mesh made directly at target_polycount, ignoring remesh/decimation; lowpoly is deprecated (billed like meshy-6, retires 2026-10-30).

pose_mode.description: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'; use 't-pose' when the model will be rigged or animated.

target_polycount.description: Standard: remesh target 100–300,000, needs should_remesh true. Smart Topology: meshy-t2 100–15,000 (default 4,000), meshy-t2.5 100–30,000 (default 15,000).

should_texture.description: Generate textures (default true); false gives a cheaper untextured mesh.

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (+5 credits; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

image_enhancement.description: Optimize the input image (meshy-6/7.1/latest); false keeps deliberate styling.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6 only; API default true there).

save_pre_remeshed_model.description: Also keep the GLB from before remeshing (with should_remesh).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

definition.name: meshy_image_to_image
definition.title: Transform Image using AI
definition.description:
Edit or restyle images with a text prompt. Cost: nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9, GPT Image models 12 credits.
Give exactly ONE reference source: input_task_id (all images of an earlier image task), reference_file_paths (local files; never base64-encode them yourself) or reference_image_urls.

To make the result 3D: meshy_image_to_3d with input_task_id = this task (multi-view output: meshy_multi_image_to_3d).

Example: { ai_model: "nano-banana-2", prompt: "make it red", input_task_id: "abc-123" }

prompt.description: Text description

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-image / image-to-image task; all its images are the references. Wins over the other sources.

reference_file_paths.description: 1–5 absolute paths to local images; the server encodes them

generate_multi_view.description: Front/side/back views (input for meshy_multi_image_to_3d). Not with aspect_ratio.

aspect_ratio.description: Default '1:1'; '3:2' and '2:3' are GPT Image models only. Not with generate_multi_view.

remove_background.description: Transparent-background PNG (no effect on multi-view output).

definition.name: meshy_list_animations
definition.title: Find Animation Actions
definition.description:
Look up preset animations: the action ids meshy_animate takes. Free. Filters combine; with none the whole (long) library comes back, so prefer search or category.

Returns [{ action_id, name, key, category, sub_category, preview_url }]; preview_url is an animated GIF.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of the animation name or key, e.g. 'walk', 'punch', 'dance'.

sub_category.description: Only this sub-category, e.g. 'AttackingwithWeapon'. Names repeat across categories, so pair it with category to be exact.

action_ids.description: Resolve these ids (up to 200); ids that no longer exist are simply absent.

definition.name: meshy_list_models
definition.title: List Finished 3D Models
definition.description: List your finished 3D models (not AI models), newest first, each with its task_id, task_type and formats ready for meshy_download_model. Queries only image-to-3d by default (one request); pass task_types to widen. meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status instead, images included.

task_types.description: Model task types to list (default ["image-to-3d"], one request). Pass several, e.g. ["text-to-3d", "image-to-3d", "multi-image-to-3d"], to widen; each type is one more request.

workspace_id.description: Deprecated; ignored.

filter.description: Deprecated; ignored.

definition.name: meshy_list_tasks
definition.title: List Generation Tasks
definition.description:
List tasks of any status, newest first by default, merged across the types queried (one request per type). Default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image and image-to-image; pass task_type / task_types for printing, rigging, animation, motion, post-processing or Creative Lab tasks. With a task_id in hand, use meshy_get_task_status instead. Tasks created through the API do not appear in the Meshy web app.

status and phase filter the fetched tasks, so a page can be shorter than limit; continue with next_offset while has_more. Types whose request failed are listed in failed_types. For finished 3D models only, meshy_list_models is cheaper.

task_type.description: One task type to list (same names as meshy_get_task_status).

task_types.description: Task types to list, merged with task_type. Default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image.

status.description: Only tasks with this status

definition.name: meshy_list_usage
definition.title: List API Usage Records

start_time.description: RFC 3339 start of the created_at window (default: 30 days before end_time; at most 1 year).

end_time.description: RFC 3339 end of the window (default now).

endpoints.description: Only these endpoints ('text-to-3d' covers preview and refine). Omit for all.

status.description: Only tasks with this final status. Omit for both.

definition.name: meshy_multi_image_to_3d
definition.title: Generate 3D Model from Multiple Images
definition.description:
Generate a 3D model from 1–4 views of the same object (better reconstruction), textured by default.
Cost: meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 20 mesh only, 30 textured, 35 at 8K; meshy-6-lite 5 / 15; Ultra geometry +5.

IMAGE INPUT (exactly ONE):
  - file_paths: 1–4 local images (never base64-encode them yourself)
  - image_urls: 1–4 public URLs
  - input_task_id: a SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image task (multi-view included); its images are the input

Example: { file_paths: ["/path/front.jpg", "/path/side.jpg"] }

file_paths.description: 1–4 absolute paths to local .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp images; the server encodes them.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-image / image-to-image task (multi-view included) whose images are the input.

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7.1) or 'meshy-7.1' (best), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, cheap, 2K textures only); 'meshy-7' is deprecated. No Smart Topology here.

geometry_resolution.description: Ultra geometry pass: standard (default) or 2k (+5 credits); meshy-7.1/latest only. No 4k here.

pose_mode.description: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'; use 't-pose' when the model will be rigged or animated.

model_type.description: Deprecated; ignored (this endpoint has no model_type).

should_texture.description: Generate textures (default true); false gives a cheaper untextured mesh.

texture_image_urls.description: 1–4 views (URLs or data URIs) of the SAME object to drive the texture; element 0 is the front. meshy-7.1/latest only; not with texture_prompt / texture_image_url.

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (+5 credits; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

image_enhancement.description: Optimize the input image (meshy-6/7.1/latest); false keeps deliberate styling.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6/7.1/latest; API default true).

save_pre_remeshed_model.description: Also keep the GLB from before remeshing (with should_remesh).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

definition.name: meshy_process_multicolor
definition.title: Process Multi-Color 3D Print
definition.description:
Turn a textured model into a multi-color 3MF that opens ready to print in the slicer of printer_brand. Cost: 10 credits.

Confirm first: max_colors (the printer's AMS/MMU capacity), style, printer_brand, and max_depth (realistic only).
Download with format "3mf", then open it with meshy_send_to_slicer (is_multicolor). Flashforge, QIDI, Snapmaker and AnkerMake slicers are not detected: give the user the 3MF path for that slicer.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED textured task: image-to-3d / multi-image-to-3d (unless should_texture was false), refined text-to-3d, remesh or retexture. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a textured .glb / .fbx, or a GLB data URI.

max_colors.description: Palette size (1–16); match the printer's AMS/MMU capacity.

max_depth.description: 3–6: higher = finer color boundaries, larger file (realistic only).

style.description: 'realistic' (default): photo-like detail, larger file, needs one base color texture with UVs on every part. 'cartoon': flat regions, smaller file, also takes vertex colors.

printer_brand.description: Brand whose slicer preset (default printer, 0.4 mm nozzle) goes into the 3MF (default bambu).

definition.name: meshy_remesh
definition.title: Remesh 3D Model
definition.description:
Remesh an existing model: change its polygon count or topology. Cost: 5 credits. For a format change only use meshy_convert (1 credit); to scale, meshy_resize (1 credit).

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", topology: "quad", target_polycount: 10000, target_formats: ["fbx"] }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d (preview or refine), image-to-3d or retexture task

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB)

definition.name: meshy_repair_printability
definition.title: Repair Model Topology for 3D Printing
definition.description:
Repair a model for 3D printing (FDM, SLA/resin or full-color): fixes non-manifold edges, degenerate faces and holes and makes it watertight. Cost: 10 credits. Textures are removed (retexture afterwards if needed).

Output format: input_task_id → GLB; model_url → the input's format (.stl → STL, .obj → OBJ…). To keep a Meshy model as OBJ, pass its OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) as model_url.
With printer_type and/or a print size it also thickens walls that are too thin, when over 5% of the surface is. The model keeps its scale (meshy_resize scales it).

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, remesh or retexture task, or a print-analyze task (which passes on its printer and size). Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB).

printer_type.description: Sets the minimum wall: fdm 1.0 mm, sla 0.8 mm, full_color 2.0 mm (fdm when only a size is sent). Without a size: 150 mm tall for GLB / tasks, an STL's own size, else 150 mm longest side.

intended_print_height_mm.description: Print height in mm (1–1000); GLB / input_task_id only. At most one print size.

intended_print_longest_side_mm.description: Print's longest side in mm (1–1000); any format. At most one print size.

definition.name: meshy_resize
definition.title: Resize 3D Model to Real-World Dimensions

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a model (output GLB). Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (output keeps its format), or a GLB data URI.

resize_longest_side.description: Longest side in meters (aspect ratio kept)

definition.name: meshy_retexture
definition.title: Retexture 3D Model
definition.description:
Apply new AI textures to an existing model. Cost: 10 credits (15 at 8K).

Ask the user for EXACTLY ONE style input (the tool rejects combinations):
  - text_style_prompt: the style in words ("rusty metal", "cartoon")
  - image_style_url: one image used as a STYLE reference
  - multiview_image_urls: 1–4 photos OF THE SAME OBJECT from different angles (not style references)

Example: { input_task_id: "abc-123", text_style_prompt: "rusty metal" }

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED text-to-3d (preview or refine), image-to-3d or remesh task

model_url.description: Public URL of a .glb / .gltf / .obj / .fbx / .stl model (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB)

text_style_prompt.description: The texture style in words (max 800 characters).

image_style_url.description: One image used as the style reference.

multiview_image_urls.description: 1–4 ordered views of the same object; element 0 is primary and alone drives metallic/roughness. Needs Meshy 7 ('latest' is sent as 'meshy-7').

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7), 'meshy-7', 'meshy-6', or 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, 2K only). No meshy-7.1 here.

enable_original_uv.description: Keep the existing UVs instead of a fresh unwrap. Default true with input_task_id, false with model_url (safest for uploads).

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (15 credits instead of 10; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6 only; API default true there).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it).

definition.name: meshy_rig
definition.title: Auto-Rig 3D Character
definition.description:
Auto-rig a humanoid character for animation. Cost: 5 credits, including free walking + running animations (GLB + FBX, separate files).

REQUIREMENT: a textured humanoid (biped) model with a clear body and limbs, ≤300,000 faces (checked first; remesh if over). model_url must be a .glb facing +Z. Generate characters with pose_mode "t-pose" for the best rig.

Next steps: meshy_download_model (task_type "rigging") returns the rigged model and walk/run URLs. Other actions: meshy_list_animations → meshy_animate. A described motion: meshy_text_to_motion → meshy_animate with motion_task_id.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a textured humanoid model

model_url.description: Public URL of a textured humanoid .glb (max 400 MB), or a GLB data URI (max 100 MB)

height_meters.description: Character height in meters; helps scaling

texture_image_url.description: Deprecated: leave it out when the model has its own textures (Meshy models and most GLBs do), which the rig keeps. Sending it makes this image the only texture and drops the PBR maps. Only for a model_url GLB without textures: its UV-unwrapped base color (.png, max 20 MB)

definition.name: meshy_send_to_slicer
definition.title: Send Model to 3D Printing Slicer
definition.description:
Detect installed 3D printing slicers and return their launch commands. Call it at the START of a print workflow and keep the result; at the END, replace {file} in a launch_command with the downloaded file's local path and run it. If you cannot run shell commands, give the user the command and the file path.

Detects OrcaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Creality Print, Elegoo Slicer, Anycubic Slicer Next, PrusaSlicer (all multicolor-capable) and UltiMaker Cura.

Several SEPARATE models: open them one at a time, ~2 s apart (`open -a "Bambu Studio" a.stl; sleep 2; open -a "Bambu Studio" b.stl`); fired together, a slicer may take only one. Parts of one model go in one project, opened together.

model_url.description: The model's URL (a placeholder is fine when only detecting)

slicer_type.description: 'auto' (default): detect all and recommend one; or one slicer.

definition.name: meshy_text_to_3d
definition.title: Generate 3D Model from Text

prompt.description: What to model (max 800 characters)

ai_model.description: 'latest' (default, = Meshy 7.1) or 'meshy-7.1' (best), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (fast, cheap, 2K textures only); 'meshy-7' is deprecated. With model_type smart-topology: 'meshy-t2' (the default there) or 'meshy-t2.5' (newest, sharper detail for game assets).

model_type.description: standard (default); smart-topology (ai_model meshy-t2 or meshy-t2.5): a clean, part-separated, triangle-only mesh made directly at target_polycount, ignoring remesh/decimation; lowpoly is deprecated (billed like meshy-6, retires 2026-10-30).

geometry_resolution.description: Ultra geometry pass: standard (default), 2k or 4k (finest); meshy-7.1/latest with model_type standard only, +5 credits.

target_polycount.description: Standard: remesh target 100–300,000, needs should_remesh true. Smart Topology: meshy-t2 100–15,000 (default 4,000), meshy-t2.5 100–30,000 (default 15,000).

pose_mode.description: 'a-pose' or 't-pose'; use 't-pose' when the model will be rigged or animated.

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

definition.name: meshy_text_to_3d_refine
definition.title: Refine Text-to-3D Preview
definition.description:
Texture a SUCCEEDED meshy_text_to_3d preview. Cost: 10 credits (15 at 8K). Get the user's approval first; omit ai_model to inherit the preview's model.

Example: { preview_task_id: "abc-123", texture_prompt: "rusty metal", enable_pbr: true }

preview_task_id.description: The SUCCEEDED preview task to texture

ai_model.description: Optional override: 'meshy-7.1', 'latest' (= 7.1), 'meshy-6', 'meshy-6-lite' (2K only). Omit (recommended) to inherit the preview's model; not meshy-t2/t2.5.

texture_resolution.description: Base color texture: 2k (default), 4k or 8k (+5 credits; PBR maps stay 4K, no emission map). 4k/8k not on meshy-6-lite.

remove_lighting.description: Remove highlights/shadows from the base color (meshy-6 only). Sent as-is when ai_model is omitted, so omit it after a meshy-6-lite preview (the API rejects it).

target_formats.description: Formats to produce (default: all but 3mf; list '3mf' to get it). Fewer formats finish faster.

auto_size.description: AI-estimate the real-world height and resize to it (default false).

definition.name: meshy_text_to_image
definition.title: Generate 2D Image from Text
definition.description:
Generate a 2D image from text, e.g. a design for the user to approve before 3D. Typically ~30 s.
Cost: nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9, GPT Image models 9 credits.

To make it 3D: meshy_image_to_3d with input_task_id = this task (multi-view output: meshy_multi_image_to_3d).

Example: { ai_model: "nano-banana-pro", prompt: "game character", generate_multi_view: true, pose_mode: "t-pose" }

prompt.description: Text description

generate_multi_view.description: Front/side/back views (input for meshy_multi_image_to_3d). Not with aspect_ratio.

aspect_ratio.description: Default '1:1'; '3:2' and '2:3' are GPT Image models only. Not with generate_multi_view.

remove_background.description: Transparent-background PNG (no effect on multi-view output).

definition.name: meshy_text_to_motion
definition.title: Generate Motion Clip from Text

prompt.description: The motion, e.g. 'jumps over a gap and lands in a crouch' (max 400 characters).

duration.description: Clip length in seconds: 2–10 in steps of 0.5.

mode.description: 'prime' (default): highest quality, FBX. 'swift': faster and cheaper, BVH.

definition.name: meshy_uv_unwrap
definition.title: Generate UV Unwrap for a 3D Model
definition.description:
Make a clean, non-overlapping UV layout ("UV white model") before texturing in Blender, Substance Painter or Unreal. Cost: 5 credits.

GLB input only, ≤40,000 faces (denser meshes are rejected: remesh first). The output GLB keeps the geometry (quads/n-gons triangulated) with fresh UVs and a grey placeholder material.

input_task_id.description: A SUCCEEDED task with a GLB. Wins over model_url.

model_url.description: Public URL or data URI of a .glb (convert other formats first).

definition.name: device_app_state
definition.title: App State
definition.description: Get the current state of an app by bundle ID. Returns whether the app is running, installed, or not found.

bundleId.description: App bundle ID (e.g. io.metamask or io.metamask.debug)

definition.name: device_clipboard
definition.title: Clipboard
definition.description: Read or write the device clipboard. Use action=get to read clipboard text, action=set to write. On Android, clipboard access requires the Appium backend.

action.description: Action: get clipboard content or set it

text.description: Text to set on the clipboard (required for action=set)

definition.name: device_close_app
definition.title: Close App
definition.description: Force-stop an app by bundle ID. The app process is terminated.

bundleId.description: App bundle ID or package name

definition.name: device_context
definition.title: Context
definition.description: List or switch between app contexts (NATIVE_APP, WEBVIEW, etc.). Use action=list to see available contexts, action=switch to change. On Android (adb), WEBVIEW appears when a debuggable in-app WebView is open; use webview_cdp to drive its DOM. On iOS, WebView contexts require the Appium backend.

action.description: Action: list available contexts or switch to one

context.description: Context name to switch to (required for action=switch)

definition.name: device_dismiss_alert
definition.title: Dismiss Alert
definition.description: Accept or dismiss a system alert or permission dialog. Use accept=true for "Allow"/"OK", accept=false for "Deny"/"Cancel". Check device_snapshot first to confirm an alert is present.

accept.description: true to accept (Allow/OK), false to dismiss (Deny/Cancel)

definition.name: device_dismiss_keyboard
definition.title: Dismiss Keyboard
definition.description: Hide the on-screen keyboard. Call after typing to reveal elements that may be obscured by the keyboard.

definition.name: device_generate_locators
definition.title: Generate Locators
definition.description: Generate ranked locator suggestions for all interactive elements on the current screen. Each element gets a prioritized list: identifier (testID/resource-id) > label > text > type. Use this after healing to find the correct selector for updating test source code.

definition.name: device_get_alert_text
definition.title: Get Alert Text
definition.description: Get the text content of the currently displayed system alert or dialog. Call this before device_dismiss_alert to understand what the alert says.

definition.name: device_get_element_text
definition.title: Get Element Text
definition.description: Find an element in the UI hierarchy by query and return its text content (label or value). Specify at least one of: label, identifier, text, type. Call device_snapshot first to see available elements.

text.description: Visible text content

definition.name: device_get_window_size
definition.title: Get Window Size
definition.description: Get the width and height of the device screen in pixels (Android) or points (iOS).

definition.name: device_info
definition.title: Device Info
definition.description: Get information about the connected device: platform, name, OS version, device ID.

definition.name: device_list_devices
definition.title: List Devices
definition.description: List all connected devices and simulators/emulators.

definition.name: device_logs
definition.title: Device Logs
definition.description: Capture recent device logs. iOS: system log via IDB. Android: logcat. Optionally filter by text pattern.

durationSeconds.description: How many seconds of logs to retrieve (default: 30)

filter.description: Text pattern to filter log entries

definition.name: device_long_press
definition.title: Long Press
definition.description: Long press an element. Used for context menus, drag initiation, and other long-press interactions. Default duration is 1000ms.

text.description: Text content

definition.name: device_open_app
definition.title: Open App
definition.description: Launch or bring to foreground an app by bundle ID. iOS: bundle ID (e.g. io.metamask). Android: package name (e.g. io.metamask).

bundleId.description: App bundle ID or package name

definition.name: device_press_button
definition.title: Press Button
definition.description: Press a physical device button. Note: iOS has no back button — "back" maps to home.

definition.name: device_screen_recording
definition.title: Screen Recording
definition.description: Start or stop recording the device screen as an MP4 video. Call with action=start to begin, action=stop to end and save. Returns the file path on stop.

action.description: Action: start or stop recording

outputPath.description: File path to save the recording (optional, for start)

definition.name: device_screenshot
definition.title: Screenshot
definition.description: Capture a screenshot of the current device screen. Returns base64-encoded PNG data. Optionally saves to a file path.

outputPath.description: File path to save the screenshot (optional)

definition.name: device_scroll_to_element
definition.title: Scroll To Element
definition.description: Scroll the screen until an element matching the query becomes visible. Combines scrolling and element search into one atomic operation. Specify at least one of: label, identifier, text, type.

text.description: Text content to match

definition.name: device_select_device
definition.title: Select Device
definition.description: Select a device to use for this session. Call device_list_devices first to see available devices.

deviceId.description: Device ID to select (UDID for iOS, serial for Android)

definition.name: device_snapshot
definition.title: Device Snapshot
definition.description: Capture the current UI hierarchy from the device. Returns all visible elements with their types, labels, identifiers, values, frames, and enabled state. Call this FIRST to see what is on screen before interacting.

definition.name: device_swipe
definition.title: Swipe
definition.description: Swipe on the device screen. Use natural scrolling: swipe "up" to scroll down. Optionally specify start coordinates and distance. Coordinates are logical points, not screenshot pixels. The gesture runs with a fixed 0.3s duration; command completion does not verify that content moved — confirm with a screenshot or snapshot.

definition.name: device_tap_coordinates
definition.title: Tap Coordinates
definition.description: Tap at exact screen coordinates. Use as a last resort when an element cannot be found by label/identifier/text. Get coordinates from device_snapshot frame data.

x.description: X coordinate in pixels

y.description: Y coordinate in pixels

definition.name: device_tap_element
definition.title: Tap Element
definition.description: Find an element in the UI hierarchy by query and tap its center. Specify at least one of: label, identifier, text, type. Call device_snapshot first to see available elements.

text.description: Visible text content

definition.name: device_type
definition.title: Type Text
definition.description: Type text into the currently focused input field. Tap an input element first to focus it, then call this. The field is cleared before typing on all backends.

text.description: Text to type

definition.name: device_wait_for
definition.title: Wait For Element
definition.description: Poll the UI hierarchy until an element matching the query appears. Useful for waiting on transitions, loading states, or navigation.

text.description: Text content to match

timeoutMs.description: Max wait time in ms (default: 10000)

definition.name: hermes_cdp
definition.title: Hermes CDP
definition.description: Speak raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) to the React Native Hermes JS runtime of a running app via Metro’s inspector proxy (iOS and Android). Requires a DEBUG build with Metro running; release builds expose no inspector. Blocked methods (for safety): Runtime.terminateExecution, Inspector.detached. Node 20 must be launched with NODE_OPTIONS="--experimental-websocket" (Node 22+ works out of the box). Example: method "Runtime.evaluate" with params {"expression":"1+1","returnByValue":true} — the raw response nests the value at result.result.value.

method.description: The CDP method to invoke, e.g. "Runtime.evaluate".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds applied to each phase independently: discovery, socket open, identity probe, and the CDP call (default 30000, floored to 1000, max 120000).

metroPort.description: Override the Metro inspector proxy port for this call.

origin.description: Override the debugger WebSocket HTTP(S) Origin to match a custom Metro server base URL (default: http://127.0.0.1:<metroPort>).

appId.description: Override the expected app bundle identifier.

definition.name: hermes_targets
definition.title: Hermes Targets
definition.description: List and diagnose the debuggable React Native Hermes targets that Metro’s inspector proxy currently exposes (iOS and Android). Reports each candidate (id / title / appId / logicalDeviceId / nativePageReloads / wsUrl) plus which target would be chosen or why it is ambiguous. Use it to confirm Metro is running and your app is registered. Requires a DEBUG build with Metro running.

metroPort.description: Override the Metro inspector proxy port for this call.

appId.description: Override the expected app bundle identifier.

all.description: Bypass the appId filter and list ALL candidates (diagnostics).

definition.name: webview_cdp
definition.title: WebView CDP
definition.description: Speak raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) to a debuggable in-app Android WebView — the web page inside the app’s in-app browser. Unlike hermes_cdp (React Native JS engine, no DOM), this targets the Chromium page and exposes the full Chrome surface (Runtime, DOM, Page, Network, Input). Android only; the app must call WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true). Blocked methods (for safety): Browser.close, Target.closeTarget, Target.disposeBrowserContext, Browser.crashGpuProcess. Node 20 must be launched with NODE_OPTIONS="--experimental-websocket" (Node 22+ works out of the box). Example: method "Runtime.evaluate" with params {"expression":"document.querySelector('#submit').click()"}.

method.description: The CDP method to invoke, e.g. "Runtime.evaluate".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds for discovery and each CDP round-trip (default 30000, floored to 1000, max 120000).

urlFilter.description: Select the WebView page whose URL contains this substring when several WebView pages are open.

definition.name: list-session-recordings
definition.description: List Microsoft Clarity session recordings based on specified filters. The filters allow you to narrow down the recordings by various criteria such as URLs, device types, browser, OS, country, city, and more. The date filter is required and must be in UTC ISO 8601 format.

referringUrl.description: Filter by the referring URL that brought users to the site

userType.description: Filter by user type. Accepted values: NewUser, ReturningUser

sessionIntent.description: Filter by session intention level/user behavior classification.

visitedUrls.description: Filter by URLs visited during the session with pattern matching.

entryUrls.description: Filter by entry/landing page URLs with pattern matching.

exitUrls.description: Filter by exit page URLs with pattern matching.

country.description: Filter by country names (e.g., ['United States', 'Canada', 'United Kingdom'])

source.description: Filter by UTM source parameter values (e.g., ['google', 'facebook', 'direct'])

medium.description: Filter by UTM medium parameter values. Common values: ['organic', 'cpc', 'email', 'social', 'referral']

campaign.description: Filter by UTM campaign parameter values (e.g., ['summer_sale', 'product_launch'])

smartEvents.description: Filter by smart event names/IDs.
