definition.name: pr_review
definition.description: Run multi-voter consensus review on a PR diff (#2233). 5 voters (architect, security, devex, catfish, scope_steward) each emit approve/request_changes/abstain with reasoning and citations. Reuses consensus_vote infra; experimental.

prDiff.description: Unified diff text (max 2000000 chars). REQUIRED SHAPE (#4451): must contain a `diff --git` header, an `@@ … @@` hunk header backed by +/- lines, or a `---`/`+++` header pair — a prose summary of the change is REJECTED, because reviewing a summary is not reviewing the code and would be recorded as though it were. (Stated here because Zod refinements do not survive JSON-schema generation, so this constraint is otherwise invisible to clients.) No need to truncate before calling: the panel reads the whole diff whenever it fits the voters' context windows (#6003); a diff larger than that is security-prioritized and PARTIALLY reviewed (lowest-priority whole files dropped; a partial panel read can block but never verified-approve). Separately, the audit record's hash binds only the first 50000 UTF-8 bytes; the response `coverage` and the record summary state both what the panel read and what the hash binds.

definition.name: run_dev_pipeline
definition.description: Run the multi-agent development pipeline. Accepts direct task instructions, a plan file, or a spec file. Implement, QA and gates use a per-run scratch worktree pinned to HEAD. Isolation of scratch-bound expert, install, gate and change-capture subprocesses is an OS sandbox with the source read-only when changes.isolation.mode is os-sandbox. Otherwise isolation is best-effort and changes.isolation.reason explains why bwrap or sandbox setup is unavailable. Pipeline-owned git runs hermetically with repository-local GIT_* variables removed, optional index refresh disabled, fsmonitor disabled and source hooks disabled. Gate subprocesses receive the hermetic git environment. Installs are scratch-local with inherited directory overrides removed, copy imports and HUSKY=0, and are killed as a process tree on timeout. Changes to the source repository's shared git config are reported as a warning, or logged when the run throws or times out. Only in best-effort mode, an install descendant that ignores SIGTERM can write during the kill grace period before the config snapshot. The OS sandbox confines descendants too. Dependencies are installed inside the scratch, frozen from the HEAD root lockfile before implementation. OS-sandbox installs use private writable package stores and caches under a private TMPDIR with copy imports. Shared package stores and caches remain read-only. Best-effort installs prefer the local package cache and fetch missing packages. Returns changes (unified diff, baseSha, worktreePath, worktreeRemoved, dependencies, isolation, empty, status: changes, no_changes or tampered) for the operator to apply. changes.dependencies reports status installed, none or failed, with manager and failure reason when applicable. No root package.json or supported lockfile means none. Provisioning failure makes the quality gate unmeasured with the reason. worktreeRemoved reflects whether the scratch path exists after cleanup, and prune failures have a separate warning. Failed removal preserves the diff with a leftover-path warning. Dirty-source warnings identify HEAD and the number of omitted uncommitted paths. Scratch-bound expert CLIs and change capture run inside the same sandbox. The sandbox executable is pinned before execution. Change capture disables external diff and textconv. The scratch gitfile, commondir and gitdir are checked against their pre-run bytes. Modified metadata refuses the diff with status tampered and a warning. Cleanup removes only the scratch and worktree metadata paths recorded before execution, then prunes from the source repository. The sandbox permits writes to the scratch, its own git metadata and a private TMPDIR. Host IPC environment redirects are removed, /run/user is masked and existing Docker socket paths are masked. DNS resolver paths under /run remain available. Network and abstract-namespace sockets remain reachable. Supports dry-run (plan+vote only). Supports dispatch: 'async' (non-dryRun runs) — returns a jobId immediately, then poll get_job_result.

Omitted means '3'. Can only lower trust: the effective tier is the least-trusted of this, the measured caller tier and every source the run fetched. Recorded with the caller tier at the consensus→execute policy gate.

definition.name: obsidian_append_to_note
definition.title: Obsidian Append To Note
definition.description: Append content to a note. **Without `section`: appends to the end of the file, or creates the file if it does not exist (your content becomes the full file).** When an existing file does not end in a line break, one is inserted before your content. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a path that differs from an existing note only in letter case fails with `case_variant_exists` (`existingPath` names the note when the folder listing shows exactly one case match). With `section`: appends to the end of that heading/block/frontmatter (on Local REST API v5.0 and later, content appended to a heading is separated from the section’s existing content by a blank line, except a list item appended to a section that ends in a list and has no sub-headings, which continues that list) — use `obsidian_get_note` with `format: "document-map"` to discover available targets. Name a heading by its full `Parent::Child` path as the document map lists it, or by a bare leaf name matched at any depth. A leaf shared by several headings is rejected with `ambiguous_section`, unless one of them has no parent heading, in which case the write targets that one; a full path that occurs more than once in the note is rejected with `ambiguous_section` too. For block-reference targets, content is concatenated adjacent to the block line without inserting a separator — include a leading newline in `content` if you want one. Set `createTargetIfMissing` to bring the target section into existence rather than failing when it does not exist.

target.description: Heading, block, or frontmatter locator. Heading: the full `Parent::Child` path as `obsidian_get_note` `format: "document-map"` lists it, or a bare leaf name matched at any depth. A leaf shared by several headings reads the first (every full path comes back in `candidates`); a write rejects it with `ambiguous_section`, unless one of them has no parent heading, in which case the write targets that one. A full path that occurs more than once in the note reads the first; a write rejects it with `ambiguous_section`. Block: the reference ID without the caret (e.g. "2d9b4a", not "^2d9b4a"). A leaf shared by several headings is rejected with `ambiguous_section`, unless one of them has no parent heading, in which case the write targets that one; a full path that occurs more than once in the note is rejected with `ambiguous_section` too.

definition.name: obsidian_replace_in_note
definition.title: Obsidian Replace In Note
definition.description: Search and replace inside a single note, literally or by regex. Replacements run in array order, each over the previous one's output, and cover the note body only unless `scope` says otherwise — the YAML frontmatter block is left byte-identical by default, because a prose edit that lands in a scalar can silently invalidate the whole block. Use for edits that don't fit `obsidian_patch_note`'s structural targets — e.g., body-wide find-and-replace. Prefer `obsidian_manage_frontmatter` for typed edits to a single property.

path.description: Vault-relative path including extension, e.g. "Projects/foo.md".

oneOf.description: Address a note by its vault-relative path.

type.description: Address the file currently open in Obsidian.

oneOf.description: Address whichever file is currently active in the Obsidian UI.

date.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the current period.

oneOf.description: Address a periodic note (current or dated).

target.description: Where the note lives.

scope.description: Which part of the note the replacements run over. `body` leaves the YAML frontmatter block byte-identical. `frontmatter` and `both` also rewrite the YAML between the `---` fences — never the fences themselves — and re-parse it afterwards, failing the whole call and writing nothing if the result no longer parses. That check catches YAML that breaks, not YAML that still parses while meaning something else: a replacement that renames a key or strips a scalar's quotes passes it.

search.description: Substring or regex pattern to match.

replace.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes matches.

useRegex.description: Treat `search` as an ECMAScript regex pattern (≤1024 chars, no nested quantifiers like `(a+)+` — catastrophic-backtracking guard).

wholeWord.description: Match only at word boundaries. Applies in both literal and regex modes — the search pattern is wrapped with `\b…\b`.

flexibleWhitespace.description: Treat any run of whitespace in `search` as matching any whitespace in the body. Literal mode only — has no effect when `useRegex: true` (express it directly with `\s+`).

replaceAll.description: When false, only the first match is replaced.

replacements.description: Replacements to apply in array order over the evolving content.

path.description: Resolved vault-relative path of the note.

totalReplacements.description: Total number of substitutions applied across all replacement entries.

search.description: The search term/pattern that ran.

count.description: Number of matches replaced for this entry, across every scope it ran in.

bodyCount.description: Matches replaced in the note body.

frontmatterCount.description: Matches replaced inside the YAML frontmatter block. Always 0 under the default `body` scope.

perReplacement.description: Per-entry counts in the order replacements were applied.

previousSizeInBytes.description: Byte size of the note before replacements were applied.

currentSizeInBytes.description: Byte size of the note after replacements were applied. Equals `previousSizeInBytes` when no matches were found and no write was issued.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `path_forbidden`: The target path is outside OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS, or OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY=true denies all writes. The pre-read also requires the path to be readable. `regex_invalid`: A `useRegex: true` replacement supplied a `search` pattern that is not a valid ECMAScript regex. `regex_unsafe`: A `useRegex: true` replacement supplied a `search` pattern that is well-formed but exceeds the 1024-character limit or contains nested quantifiers known to cause catastrophic backtracking against the note body. `frontmatter_invalid`: A `scope` of "frontmatter" or "both" produced YAML that no longer parses as a mapping of properties, or that parses but cannot be re-emitted (an alias whose anchor the replacement removed). Nothing is written — the note keeps its original bytes. The check reads the rewritten YAML only, so a replacement that renames a key or changes a scalar's type while still parsing is not caught by it. `note_missing`: The vault path does not resolve to an existing note. `no_active_file`: Target was `active` but no file is currently open in Obsidian. `periodic_unsupported`: Target was `periodic` and this vault runs Local REST API v5.0.2 or later without the companion periodic-notes extension, so the `/periodic/` routes are not served at all. `periodic_not_found`: Target was `periodic`, the `/periodic/` routes are served on this vault, and no note exists for the requested period. `periodic_disabled`: Target was `periodic` but the requested period is not enabled in Obsidian's Periodic Notes plugin settings. `path_is_directory`: The supplied path names a folder rather than a note file. `path_traversal`: The path contains a `.` or `..` segment, which is rejected to prevent vault escape. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: obsidian_search_notes
definition.title: Obsidian Search Notes
definition.description: Search the vault by text tokens or JSONLogic predicate. Pick the mode that matches the query shape. Results paginate via opaque cursors: omit `cursor` for the first page, then pass `nextCursor` from the prior response. Text-mode hits additionally clip per file at `maxMatchesPerHit` match locations.

mode.description: Which search algorithm to run. `text` splits `query` on whitespace and requires every token, each matched case-insensitively as a substring of the filename or note body. Quotes are literal characters, not a phrase operator. Each hit returns match locations with surrounding context windows; tokens that sit close together, such as the words of a phrase, share one location. `jsonlogic` evaluates a JSONLogic tree against each note, with `var` paths into `path`, `content`, `frontmatter.<key>`, `tags`, `stat.{ctime,mtime,size}`, and `links`, `backlinks`, and `unresolvedLinks` (on plugin versions that provide them; under OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS, readable entries only), plus `glob` and `regexp` operators — both take their arguments as `[PATTERN, VALUE]`, so the pattern comes first and the `{"var": ...}` reference second.

query.description: The query string. Required for `text` and `omnisearch` modes; ignored in `jsonlogic` mode (use `logic` instead — this field must be a string, so passing a JSONLogic tree here is rejected). In `text` mode it is split on whitespace and every token must appear; quotes stay part of the tokens, so a quoted phrase matches nothing unless the note contains the quote characters.

logic.description: JSONLogic tree. Required for `jsonlogic` mode; ignored in `text` and `omnisearch` modes (use `query` instead — this field must be an object, so passing a string here is rejected). `glob` and `regexp` take `[PATTERN, VALUE]` — pattern first: `{"glob": ["Projects/*.md", {"var": "path"}]}`. Backlinks ("what links here") have no dedicated tool; find them this way: `{"regexp": ["\\[\\[Target Note(\\\\?\\||#|\\]\\])", {"var": "content"}]}` finds every readable note whose body wikilinks or embeds `Target Note`, in plain, aliased (`|`, or the table-safe `\|`), or section form. `obsidian_get_note` with `includeLinks: true` covers the outgoing direction.

contextLength.description: Characters of context on each side of a match location (text mode only). Sizes the rendered text as well as the structured payload, so a wide window multiplies the response across every location on the page. Query tokens within 2 × `contextLength` of each other share a location.

pathPrefix.description: Filter returned filenames by prefix (text mode only, applied after matching — does not narrow the search itself).

maxMatchesPerHit.description: Cap on match locations returned per file in text mode. A phrase whose tokens share one location counts once. When clipped, the hit carries `truncated: true` and `totalMatches`.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response. Omit for the first page. Page size is server-determined; do not assume a fixed value. Under OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS, later `jsonlogic` pages come from the hit list the first page computed.

mode.description: Echoed mode.

filename.description: Vault-relative path of the matching note.

context.description: Surrounding text around the location.

start.description: Location start offset within the subject upstream matched — the note body in the usual case, or the note basename (extension stripped) when the filename itself matched, in which case `context` is that basename. This is not an offset into `context`; use `contextStart` for that. Note-body values index the same string `obsidian_get_note` returns.

end.description: Location end offset within the same subject `start` indexes.

contextStart.description: Location start offset within `context`. `context.slice(contextStart, contextEnd)` is the matched text, from the first matched token through the last.

match.description: Where the location sits, on two origins: `start`/`end` index the matched subject, `contextStart`/`contextEnd` index the accompanying `context` window.

items.description: A match location within a file: one token occurrence, or several query tokens close enough to share one context window (a phrase).

matches.description: Match locations with their context windows, in document order. Capped per file by `maxMatchesPerHit`.

totalMatches.description: Total match locations in this file. Present only when `matches` was clipped to `maxMatchesPerHit`.

truncated.description: True when `matches` was clipped to `maxMatchesPerHit` locations. Use `obsidian_get_note` to read the full file when more context is needed.

items.description: A file with one or more text-search match locations.

hits.description: Matching files with their match locations.

totalCount.description: Total post-path-policy hit count across all pages, before pagination.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Omitted on the last page (do not treat absent as null).

oneOf.description: Text-search results.

mode.description: Echoed mode.

filename.description: Vault-relative path of the matching note.

result.description: The query result for this file — shape determined by the query.

items.description: A file with a structured (Dataview/JSONLogic) result value.

hits.description: Matching files with the JSONLogic result per file.

totalCount.description: Total post-path-policy hit count across all pages, before pagination.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Omitted on the last page (do not treat absent as null).

oneOf.description: JSONLogic results.

effectiveQuery.description: The query string as submitted (text and omnisearch modes only).

notice.description: Recovery guidance when the search returned no hits.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `path_prefix_invalid_mode`: `pathPrefix` was provided in a non-text mode (only `text` supports prefix filtering). `query_required`: `query` is missing for `text` or `omnisearch` mode (required for both). `context_length_too_large`: The Local REST API exhausted its string capacity building one context window per match, so the whole text search failed. `logic_required`: `logic` is missing for `jsonlogic` mode. `logic_invalid`: The JSONLogic tree failed to evaluate against a note — an unrecognized operator, or an operand that could not be evaluated (an uncompilable `regexp` pattern). A mis-arity operator is not rejected: it evaluates to false and the search returns zero hits. `logic_too_costly`: With OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS set, the server evaluates the JSONLogic tree itself, and the tree passed a bound: nesting deeper than 1,000 levels, more than a work budget, or more than 10 s of evaluation. One work budget is per note — the size of values built by `merge`, `cat`, `map`, and array literals while evaluating that note, up to the note's own size plus 10,000,000 units — and one is per search: 10,000,000 units across every note for returned results, where a result whose JSON is at most 1,024 characters is free and a larger one pays for what it holds beyond its own note. `note_too_deep`: With OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS set, a readable note holds data, usually a frontmatter value, nested deeper than the server can hand to its evaluator (about 3,500 levels under Node, more under Bun). `omnisearch_unreachable`: Omnisearch was reachable at startup but is now unreachable (Obsidian quit, plugin disabled, or mobile session). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

definition.name: obsidian_write_note
definition.title: Obsidian Write Note
definition.description: Create or overwrite a note. With `section`, replaces just that heading/block/frontmatter section in place — use `obsidian_get_note` with `format: "document-map"` to discover available targets. Name a heading by its full `Parent::Child` path as the document map lists it, or by a bare leaf name matched at any depth. A leaf shared by several headings is rejected with `ambiguous_section`, unless one of them has no parent heading, in which case the write targets that one; a full path that occurs more than once in the note is rejected with `ambiguous_section` too. Whole-file writes fail with `file_exists` against an existing note unless `overwrite: true`, and with `case_variant_exists` when the path differs from an existing note only in letter case on a case-insensitive filesystem (`existingPath` names the note when the folder listing shows exactly one case match) — for in-place edits, prefer `obsidian_patch_note` (sections), `obsidian_append_to_note` (append), or `obsidian_replace_in_note` (find-and-replace). For heading sections, `content` is the new body; the heading line is preserved automatically.

path.description: Vault-relative path including extension, e.g. "Projects/foo.md".

oneOf.description: Address a note by its vault-relative path.

type.description: Address the file currently open in Obsidian.

oneOf.description: Address whichever file is currently active in the Obsidian UI.

date.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the current period.

oneOf.description: Address a periodic note (current or dated).

target.description: Where the note lives.

content.description: Body to write. For heading sections, the new section body — do not repeat the heading line (it stays in place). Markdown unless `contentType` is `json`.

section.description: Optional sub-document target. When set, only this section is replaced; rest of the note is untouched.

type.description: Heading by name, block by reference, or frontmatter field by key.

target.description: Heading, block, or frontmatter locator. Heading: the full `Parent::Child` path as `obsidian_get_note` `format: "document-map"` lists it, or a bare leaf name matched at any depth. A leaf shared by several headings reads the first (every full path comes back in `candidates`); a write rejects it with `ambiguous_section`, unless one of them has no parent heading, in which case the write targets that one. A full path that occurs more than once in the note reads the first; a write rejects it with `ambiguous_section`. Block: the reference ID without the caret (e.g. "2d9b4a", not "^2d9b4a"). Frontmatter: the field name.

contentType.description: Content body format. Use "json" for typed frontmatter values or block-targeted table rows. JSON values must be valid JSON literals — strings need quoting (`"\"draft\""`, not `"draft"`), and numbers/booleans/arrays/objects pass through as-is.

overwrite.description: Whole-file mode only (ignored when `section` is set). When `false` (default), the call fails with `file_exists` if the target note already exists — read it first and use `obsidian_patch_note` / `obsidian_append_to_note` / `obsidian_replace_in_note` for in-place edits, or retry with `overwrite: true` for a deliberate full replacement.

path.description: Resolved vault-relative path of the note that was written.

sectionTargeted.description: True when only a section was replaced; false for full-file writes.

sectionTarget.description: Section locator the replacement was applied to. Present when `section` was supplied. For headings this is the resolved locator — a bare leaf name is reported back as its full `Parent::Child` path.

created.description: True when the write created a new file. False when it replaced an existing one or targeted a section.

previousSizeInBytes.description: Byte size of the note before the write. Zero when `created` is true. On overwrites this is the destructive blast radius.

currentSizeInBytes.description: Byte size of the note after the write, read from the upstream after the operation completed. Compare against `previousSizeInBytes` and your own content length to detect unexpected upstream behavior.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `file_exists`: Whole-file write was attempted against an existing note and `overwrite` was not set to `true`. `case_variant_exists`: Whole-file write to a path that differs from an existing note only in letter case, on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS, Windows) where both name one file. `existingPath` names that note when the parent folder listing shows exactly one case match; it is omitted when several match, and when a file Obsidian does not index, such as a dot-file, already sits at the path. `path_forbidden`: The target path is outside OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS, or OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY=true denies all writes. `note_missing`: Section replace targets a path that does not resolve to an existing note (PATCH requires the file to exist). `no_active_file`: Target was `active` but no file is currently open in Obsidian. `periodic_unsupported`: Target was `periodic` and this vault runs Local REST API v5.0.2 or later without the companion periodic-notes extension, so the `/periodic/` routes are not served at all. `periodic_not_found`: Target was `periodic`, the `/periodic/` routes are served on this vault, and no note exists for the requested period. `periodic_disabled`: Target was `periodic` but the requested period is not enabled in Obsidian's Periodic Notes plugin settings. `section_target_missing`: `section` was provided but the named heading/block/frontmatter field does not exist in the note. `ambiguous_section`: A bare heading leaf name matches more than one heading in the note, or the resolved full heading path occurs more than once, so the replacement target is undetermined. `heading_outside_section`: On Local REST API v5.0 and later, the new body of a heading section carries a heading at or above that section’s own level, which would have to sit outside the section. `patch_rejected`: The section exists but the plugin refused the new content for it — table rows for a block that is not a table, a row with the wrong cell count, or content of the wrong shape. `path_is_directory`: The supplied path names a folder rather than a note file. `path_traversal`: The path contains a `.` or `..` segment, which is rejected to prevent vault escape. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

definition.name: analyze_javascript_application
definition.title: Analyze Javascript Application
definition.description: Reconstruct one local ASAR or extracted JavaScript application as an inline application graph without executing it. Returns recovered graph nodes, edges, semantic relations, integrity contradictions, limitations, and coverage. Select source_paths to acquire and analyze only exact inventoried file paths; the complete artifact inventory and identity remain intact, and unselected sources remain explicit unknowns. Dependencies are not implicitly analyzed. Select detail summary to retain the complete analysis Evidence in this session and receive only its summary view, then inspect selected modules or pages with inspect_analysis_view. Select a javascript-routes view with summary detail to query deduplicated static patterns, source-linked occurrences, source status or interpretation gaps with filters, fields and paging. Static routes do not establish reachability or the full application route set. Summary detail reduces delivery, whereas source_paths bounds source analysis. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue retains observed bytes as untrusted and marks graph coverage partial. Timeout recovery: returned provider_timeout uses the per-source analysis_timeout_ms budget. A host-only 'timed out awaiting tools/call' needs a longer client tool deadline, not a larger analysis_timeout_ms. Never repeat the unchanged call to test whether that timeout persists; report the host setting if configuration is not editable (Codex: mcp_servers.<server>.tool_timeout_sec, seconds).

input_path.description: Absolute path to the JavaScript application on the machine running REA.

format.description: Declared input artifact format.

source_paths.description: Exact relevant file paths from the artifact inventory, relative to the application root, analyzed in first-request order before unselected scopes; no globs or implicit dependencies. Omit to analyze all sources.

max_semantic_nodes.description: Maximum retained semantic nodes across the application; defaults to 100000. Worker heap and parent result admission remain enforced.

max_semantic_nodes_per_file.description: Maximum retained semantic nodes per source file; defaults to 20000, additionally bounded by max_semantic_nodes and memory/transfer limits.

max_semantic_unknowns.description: Maximum retained semantic unknown records across the application; defaults to 100000. Omitted emission occurrences are counted by family and reason.

max_semantic_unknowns_per_file.description: Maximum retained semantic unknown records per source file; defaults to 20000, additionally bounded by max_semantic_unknowns and memory/transfer limits.

max_heap_mb.description: Maximum V8 old-space heap in MiB for the isolated JavaScript source analyzer; defaults to 1024. This does not change the CLI/MCP process heap. When REA runs on Bun, which ignores V8 heap flags, Windows instead limits the analyzer's committed memory to this budget plus a 512 MiB runtime reserve; other Bun hosts enforce no limit.

analysis_timeout_ms.description: Maximum startup, analysis and transfer time per JavaScript source, in milliseconds; defaults to 300000. On timeout, return collected partial Evidence and stop the analysis.

definition.name: capture_browser_scenario
definition.title: Capture Browser Scenario
definition.description: Run a controlled browser scenario when passive observation cannot exercise the application. Launch the selected executable or connect to a loopback CDP target, provide a start URL and actions, and select storage or artifacts when needed. A request action sends one HTTP request to the start origin through the page's own fetch, with header values from secrets, page cookies or local storage; write methods change application state. Environment, empty storage, a URL-only final capture, and measured event-retention budgets are defaults. capture.network selects request_body, response_body, and header_values independently; capture.limits lets callers raise or lower the event count, retained-allocation estimates, network transaction count, and network content budgets. Selected content is returned inline with transaction and event references, byte digests, and explicit unavailable states. Budget omissions identify affected event kinds and network transactions. Credentials and declared secrets are redacted. Agents can run their own local fixture servers to control application responses. Actions run until completion or cancellation unless timeout_ms is set. Results are returned inline.

definition.name: capture_process_scenario
definition.title: Capture Process Scenario
definition.description: Run one caller-selected command under a PTY and return process capture Evidence with residual unknowns. The renderer admits at most 1,000,000 combined terminal cells, computed as columns × (rows + scrollback); every resize uses the selected scrollback and must fit the same budget. Supply a smaller terminal shape when that product is too large; dimensions are never clamped. This release has no runtime override for that cell budget. A command name resolves through the inherited PATH; the working directory defaults to the caller's current directory; host environment variables are inherited with scenario overrides. Environment keys cannot contain '=' or NUL, and REA_PROCESS_RUN_ID is reserved for process ownership. Filesystem snapshots are opt-in through filesystem_observation_paths. A positive finalization_ms makes a timeout or idle deadline send SIGTERM to the captured root through its start identity, keep observing, and send SIGKILL once after the interval; exit.finalization records each attempt with its delivery result and the observed exit, and cancellation still ends the run at once. The target runs with the current user's permissions; this is not a security sandbox.

__schema12.description: Verbatim direct-request path; not part of semantic identity.

__schema15.description: The capture must preserve its canonical scenario, comparison, and normalization SHA-256 commitments; ordered capture timestamps and contiguous sequence numbers; before and final filesystem snapshots with truncation propagated; and exit-code consistency with deadline termination. The event journal is required; empty journals are valid. A non-empty journal must reference every captured observation exactly once with unique in-range references. These cross-field invariants are checked by REA after capture.

definition.name: decompile_all
definition.title: Decompile All
definition.description: Write provider pseudocode for every analyzed function, or a filtered subset, into a caller-selected directory and return only a manifest. Each file records the provider function name, canonical address, inclusive body ranges when procedure_info supplies them, and that function's procedure_info and pseudocode limitations. Each function's index record keeps its complete limitations. Evidence keeps at most eight first-observed distinct per-function limitations within an encoded-text budget; the omitted count measures observations, not distinct warnings. The manifest reports counts, the output directory, the index path, at most 32 failure details within 2,048 JSON-encoded UTF-8 bytes (names can be omitted; full names remain in the index), provider identity, and the analysis-profile digest. Pseudocode stays in the files. An existing directory is refused unless resume is set and the journal matches the target SHA-256, provider, and analysis profile; verified files are skipped and conflicting files are left unchanged. layout dwarf reports that compilation-unit paths are unavailable and names files by address. A failure of one function does not stop the others. Functions procedure_info classifies as external are counted as external, get no file, and are not decompiled; a resume skips them. Cancellation leaves files already written. Per-function limits do not bound the whole call; use limit and resume to select work that fits the client deadline, including import, listing and file work.

resume.description: Continue a journal for the same target SHA-256, provider, analysis profile, and layout. Both digests must be known. Verified files and functions recorded as external are skipped, conflicting files are left unchanged, and functions not yet tried run before retries of recorded failures.

definition.name: inspect_analysis_view
definition.title: Inspect Analysis View
definition.description: Use javascript-routes collections to query route patterns, source-linked occurrences, source status, unknowns or summary counts from retained JavaScript application or web-bundle Evidence. Inspect selected views of supported completed Evidence without repeating analysis. Choose a view compatible with the parent operation described below. Command summary views preserve ordered GDB records or opaque objdump stdout/stderr once, source parameters, completion facts and parent identity. They do not establish current target state. Historical capture summaries return identity and counts without bodies or archive inventories. Capture views page retained records: view {kind: "capture", detail: "preview" | "complete", offset: 0, limit: 20}; preview selects recorded headline fields and binary descriptors, complete returns exact records with all sidecars. Offsets follow the selected parent record order, preserving original producer ordinals. Paging never reopens the source or reruns the decoder. Native export tables use kind native-exports, collection exports/issues, exact names or original indices, selected fields and matching-row pagination; parent Evidence plus source_index identifies each row. Source coverage stays separate from page coverage. BEAM views use kind beam, collections atoms/exports/imports/lambdas/chunks, exact names/indices/fields and matching-row pages; import modules intersects function names. source_index identifies original parent-and-collection rows, preserving every arity and raw atom index. beam.counts preserves null missing tables versus decoded empty tables; runtime absence remains unknown. PYC views use kind python-pyc, collection code_objects, names/indices/fields and paging; source_index scopes every same-name alternative to the parent, nested_code keeps code-constant references, and pyc.coverage preserves source coverage. Go metadata uses kind go, collection dependencies/settings, exact paths/keys or indices, fields and pagination. Row index refers to the original collection; empty selections return no rows, and dependency coverage remains unknown. Rust metadata uses kind rust, collection packages/edges, exact names/versions or original indices, selected fields, edge from_indices/to_indices and matching-row pagination. Embedded-record coverage is separate from unknown runtime dependencies. For inspect_pcap_capture parents, kind pcap pages endpoints, dns-queries, tls-sni, protocols, http-uris or unattributed-addresses. Select an exact query for dns-addresses, or a tshark/capinfos stream for UTF-16 diagnostics text. Page totals count retained facts; source coverage remains explicit. Qlog summaries keep profile/scope and counts; kind qlog pages traces, streams, loss-declarations, incomplete-records, contributions, ranges or final-sizes. Except traces, select trace_index; stream-specific facets also require exact stream_id and direction. Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope, and interval overlap or endpoint loss declarations do not prove retransmission or network loss. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. The environment-manifest view projects the same HAR requests on the primary origin (most JSON-like records) into a replayable tool surface: view {kind: "environment-manifest", template_rules: ["after-uid-literal", "opaque-token", "sibling-variance"], include_query_parameter_names: true}. Each tool has a deterministic name, a path template and parameters from the four format rules plus the selected opt-in rules, observed query parameter names, a value-free body shape for POST/PUT/PATCH, status and content-type sets and record ordinals; records are pointers into the parent, excluded groups carry a reason and three fixed unknowns are always stated. Templates, parameters and names are inferences; the view copies no header, cookie or body values and refuses parents inspected with sensitive values. A capture_browser_scenario parent that selected response bodies or header values projects the same way, one record per network transaction in request order; it relies on capture-time redaction of declared secrets instead of that refusal, and a transaction whose URL was redacted is left unrepresented. The environment-state view extracts, from the same parents, the initial state the recorded reads observed: view {kind: "environment-state", template_rules: [...]} with the rules of the manifest it accompanies. It reads response bodies recorded before the first related write and reports entity types with an identity field (proved by a path parameter or inferred from a field name), entities in collection order with per-view values where views differ, documents for non-parameterized reads that are not entities and have one initial request line (item-shaped paths stay recorded), and a render plan per read tool: item and list views reproduce their latest recordings from the state (a list also learns the filters, search, sort and paging its recordings verify, and answers new values of them from the state), and every other read tool is a recorded view with a reason. It also reports a write plan per state-changing tool (create, update, delete or document, built from its first successful call) and write_clock; a plan is served only when replaying the capture shows a later read confirming its effect and none contradicting it. Types and identity are inferences; values are recorded data, so it refuses parents inspected with sensitive values, and a scenario parent must have selected response bodies; its values keep the capture redaction markers, and a write whose URL it redacted ends the state of every type. The environment-coverage view, view {kind: "environment-coverage", template_rules: [...]}, summarizes that state without its entities: reads.state and reads.recorded count read tools answered from the state and replayed (recorded_reasons per view reason), writes.served lists the served write tools, and writes.withheld lists each other write tool with its reason, plan record, contradicting read and a hint about what to record next; it refuses what the environment-state view refuses. For a retained record use source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary receipt. Source kind is required. Portable source uses {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>}. A completed Evidence JSON file on this host uses {kind: "evidence-file", path: "<absolute path>"}: REA reads and authenticates it, then projects it like retained Evidence, so a large capture is bounded by the file reader rather than by inline-input accounting. The file may also be an Evidence bundle written by CLI --evidence_output or export_evidence_bundle; select evidence_id when it contains more than one record. For layout, JavaScript, inventory, WASM, Mach-O, Interface Builder, EVM, managed artifact, Android package and Dart AOT sources, request a summary with view: {kind: "summary"}; summary is a view kind and has no facet. The WASM summary gives validation, counts, WAT digest/length, tool profile and execution/network states without reading WAT text. Select a layout mitigations/linkage facet, one section/symbol/module, or a stable page. Module pages include assets, bundled and source modules; use node_id for ambiguous or unavailable paths. Typed module references use view {kind: "javascript", collection: "modules", projection: "references", where: {path: "main.js", kind: "javascript-module"}, offset: 0, limit: 64}; where matches exact retained strings (null selects unavailable paths). Rows include canonical identity, retained source-range count and observation support states. Source coverage and selection remain explicit; exhausting matching rows does not prove runtime loading or complete analysis. For exact file/native facts and processing gaps, use view {kind: "javascript-facts", where: {paths: ["package.json"]}, property_keys: ["name", "operation", "analysis_status"]}. Rows page original observations with canonical identities and Evidence; missing properties remain omitted. Paths match recorded artifact-path/source-range locations; optional kinds filter nodes. To discover field names without values, opt into include_available_property_keys: true with property_keys: []. Canonical identity and Evidence are separate from properties; keep each node_id/observation_id pair together when composing results. Inventory uses view: {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64}. Inventory views page nodes, occurrences, edges or integrity contradictions. Occurrences accept exact logical_paths and occurrence_ids; nodes accept artifact_ids. Batch filters intersect (omitted means all available, [] means none); fields selects columns while retaining identity links. source_complete describes retained graph membership; source_coverage describes producer coverage, including unknown encrypted PCK directories. Page exhaustion does not prove absence in a partial source. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Interface Builder views use kind interface-builder and collection documents/nodes/edges/coverage; nodes and edges accept an exact document relative_path. EVM summary returns all inferred interface candidates, carrier/decoded identities and explicit unknowns without hex or duplicate stdout. EVM views use kind evm and facet functions/bytecode_hex/stdout/stderr; function pages preserve the original candidate rows, and text offsets/limits count UTF-16 code units (hex has two characters per decoded byte). Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings and carry the source selection and coverage. Android package summaries retain all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text. Android manifest pages use kind android, facet manifest, offset and limit in UTF-16 code units; source_status preserves partial decoded coverage even when the retained text page is exhausted. Dart AOT summary preserves target/ABI/library identity, snapshot headers and pool lower bounds. String pages use kind dart-aot, collection package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens; source coverage remains partial when the producer says partial. Protobuf views use kind protobuf, collection bodies/frames/fields, with record_ordinals, body_pointers and fields; field pages also select frame_indices, field_ids, field_numbers or schema_names. Byte identity, offset basis and body status remain present. Text and schema_value are opt-in page columns. APK signing views use kind apk-signature and collection signers/digests/lineage, with ids, signer_ids, schemes, fields and paging. Identity links remain when fields is empty. Declared identities and digest matches do not establish signature verification or authenticity. Model views use kind model-artifact and collection metadata (keys), tensors (names/types) or types (derived totals), with indices, fields and paging. Header SHA-256 scopes declarations; full-file identity remains unknown unless full hashing was selected. Arrays retain typed eight-element previews with explicit omissions. IL2CPP metadata views use kind il2cpp-metadata and collection sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/string_literals/code_gen_modules/method_addresses/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances/generic_method_issues. Select indices, fields and pages; sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances accept exact names (native type names match retained rendered values, preserving same-name rows; null names never match), types also accept image_indices/namespaces/declaring_types, and methods/members accept declaring_types. Parameters and parameter_types accept method_indices; code_gen_modules accept image_indices; method_addresses and generic_method_instances accept addresses/states (generic_method_instances also method_indices), preserving every folded alternative; generic_method_issues accept rows. Row index is scoped to the metadata digest; native pages add binary_source. Uncollected native tables have null counts and remain unavailable. Desktop directory views use kind desktop-application and collection files/omissions/candidates/components/next_probes, with fields and pagination; files and omissions accept exact paths or their stable IDs, and candidates accept families. Source coverage and stable row IDs remain available. Native inventory Evidence from list_names, list/search_procedures or list/search_strings uses view: {kind: "native-inventory", offset: 0, limit: 64, fields: ["value"]}. Rows keep source_index and address even with selected fields. Summary counts describe retained rows; provider discovery coverage remains unknown. Native function Evidence accepts kind summary for identity, availability and facet counts, or kind native for selected facts: view: {kind: "native", facet: "procedure"}. Facets select procedure, pseudocode, assembly, basic blocks, comments, callers/callees, references, unresolved calls, referenced strings/names, native API and high-pcode. Use nonnegative offset and a positive caller-selected limit (defaults 0 and 64); pseudocode uses UTF-16 code units, other native pages use rows. Returns artifact identity, parent Evidence ID, a distinct view digest, coverage, limitations and unknowns. Actual serialized size determines MCP transport admission; choose a smaller page or export the complete retained Evidence if needed.

definition.name: search_procedures

definition.description: Search every analyzed procedure name using literal matching by default or regex when requested. Results are deterministic and complete. Hopper regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode syntax in a cancellable worker. The matching deadline is REA_REGEX_MATCHING_DEADLINE_MS (a positive decimal integer of milliseconds from 1 to 2147483647, default 5000). Unset keeps the default. A deadline failure names the effective milliseconds, source (default or setting), the default, and the maximum, and leaves the API usable. The worker old-generation request is REA_REGEX_WORKER_HEAP_REQUEST_MIB (a decimal integer of mebibytes from 7 to 16384, default 128). Unset keeps the default. A positive Node --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, overrides that request and is not limited by the setting's floor or maximum. A heap failure names the effective request, its source (default or setting), the default, the floor, and the maximum. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

definition.name: start_gdb_session

definition.description: Start a BYO GDB process in MI3 mode when available, suppress startup files, and disable auto-loading. Optionally set inferior_tty to a caller-selected terminal for future inferior runs; REA verifies the setting through GDB/MI before the session becomes ready. The selected terminal must remain available after GDB exits. A live inferior can be detached during close only while this durable output sink remains verified. REA verifies both destinations and `dbg.exitkills=false` before detaching. Backend and target capabilities depend on the installed build. The session lives in this REA MCP process. Persistent sessions require Linux `/proc` descriptor readback. In a shared MCP server, starting this session retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. definition.name: attach_packed_output
definition.title: Attach Packed Output
definition.description:
Attach an existing Repomix packed output file for AI analysis.
This tool accepts either a directory containing a repomix output file or a direct path to a packed repository file.
Supports multiple formats: XML (structured with <file> tags), Markdown (human-readable with ## headers and code blocks), JSON (machine-readable with files as key-value pairs), and Plain text (simple format with separators).
Calling the tool again with the same file path will refresh the content if the file has been updated.
It will return in that case a new output ID and the updated content.

definition.description:
Generate a Claude Agent Skill from a local code directory. Creates a skill package containing SKILL.md (entry point with metadata) and references/ folder with summary.md, project-structure.md, files.md, and optionally tech-stacks.md.

This tool creates Project Skills in <project>/.claude/skills/<name>/, which are shared with the team via version control.

Output Structure:

  ├── SKILL.md                    # Entry point with usage guide

definition.name: pack_codebase
definition.title: Pack Local Codebase
definition.description: Package a local code directory into a consolidated file for AI analysis. This tool analyzes the codebase structure, extracts relevant code content, and generates a comprehensive report including metrics, file tree, and formatted code content. Supports multiple output formats: XML (structured with <file> tags), Markdown (human-readable with ## headers and code blocks), JSON (machine-readable with files as key-value pairs), and Plain text (simple format with separators). Also supports Tree-sitter compression for efficient token usage.

directory.description: Directory to pack (Absolute path). Any directory readable by this process can be packed.

compress.description: Enable Tree-sitter compression to extract essential code signatures and structure while removing implementation details. Reduces token usage by ~70% while preserving semantic meaning. Generally not needed since grep_repomix_output allows incremental content retrieval. Use only when you specifically need the entire codebase content for large repositories (default: false).

includePatterns.description: Specify files to include using fast-glob patterns. Multiple patterns can be comma-separated (e.g., "**/*.{js,ts}", "src/**,docs/**"). Only matching files will be processed. Useful for focusing on specific parts of the codebase.

Patterns are evaluated in order and the first match wins; directoryStructureOnly takes precedence over compress, and a match with neither flag forces FULL content (use this to exempt specific files from a global compress). Files matching no pattern fall back to the global compress setting. Overrides any output.patterns from the target repository's repomix.config.json. Example: set compress=true and outputPatterns=[{"pattern":"src/core/**"}] to keep src/core at full detail while compressing everything else.

definition.name: create_gtm_tracking_tag
definition.description: [WRITE] PREFERRED way to create a GA4 event tag that fires on an event. Builds a CORRECT GTM resource from plain fields, so you never hand-write GTM JSON. ONE call: enables the built-in variables the tag and trigger reference, reuses or creates the named trigger, and creates the tag linked to it in the draft workspace. Use this instead of tags_create + triggers_create + built_in_variables_enable, which needs three round trips and gets the shapes wrong. eventParameters values may reference built-in variables ({{Click URL}}, {{Click Text}}, {{Page URL}}, {{Form ID}}) and those are enabled automatically. Requires GTM_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES=true and confirm=true.

tagName.description: Name for the tag, e.g. "GA4 Event - Email Click".

platform.description: What KIND of tag to build. "ga4_event" (the default) builds a GA4 event tag from measurementId + eventName. "google_tag" builds the BASE Google tag (googtag) from `tagId`, the one that loads gtag.js and configures GA4 - a container needs exactly one, firing on All Pages. "custom_html" builds a Custom HTML tag from `html`, which is how a dataLayer LISTENER is installed for forms GTM cannot see natively (an AJAX or cross-origin embed). Any OTHER value is REFUSED rather than quietly built as GA4: a Meta or Ads tag asked for here would otherwise come out as a GA4 tag pointing at that platform's id, which looks created and is wrong.

html.description: For platform "custom_html": the complete tag body, a single self-contained <script>.

tagId.description: For platform "google_tag": the id this base tag configures, e.g. "G-ABC123XYZ", or a {{Variable}} holding it. Referencing a Constant is the recommended setup: one variable holds the Measurement ID and every GA4 tag points at it, so changing containers or properties is one edit rather than one per tag.

measurementId.description: The GA4 Measurement ID, e.g. "G-ABC123XYZ", or a {{variable}} reference. Read the real id from the container's Google tag (type "googtag", parameter "tagId") rather than inventing one: an obvious placeholder is refused, because GTM would accept it and the tag would report to nothing.

eventName.description: The GA4 event name, snake_case, e.g. "email_click". Required for platform "ga4_event".

eventParameters.description: Event parameters as plain name/value pairs, e.g. [{"name":"click_text","value":"{{Click Text}}"}]. They are placed in the eventSettingsTable list-of-maps shape GTM requires; do NOT build that structure yourself.

name.description: Trigger name. An existing trigger with this name is REUSED, not duplicated.

kind.description: pageview | link_click | all_clicks | form_submit | custom_event | dom_ready | window_loaded | history_change | scroll_depth | element_visibility | youtube_video | js_error | timer. Use link_click for <a> clicks (outbound links, downloads, mailto:, tel:) and all_clicks for any element.

clickUrlValue.description: Scope a click trigger by {{Click URL}}, e.g. "mailto:" or "tel:".

clickUrlOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default contains.

clickUrlIgnoreCase.description: For a matchRegex {{Click URL}} condition: match case-insensitively.

clickTextValue.description: Scope a click trigger by {{Click Text}}, e.g. an exact CTA label.

clickTextOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default equals.

clickTextIgnoreCase.description: For a matchRegex {{Click Text}} condition: match case-insensitively.

clickElementValue.description: Scope a click trigger by {{Click Element}}, normally a CSS selector.

clickElementOperator.description: cssSelector | equals | contains | matchRegex. Default cssSelector.

clickIdValue.description: Scope a click trigger by {{Click ID}}, the element's id attribute.

clickIdOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default equals.

clickClassesValue.description: Scope a click trigger by {{Click Classes}}.

pagePathValue.description: Scope to a page by {{Page Path}}.

pageUrlValue.description: Scope by {{Page URL}}, e.g. a "?thanks=1" success page.

pageUrlOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default contains.

eventName.description: For kind "custom_event": the dataLayer event name, e.g. "generate_lead".

formIdValue.description: For kind "form_submit": scope to one form by {{Form ID}}.

formIdOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default equals.

intervalMs.description: For kind "timer": firing interval in milliseconds. REQUIRED for timer.

limit.description: For kind "timer": how many times it may fire.

visibilitySelector.description: For kind "element_visibility": CSS selector of the element to watch, e.g. "#gform_confirmation_message". REQUIRED unless visibilityElementId is given.

visibilityElementId.description: For kind "element_visibility": the element's id attribute, as an alternative to visibilitySelector.

visibilityFiringFrequency.description: For kind "element_visibility": ONCE | ONCE_PER_ELEMENT | MANY_PER_ELEMENT. Default ONCE.

visibilityObserveDomChanges.description: For kind "element_visibility": keep watching for elements added AFTER page load (an AJAX confirmation message). Default true.

visibilityMinOnScreenMs.description: For kind "element_visibility": require the element to stay on screen for N milliseconds first.

scrollPixels.description: For kind "scroll_depth": vertical PIXEL thresholds instead of percentages.

scrollHorizontalPercentages.description: For kind "scroll_depth": horizontal percent thresholds. Off unless supplied.

pageHostnameValue.description: Scope by {{Page Hostname}}. ANDed into the filter of any filter-capable kind.

pageHostnameOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default equals.

referrerValue.description: Scope by {{Referrer}}. ANDed into the filter of any filter-capable kind.

referrerOperator.description: equals | contains | startsWith | endsWith | matchRegex. Default contains.

trigger.description: The trigger this tag fires on. Reused by name when it already exists, otherwise created.

builtInVariables.description: Extra built-in variable types to enable beyond the ones inferred, e.g. ["formElement"].

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm this write operation.

name.description: Trigger name.

type.description: Condition type: contains, cssSelector, endsWith, equals, greater, greaterOrEquals, less, lessOrEquals, matchRegex, startsWith, urlMatches.

key.description: MUST be "arg0" or "arg1" — GTM accepts no other key here, and anything else fails with "Parameter key is unknown". arg0 is the LEFT side (the variable being tested), arg1 is the RIGHT side (the value compared against).

value.description: For arg0, a variable reference in double braces, e.g. "{{Click URL}}", "{{_event}}", "{{Page Path}}". For arg1, the literal to compare, e.g. "mailto:". A built-in variable referenced in arg0 must be ENABLED in the workspace first — see built_in_variables_enable (Click URL is "clickUrl", Click Text "clickText", Form ID "formId", and so on).

parameter.description: EXACTLY TWO entries, keyed arg0 then arg1. Example, a link click on a mailto: address: [{"type":"template","key":"arg0","value":"{{Click URL}}"},{"type":"template","key":"arg1","value":"mailto:"}] with condition type "contains".

filter.description: Conditions that must be met for the trigger to fire ("fires on SOME …").

eventName.description: TIMER triggers ONLY: the name of the GTM event the timer fires, as a single Parameter {type:"template", value:"gtm.timer"} (no key). Defaults to gtm.timer when omitted. Do NOT send this for a customEvent trigger: GTM rejects it. A customEvent trigger carries its name in `customEventFilter` as EXACTLY ONE condition, {{_event}} equals <name>, e.g. [{"type":"equals","parameter":[{"type":"template","key":"arg0","value":"{{_event}}"},{"type":"template","key":"arg1","value":"purchase"}]}]. intervalSeconds.description: Timer trigger: firing interval in SECONDS as a single Parameter (no key). Top-level GTM field. Use interval (ms) OR intervalSeconds, not both.

limit.description: Timer trigger: max number of times the timer fires, as a single Parameter {type:"template", value:"3"} (no key). Dedicated TOP-LEVEL GTM field — do NOT put it in `parameter`.

prompts.name: setup_server_side_container
prompts.title: Set up a server-side GTM container
prompts.description: One guided flow to create a server-side (sGTM) container: the SERVER container + GA4 client + built-ins + Event-Data/Constant/Request-Header variables + per-event triggers + GA4 (and optional Google Ads) server tags, in the correct order with the exact resource shapes. Optional args: accountId, containerName, measurementId, adsConversionId.

arguments.name: accountId
arguments.description: GTM account ID to create the server container in (ask the user if omitted).

arguments.name: containerName
arguments.description: Name for the new SERVER container, e.g. "example.com - Server".

arguments.name: measurementId
arguments.description: GA4 Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXX) the server relays to. Omit to derive it from the web container or ask.

arguments.name: adsConversionId
arguments.description: Google Ads conversion ID (AW-XXXXXXXX) — only if you also want a server Ads conversion tag.

prompts.name: setup_ecommerce_funnel
prompts.title: Install the GA4 ecommerce funnel (web)
prompts.description: One guided flow to install the full GA4 ecommerce funnel in a WEB container: per-event Custom Event triggers + GA4 event tags with native ecommerce forwarding (sendEcommerceData), the dlv - ecommerce.* variables, and a Consent Mode v2 defaults tag on Consent Initialization — then a verification checklist. Optional args: accountId, containerId, measurementId, events (comma-separated).

arguments.name: accountId
arguments.description: GTM account ID (ask the user if omitted).

arguments.name: containerId
arguments.description: The WEB container ID to install the funnel in.

arguments.name: measurementId
arguments.description: GA4 Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXX). Omit to derive it from the container's Google tag or ask.

arguments.name: events
arguments.description: Comma-separated funnel events. Omit for the standard funnel: view_item, add_to_cart, view_cart, begin_checkout, add_shipping_info, add_payment_info, purchase.

prompts.name: audit
prompts.title: Audit a GTM container
prompts.description: Run a read-only GTM container audit and summarise the findings by severity (error/warning/info) + category (missing_trigger, paused_tag, broken_reference, ga4_config, duplicate_name, broad_trigger, unused_trigger, missing_builtin_variable, empty_folder). Optional args: account, container (a GTM-XXXXXXX id or name).

arguments.name: account
arguments.description: GTM account id (optional — the assistant will list accounts if omitted).

arguments.name: container
arguments.description: Container to audit: a public GTM-XXXXXXX id or its name (optional).

prompts.name: report
prompts.title: Run a GA4 report
prompts.description: Run a read-only GA4 report (sessions / users / conversions by channel, default last 28 days) and summarise it. Optional args: property (properties/NNNNNNN), dateRange, metrics (comma-separated).

arguments.description: GA4 property id (properties/NNNNNNN) — optional; the assistant will list properties if omitted.

arguments.description: Date range, e.g. "last 28 days", "2026-01-01..2026-01-31" (optional).

arguments.name: metrics
arguments.description: Comma-separated GA4 metrics, e.g. "sessions,totalUsers,conversions" (optional).

prompts.name: create-tag
prompts.title: Create a GA4 event tag
prompts.description: Guide the end-to-end creation of a GA4 event tag (event name → trigger → variables → tag), DRAFT-ONLY and gated behind GTM_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES + confirm=true. Optional args: description (what to track), account, container.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: What to track, e.g. "contact form submit", "add to cart button", "phone number click" (optional).

arguments.name: account
arguments.description: GTM account id (optional).

arguments.name: container
arguments.description: Container to create the tag in (optional).

prompts.name: debug
prompts.title: Debug a tag that is not firing
prompts.description: A read-only diagnostic flow to find why a tag is not firing: audit → tag config (paused? trigger?) → trigger conditions → referenced variables → Consent Mode, then the single most likely cause + fix. Optional args: tag, symptom, account, container.

arguments.description: The tag (or trigger) that is misbehaving (optional).

arguments.name: symptom
arguments.description: What is wrong, e.g. "never fires", "fires twice", "no GA4 hit" (optional).

arguments.name: account
arguments.description: GTM account id (optional).

arguments.name: container
arguments.description: Container to debug (optional).

definition.name: auditAccessibility
definition.description: Audit a Semiotic chart configuration against the Chartability (POUR-CAF) accessibility framework — Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust, Compromising, Assistive, Flexible. Statically grades the config (no DOM/AT): credits the built-ins every HOC ships (keyboard nav, focus ring, skip link, screen-reader data table, reduced-motion + forced-colors, shareable state), flags author-actionable gaps (missing title/description/summary, low contrast, small text, color-only encoding, undescribed trends, data density), and routes everything that needs real assistive-technology testing to a 'manual' item. Returns a per-principle report with the 14 critical heuristics marked. Pass inChartContainer=true to credit data-download/share affordances. Pair with manual NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver testing — Chartability is not a pass/fail certification.

definition.name: renderChart
definition.description: Render a Semiotic chart to static SVG or PNG. This is a static snapshot path: props must include data immediately, and ref/push-mode charts cannot be rendered through this tool. Returns SVG text by default or an image/png artifact when format='png', plus a "Render evidence" JSON block (mark counts by type, resolved axis domains, empty flag, annotation count, accessible name) — read the evidence instead of parsing the SVG to verify the chart actually rendered data marks. now.description: Explicit reference clock for review, freshness, and expiry checks. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp.

applySafeIdentityRepairs.description: Fill missing identity fields only; existing mismatches require an explicit revision and claim reassessment. Defaults to false.

expiresAt.description: Explicit reference clock for review, freshness, and expiry checks. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp.

reviewAt.description: Explicit reference clock for review, freshness, and expiry checks. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp.

items.description: Accountable policy exception. It applies only when a supplied expiry or review bound remains in the future at the explicit reference clock.

expiresAt.description: Explicit reference clock for review, freshness, and expiry checks. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp.

reviewAt.description: Explicit reference clock for review, freshness, and expiry checks. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp.

items.description: Accountable policy exception. It applies only when a supplied expiry or review bound remains in the future at the explicit reference clock.

contract.description: Complete explicit artifact contract. Validate against semiotic://artifact-contract-schema; omitted source, review, and time facts stay omitted or explicitly unknown.

definition.name: repairChartConfig
definition.title: Repair an unsuitable chart choice
definition.description: Validate that a chart component is a sensible choice for a dataset, and if not, propose ranked alternatives that fit. Returns a structured status of ok, alternative, or unknown.

component.description: Chart component name to validate, e.g. 'PieChart'

data.description: Row data — array of objects.

intent.description: User intent — informs ranking of alternatives when the chart doesn't fit.

identifiers.description: Fields that identify records and must not be used as visual encodings or measures.

fieldRoles.description: Per-field semantic or exact encoding-role hints used before chart ranking.

definition.name: reportIssue
definition.description: Generate a GitHub issue URL for Semiotic bug reports or feature requests. Returns a URL the user can open to submit. For rendering bugs, include the component name, props summary, and any diagnoseConfig output in the body.

title.description: Issue title, e.g. 'Bug: BarChart tooltip shows undefined'

body.description: Issue body with details, reproduction steps, diagnoseConfig output

labels.description: GitHub labels, e.g. ['bug'] or 'bug'

definition.name: suggestChart
definition.description: Lightweight heuristic chart recommender for a small data sample (1-5 rows) with capability filtering (push API, linked hover, SSR, selection, legend). Returns ranked recommendations with example props. For richer capability-descriptor ranking (scores, reasons, caveats) and the full 13-intent taxonomy, prefer `suggestCharts` (plural).

data.description: 1-5 sample data objects

intent.description: Visualization intent. Accepts this engine's intents (comparison, trend, distribution, relationship, composition, geographic, network, hierarchy) AND the richer suggestCharts taxonomy (compare-categories, part-to-whole, correlation, flow, geo, rank, …), which is translated automatically; an unrecognized intent is ignored rather than rejected.

capabilities.description: Capability constraints — set a key to true to require, false to forbid. Unset keys are ignored.

push.description: Require ref-based push API (live streaming via ref.current.push())

definition.name: suggestCharts
definition.title: Recommend Semiotic charts
definition.description: Recommend Semiotic charts for a dataset using heuristic capability descriptors. Returns ranked, structured suggestions with scores, reasons, caveats, and ready-to-use props; no LLM call is made.

data.description: Row data — array of objects.

intent.description: Ranking intent. One of: trend, compare-series, compare-categories, rank, part-to-whole, distribution, correlation, flow, hierarchy, geo, outlier-detection, composition-over-time, change-detection. Custom intents accepted.

maxResults.description: Cap on suggestions returned (default 8).

identifiers.description: Fields that identify records and must not be used as visual encodings or measures.

fieldRoles.description: Per-field semantic or exact encoding-role hints used before chart ranking.

audience.description: Audience profile — familiarity, adoption targets, exposure level, and reception modality.

receptionModality.description: Reception channel. A non-visual value down-ranks charts the audience can't receive in that channel and adds receivability caveats.

definition.name: suggestDashboard
definition.description: Generate a dashboard of complementary chart panels for a dataset — each panel answers a distinct analytical intent (trend, rank, distribution, correlation, etc.) and the engine diversifies by chart family by default. Heuristic only; no LLM call. Use when the user asks 'show me this data' or 'build me a dashboard' rather than picking one chart.

data.description: Row data — array of objects.

intents.description: Intents to cover. Omit to let the engine pick based on the data shape.

diversifyByFamily.description: Prefer not to repeat chart families across panels (default true).

identifiers.description: Fields that identify records and must not be used as visual encodings or measures.

fieldRoles.description: Per-field semantic or exact encoding-role hints used before chart ranking.

audience.description: Audience profile — familiarity, adoption targets, exposure level, and reception modality.

definition.name: suggestStreamCharts
definition.description: Recommend streaming Semiotic charts for a schema (not row data). Pass fields plus optional throughput (band or rows/sec), retention, shape ('append'|'keyed'|'aggregate'), and keyFields. Ranks realtime XY charts plus push-capable ordinal/value charts (BarChart, PieChart, BigNumber, GaugeChart, …). Returns suggestions, excluded fits-reasons, and optional stretch picks when audience is set.

schema.description: Stream schema — fields plus throughput/retention/shape hints. No row data.

definition.name: suggestStreamDashboard
definition.description: Compose a multi-panel dashboard from one or more stream schemas. Honors AudienceProfile.dashboard layout policy (cellBudget, leadFamilies, windowPreference).

definition.name: suggestStretchCharts
definition.description: Recommend literacy-growth chart picks for a dataset given an AudienceProfile. Returns charts the data supports but the audience is unfamiliar with (familiarity ≤ 3, or ≤ 4 at exposureLevel 2), each paired with the familiar chart it could substitute for and a rationale. Use when the consumer wants to gently expose users to less familiar but more analytically appropriate visualizations.

data.description: Row data.

audience.description: Audience profile — familiarity, targets, exposure level, reception modality.

identifiers.description: Fields that identify records and must not be used as visual encodings or measures.

fieldRoles.description: Per-field semantic or exact encoding-role hints used before chart ranking.

definition.name: suggestTokenEncoding
definition.description: Recommend a semantic token / ISOTYPE encoding for a reader task. Use before drawing repeated dots, icons, glyphs, natural-frequency grids, quantile dotplots, or hybrid bar-token views. Returns the recommended tokenEncoding, warnings, alternatives, and matching suggestCharts capability intents. Accepts canonical token intents (precise-comparison, probability-estimation, risk-communication, memory, support-decision, etc.) and friendly aliases (measure, estimate probability, understand risk, remember, decide).

taskIntent.description: Reader task intent, e.g. 'estimate probability', 'understand risk', 'remember', 'measure', 'decide', or canonical token intents like 'probability-estimation'.

dataType.description: Data shape or meaning behind the tokenized view.

precisionNeed.description: How much exact magnitude reading matters.

concreteEntity.description: Concrete icon/glyph concept, e.g. person, bus, server. Becomes tokenEncoding.icon when useful.
